findings.title: Seller onboarding never shows a paywall: the plan step only stores a choice, then opens the dashboard
findings.problem: The seller PLAN step (SellerPlanRecommendationStep) only calls setSelectedPlanId and goNext(). Its own copy says 'No charge is made on this step'. finishSeller() then writes onboarding_complete=true and router.replace('/(tabs)/'). Nothing in the codebase opens /plans?fromOnboarding=true (grep 'fromOnboarding' finds only plans.tsx:103), so the 5-day card-required trial is never started. app/_layout.tsx:958-961 still has a comment saying onboarding_complete is 'only written by plans.tsx after plan selection', so this looks like a regression.
findings.why_costs_money: Every new seller lands in a working store without ever seeing a purchase sheet. Subscription conversion only happens if a seller later goes looking for Settings > Subscription on their own.
findings.fix: In finishSeller, router.replace('/plans?fromOnboarding=true') instead of '/(tabs)/', and only write ONBOARDING_KEY in plans.tsx after a purchase or an explicit 'Not now'. Pass onboarding_selected_plan as the preselected plan (already read at plans.tsx:149-161).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks nearly all subscription revenue: with a card-required trial typically converting 30-60% of the sellers who see it, against ~0% for sellers who never see it, this is most of the subscription share of the $50k/mo target

findings.title: No server route requires a paid plan to sell: an unpaid seller gets everything Starter promises
findings.problem: resolveEffectiveEntitlement returns planId 'starter' for a seller with no subscription (provider 'none'). requirePlan is only ever called with 'growth' or 'pro' (grep finds index.ts:239-244,385, analytics.ts:624,676, live.ts:48, live-commerce.ts:29, manufacturers.ts:77, analytics-insights.ts:546, iap-promotions.ts:98). Storefront, products (up to 25), checkout, orders and payouts are not gated at all. handleSubscriptionDeleted even calls Starter 'the free Starter plan' (webhooks.ts:1659-1669).
findings.why_costs_money: The $29 Starter tier is in effect a free tier, so any seller who skips or cancels the paywall keeps selling and only pays the commission. That removes the reason to buy the entry plan.
findings.fix: Choose the free-tier policy explicitly. Either require an active or trialing entitlement (provider != 'none') to publish a store or receive orders (add requirePlan('starter') with a provider check to store publish, products create, and the checkout-intent seller eligibility check), or rename the unpaid state to 'Free' with tighter limits (for example 5 products) and price Starter on what it adds.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks Starter revenue: e.g. 300 sellers x $29 = ~$8.7k/mo that unpaid sellers currently get for free

findings.title: Native RevenueCat identity flow calls logOut() on an anonymous user, which throws, so offerings never load
findings.problem: After Purchases.configure() with no appUserID the SDK customer is anonymous. The identity effect always runs `await Purchases.logOut()` before logIn(clerkId). Per RevenueCat SDK docs, logOut on an anonymous user throws LOGOUT_CALLED_WITH_ANONYMOUS_USER. The identity queue re-throws the error, the catch at line 128 swallows it, and getOfferings and setPackages never run. With packages=[] the paywall shows 'Subscriptions are temporarily unavailable' (plans.tsx:252-253) and the CTA is disabled after 6s (pricesFailed, plans.tsx:136). No test covers anonymous logOut.
findings.why_costs_money: On a fresh install the iOS and Android paywall may never be able to sell a subscription. Every native purchase depends on this code path.
findings.fix: Call `if (!(await Purchases.isAnonymous())) await Purchases.logOut()`, or wrap logOut in try/catch, then logIn. Better still, pass appUserID: clerkId to configure() once signed in. Verify with a sandbox purchase on a clean install before submitting.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks all native subscription revenue if confirmed on device (iOS is expected to be the main channel)

findings.title: 5-day free trial is not a duration App Store Connect offers; paywall and onboarding copy hard-code '5-day'
findings.problem: Apple introductory free-trial durations are 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month and longer. 5 days cannot be configured. The native CTA still says 'Start my 5-day free trial' with 'Free for 5 days, then X/month' and a Day 4 / Day 5 timeline whenever the store returns any introPrice. The real period is never read from introPrice.periodNumberOfUnits/periodUnit. The day-4 reminder logic (isDayFourOfFive) also assumes exactly 5 days.
findings.why_costs_money: A paywall that states a trial length different from the one StoreKit actually charges is a 3.1.2 / 2.3.1 rejection risk on first review, and a source of refund requests and chargebacks after launch.
findings.fix: Choose a 1-week (or 3-day) iOS intro offer. Render the trial length from pkg.product.introPrice (periodNumberOfUnits + periodUnit), and drive the timeline and reminder day from that value instead of constants. Keep Stripe/web trial_period_days in sync, or make it configurable.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks launch if rejected; misstated trials also add refund losses of a few % of subscription revenue

findings.title: Boost buys a digital feature through Stripe inside the iOS app by default (IAP rail flagged off)
findings.problem: nativePromotionsEnabled() is true only when EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS=1 is baked into the build. eas.json sets no such env and docs/app-store/release-flow.md:83-91 does not list it. With the flag unset, iOS opens Stripe Checkout through WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync and shows 'Secure payment via Stripe'. The server side also needs IAP_PROMOTIONS_ENABLED=true (lib/iapPromotions.ts:59). docs/review-readiness/iap-rails.md marks this 'FIXED (flagged OFF)', but the shipped default is non-compliant.
findings.why_costs_money: Paid post reach is a digital service consumed in the app. Guideline 3.1.1 requires IAP, so a reviewer who reaches Boost rejects the build. In the US storefront only a link out is allowed, not an in-app Stripe sheet.
findings.fix: Create the 7 brandthread_boost_* consumables in App Store Connect, Play and RevenueCat. Set EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS=1 in the EAS production environment and IAP_PROMOTIONS_ENABLED=true on the API, and add both to release-flow.md. Alternatively hide Boost on native until that is done.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks launch (rejection) if a reviewer opens Boost; boost revenue itself is small at launch (<$1k/mo)

findings.title: Create-ad (Brandthread Ads) also uses Stripe on native by default
findings.problem: This uses the same EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS gate as Boost. Off by default, the native app creates a Stripe Checkout Session for an in-app ad placement and opens it in an auth session. ad-campaigns /:id/pay has no plan gate, so every seller sees this path.
findings.why_costs_money: An in-app ad placement is a digital service, so this is a 3.1.1 rejection. It is more likely to be found than Boost because no Pro plan is needed to reach it.
findings.fix: Ship with the brandthread_ad_* consumables live and the flag on, or hide 'Create ad' on iOS until they are.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks launch if found in review

findings.title: Native 'Manage subscription' opens the Stripe billing portal for web-billed sellers
findings.problem: For effectiveProvider==='stripe', handleOpenPortal opens a Stripe Billing Portal session with Linking.openURL from inside the iOS app. Depending on the portal configuration, sellers can switch plans or pay there. The legal footer on the same screen tells them to 'Manage or cancel in your App Store account settings', which is wrong for them.
findings.why_costs_money: Outside the US storefront, an in-app link to an external purchase/upgrade surface breaks 3.1.1/3.1.3 anti-steering rules. Inside the US it is allowed after the May 2025 Epic ruling.
findings.fix: On iOS, for Stripe-billed sellers, show 'Manage your plan at brandthread.app' as plain text outside the US storefront, and keep the button only for US. Disable plan switching in the Stripe portal configuration. Show the footer copy that matches the provider.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Review risk, not $; affects only web-subscribed sellers using iOS

findings.title: A web (Stripe) subscriber who upgrades in the iOS app gets billed twice
findings.problem: On native, handleChangePlan and handleSelect always buy a RevenueCat package, even when effectiveProvider is 'stripe'. Nothing cancels the Stripe subscription. resolveEffectiveEntitlement simply prefers the higher of the two. The reverse also happens: an IAP subscriber using the web checkout gets a new Stripe subscription, because users.subscriptionId is null (subscription.ts:390-421).
findings.why_costs_money: Both rails keep billing the same seller. That leads to chargebacks (about $15 per Stripe dispute), Apple refunds and churn.
findings.fix: If the provider is the other rail, block the purchase with 'You're billed on the web; change plans at brandthread.app' (and the reverse on web), or cancel the Stripe subscription at period end once the native entitlement is confirmed.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-500/mo in disputes and refunds once both rails have users

findings.title: Android upgrades and downgrades create a second Play subscription
findings.problem: purchase() calls Purchases.purchasePackage(pkg) without googleProductChangeInfo. On Google Play, RevenueCat then starts a new concurrent subscription instead of replacing the old base plan, so a Starter seller who 'switches to Growth' pays $29 + $79.
findings.why_costs_money: Double billing leads to refunds, Play policy complaints and 1-star reviews.
findings.fix: When customerInfo.activeSubscriptions holds a brandthread_*_monthly product, pass googleProductChangeInfo { oldProductIdentifier, prorationMode } (or the purchaseParams equivalent in SDK v9).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-400/mo in refunds and churn on Android

findings.title: Stripe API version 2026-07-29.dahlia removed invoice.subscription, so payment-failed dunning never fires
findings.problem: handleInvoicePaymentFailed reads invoice.subscription. Since the 2025-03-31 'basil' API, that field moved to invoice.parent.subscription_details.subscription. On a new Stripe account (the new LLC) the webhook endpoint defaults to the latest API version, so the field is undefined and the handler logs 'not subscription-backed' and returns. The 'Payment failed, update your card' notification and push never go out. webhooks.trial.test.ts mocks the old shape, so tests still pass.
findings.why_costs_money: Failed renewals get no recovery prompt. Recovered involuntary churn is usually 20-40% of failed payments, and all of it is lost.
findings.fix: Read `invoice.parent?.subscription_details?.subscription ?? invoice.subscription`. Add a fixture with the current payload shape, and pin the webhook endpoint's api_version explicitly.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-1,000/mo of recoverable failed renewals at the target scale

findings.title: past_due keeps full paid access with no time limit
findings.problem: stripeActive counts 'past_due' as active with no grace window. If the Stripe dashboard is set to leave subscriptions past_due after retries fail, the seller keeps Growth/Pro (including unlimited Pro AI and the 3% fee) indefinitely without paying. No past_due_since is stored.
findings.why_costs_money: Non-paying sellers keep paid features and AI spend for free.
findings.fix: Store past_due_since in handleSubscriptionUpdated, and treat past_due as active only for 7 days. In Stripe Billing settings, set 'cancel subscription' after the final retry.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-800/mo of unpaid Growth/Pro access plus AI cost

findings.title: A failed payment only ends access by dropping the seller to free Starter, which still sells
findings.problem: When Stripe cancels after dunning, handleSubscriptionDeleted sets the plan to 'starter' and the status to 'canceled'. Because Starter is ungated (see the 'no server route requires a paid plan' finding), a seller whose card fails at trial end keeps a live store, products and checkout.
findings.why_costs_money: There is no consequence for an expired or failed card at trial end, so trials don't convert under pressure.
findings.fix: After cancellation or expiry, move the store into a locked state: store hidden, no new orders, products kept, banner 'Reactivate your plan'. Use that lock for both rails.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Large part of trial-to-paid conversion; ~$2-5k/mo

findings.title: Stripe gives a fresh 5-day trial on every checkout (no one-trial-per-seller rule)
findings.problem: subscription_data.trial_period_days: 5 is always set. A seller who cancels and re-subscribes, or opens new accounts with the same card, gets unlimited trials. users.subscriptionTrialStartedAt exists but is not checked, and the card fingerprint is not deduplicated.
findings.why_costs_money: Pro trials include unlimited AI credits (aiCredits/catalogue.ts:31) and the 3% commission rate. Repeat trials burn AI spend and delay paying forever.
findings.fix: Omit trial_period_days when subscriptionTrialStartedAt is set or when an earlier customer with the same card fingerprint exists. Use Stripe Radar or setup-intent fingerprint checks.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-1,000/mo in AI cost and lost conversions from trial cycling

findings.title: Account deletion leaves the Stripe subscription billing and orphans it
findings.problem: Purge nulls stripeCustomerId and subscriptionId but never calls stripe.subscriptions.cancel. Stripe keeps charging a deleted seller, and later webhooks can't map to a user. Native subscribers are not told that deleting the account does not cancel their Apple or Google subscription, which Apple's account-deletion guidance requires.
findings.why_costs_money: This guarantees disputes ($15 each, plus dispute-rate risk on the new Stripe account) and Apple review risk under 5.1.1(v).
findings.fix: At deletion request, cancel the Stripe subscription (at period end or immediately). On delete-account, show 'Cancel your App Store/Google Play subscription' with a managementURL link when the provider is revenuecat.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-500/mo in disputes plus Stripe account health

findings.title: No cancel flow, cancel reason, or win-back anywhere
findings.problem: Cancel is the external Stripe portal or Apple managementURL with no retention step. handleSubscriptionUpdated doesn't store cancel_at_period_end or cancellation_details. There is no win-back email or job (grep 'win-back', 'cancel_at_period_end' finds nothing). The one-time offer is hard-disabled (ONE_TIME_OFFER_ENABLED=false, no promo product).
findings.why_costs_money: A good cancel flow saves 10-20% of cancellations, and win-back offers recover 5-10% of churned sellers.
findings.fix: Add an in-app 'Cancel plan' screen that asks for a reason, offers a pause or downgrade, then deep-links out. Persist cancel_at_period_end and send a win-back email 7 and 30 days after expiry. Configure Stripe promotion codes or Apple win-back offers.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo of retained subscription revenue at target

findings.title: Apple keeps 15-30% of every native subscription with no price difference or US web-link strategy
findings.problem: Native prices mirror web ($29/$79/$199). Apple takes 15% under the Small Business Program (below $1M proceeds, which Dev must enrol in) or 30% in year one and 15% after a year of continuous subscription, versus about 3% on Stripe. Since the May 2025 Epic ruling, US-storefront apps may show a button or link to web checkout with no Apple commission, but the app doesn't offer this.
findings.why_costs_money: At $25k/mo of subscriptions all on iOS: about $3.75k/mo to Apple at 15%, or $7.5k at 30% if not enrolled, against about $0.9k on Stripe.
findings.fix: Enrol in the App Store Small Business Program before launch. On the US storefront (check Purchases.getStorefront()), add a 'Subscribe on the web' link alongside IAP. Consider native prices about 15% higher. Keep IAP as the default everywhere else.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $2.8-6.6k/mo margin swing at $25k/mo of native subscriptions

findings.title: Missing RevenueCat keys or project id fail silently ('temporarily unavailable'), and boot only warns
findings.problem: If EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_IOS_API_KEY is absent from the EAS production environment, available=false and every paywall says 'Subscriptions are temporarily unavailable' (no crash, no alert). On the API, REVENUECAT_PROJECT_ID and REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION are OPTIONAL_VARS (warning only), so production can boot unable to verify any native purchase (sync returns 503). Keys live in .replit (lines 31-37), not in eas.json, and their presence in the EAS 'production' environment can't be verified from the repo.
findings.why_costs_money: A forgotten env var silently zeroes native subscription revenue.
findings.fix: Make both server vars required in production. Add a release-build assertion (EAS build hook or a CI check of `eas env:list production`) for the RevenueCat iOS/Android keys and EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS, and send a Sentry error when available=false in a release build.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks all native subscription revenue if misconfigured

findings.title: current_period_end moved to subscription items, so renewal dates are blank
findings.problem: On the dahlia API version, subscription.current_period_end no longer exists (it is now items.data[].current_period_end). /status returns renewsOn null and the webhook never stores subscriptionPeriodEnd. Subscription and billing show 'Renews —'.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers can't see when they'll be charged. That brings support tickets and 'surprise charge' disputes.
findings.fix: Use sub.items.data[0].current_period_end with a fallback to sub.current_period_end.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100/mo in disputes and support

findings.title: Sandbox (TestFlight) purchases grant real paid access in production
findings.problem: isSandbox is stored but never checked in resolveEffectiveEntitlement. The seeded RevenueCat webhook has environment:null, so sandbox events go to production. Any TestFlight tester, or anyone with a sandbox Apple ID on a TestFlight build pointed at prod, gets Growth/Pro for free.
findings.why_costs_money: Paid features and AI spend are given away. TestFlight testers are a self-selected group of sellers.
findings.fix: In production (APP_ENV=production), ignore native rows with isSandbox=true unless the user is on an allowlist. Set the RevenueCat production webhook to environment 'production'.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-500/mo depending on TestFlight audience

findings.title: Native subscription verification depends on Replit's connector proxy
findings.problem: Every native entitlement read (sync, webhook, promo verify) goes through new ReplitConnectors().proxy('revenuecat', ...). It only works on Replit hosting with the RevenueCat connector authorised. Off Replit, or if the connector token lapses, reconcile throws: /native/sync returns 503, the webhook returns 500, and paying iOS sellers stay on 'starter'.
findings.why_costs_money: Paying native sellers lose access, and the failure shows as a 503 rather than an obvious misconfiguration.
findings.fix: Use a direct RevenueCat v2 secret key (REVENUECAT_SECRET_API_KEY) with fetch, and keep the connector as a fallback. Add a startup health check that GETs /v2/projects/{id}.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: All native subscription revenue is at risk during an outage

findings.title: RevenueCat TRANSFER events are rejected with 400, so the old account keeps access
findings.problem: The handler requires event.app_user_id. RevenueCat TRANSFER events (fired when 'Restore purchases' moves a subscription to another Clerk account) carry transferred_from/transferred_to instead, so they 400 and are never reconciled. The original account's seller_subscription_entitlements row stays active until expiresAt.
findings.why_costs_money: One Apple ID can unlock paid plans on several seller accounts in turn (restore, switch, restore), and the old accounts keep access until expiry.
findings.fix: For type TRANSFER, reconcile every id in transferred_from and transferred_to, and accept events without app_user_id.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-300/mo of plan sharing

findings.title: Apple-charged boost/ad purchases are acknowledged but not delivered when the API flag is off or the target doesn't match
findings.problem: If the mobile flag is on but IAP_PROMOTIONS_ENABLED is off, the webhook records the event id and returns 200 'ignored', so RevenueCat never retries. Results of unmatched, amount_mismatch, ineligible (for example a moderated post) or conflict also return 200 with nothing granted and no queue for later redemption or refund.
findings.why_costs_money: The seller is charged by Apple for nothing, which brings Apple refund requests (counted against the app), support load and 1-star reviews.
findings.fix: Store unmatched purchases as a credit balance the seller can apply to the next boost or ad. Return 503 (so RevenueCat retries) when the flag is off. Alert on any non-granted result.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$50-200/mo once promotions sell natively

findings.title: Native trial users see 'Free' and 'Upgrade to unlock' because the status vocabularies don't match
findings.problem: For RevenueCat, /status returns status 'trial' or 'grace' (nativeEntitlements statuses), with renewsOn and trialEnd always null. subscription.tsx only knows 'active', 'trialing', 'past_due' and 'canceled', so a native trialing seller gets statusLabel 'Free' and the line 'Upgrade to unlock more features'.
findings.why_costs_money: Confused trial sellers buy again, cancel, or ask for refunds. A trial that looks inactive gets cancelled.
findings.fix: Map 'trial' to Trial and 'grace' to Payment issue. Return trialEnd and renewsOn from native.trialEndsAt and expiresAt in /status.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~1-3% trial conversion loss on native

findings.title: No payment-failed banner for App Store or Play billing issues
findings.problem: isSubscriptionPaymentRecoveryRequired only checks 'past_due' and 'unpaid' (Stripe values). Native billing retry maps to 'grace' or 'expired', so the recovery alert never shows. The RevenueCat BILLING_ISSUE webhook only reconciles: no push, no notification row.
findings.why_costs_money: Store-side involuntary churn is never surfaced inside Brandthread, so recoverable renewals are lost.
findings.fix: On BILLING_ISSUE, insert a 'subscription_payment_failed' notification and push with a deep link to managementURL. Treat 'grace' as recovery-required in the UI.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-600/mo recovered native renewals

findings.title: Day-4 trial reminder exists only for Stripe trials, while the native paywall promises it
findings.problem: createEligibleEvents selects users.subscriptionStatus='trialing', which only Stripe webhooks set. Native trials live in seller_subscription_entitlements, so they never get the 'We remind you before your trial ends' step shown on the paywall timeline. Apple sends no trial-ending notice for subscriptions.
findings.why_costs_money: Breaking a disclosed promise brings 'charged without warning' refunds and disputes, and the missed reminder is also a missed chance to convert the seller.
findings.fix: Include native rows with status 'trial' using their trialEndsAt (the day before end, given Apple durations), or drop the reminder step from the native timeline.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-300/mo in refunds

findings.title: 'Start my free trial' is shown even to users who aren't eligible for the intro offer
findings.problem: hasRealTrialOffer is true whenever any package has product.introPrice. StoreKit returns introPrice to everyone, including users who already used a trial in the subscription group, and they are charged immediately. Eligibility is never checked (Purchases.checkTrialOrIntroductoryPriceEligibility).
findings.why_costs_money: A re-subscriber who reads 'Free for 5 days' is charged on day 0. That brings refunds, 3.1.2 complaints and chargebacks.
findings.fix: Call checkTrialOrIntroductoryPriceEligibility for the three product ids, and show the trial copy only when eligible.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100/mo in refunds; review risk

findings.title: Price is less prominent than the trial in the paywall CTA (Apple 3.1.2(c))
findings.problem: The main button says 'Start my 5-day free trial'. The billed amount appears only in the smaller billingLine subtext and on plan cards. The headline subtitle says 'start free' even though Starter is paid. Apple has rejected paywalls where the free-trial text is more prominent than the renewal price.
findings.why_costs_money: First-review rejection delays the Oct 31 launch.
findings.fix: Put '{price}/month after {N}-day free trial' at the same or larger size as the CTA label, directly above it, and remove 'start free' from the subtitle.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Launch-delay risk

findings.title: Stripe success and portal return URLs point at /api-server/seller/... (missing /api) and sit behind requireAuth
findings.problem: The API is mounted at /api (app.ts:210) and webhooks live at /api-server/api/webhooks (ensureWebhookEvents.ts:48), but success_url and cancel_url are `${origin}/api-server/seller/subscription/return` without /api. Even with the right path, router.use(requireAuth) on line 33 runs before the '/return' 'skip' hack (which only sets a flag), so the browser redirect without a bearer token gets 401.
findings.why_costs_money: Web sellers finish Stripe checkout and land on an error page, then abandon or retry and create duplicates.
findings.fix: Mount the /return and /portal/return pages on a separate unauthenticated router before subscriptionRouter, use the /api-server/api/... path, or return straight to the web app's /plans?checkout=success.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Web checkout drop-off; ~$200-500/mo

findings.title: Reflected HTML injection on the subscription return page
findings.problem: req.query.plan is interpolated unescaped into the HTML body (`${plan}`) on a page served from the Brandthread domain.
findings.why_costs_money: Attackers can build phishing pages on brandthread.app (for example a fake 'enter card' prompt), which erodes trust and invites Stripe and Apple scrutiny.
findings.fix: Map plan through isSellerPlanId to a display name, or escapeHtml it.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Fraud and brand risk, not direct $

findings.title: A past_due seller who re-runs checkout gets a duplicate Stripe subscription
findings.problem: In-place update only happens for 'active' or 'trialing'. A past_due, unpaid or incomplete subscription falls through to a brand-new Checkout Session with another trial, while the old subscription keeps retrying the card.
findings.why_costs_money: Two subscriptions for one seller lead to double charges and disputes. It also gives an easy free trial to sellers who are behind on payment.
findings.fix: For past_due or unpaid, return a portal or hosted invoice URL to pay the open invoice instead of a new checkout.

findings.title: Webhooks write by customer, not subscription id, so a stale or duplicate subscription can overwrite the live one
findings.problem: handleSubscriptionUpdated and handleSubscriptionDeleted update users WHERE stripeCustomerId = customer. They don't check sub.id === users.subscriptionId or event ordering. Deleting an old duplicate subscription resets an active payer to canceled/starter, and an out-of-order 'trialing' event can overwrite 'active'.
findings.why_costs_money: Paying sellers lose access (support tickets, churn), or non-payers keep it.
findings.fix: Ignore events for a sub.id that differs from the stored subscriptionId unless the stored one is canceled. Compare event.created against a stored subscriptionUpdatedAt.

findings.title: Mid-cycle upgrade then immediate downgrade with prorations lets sellers rent Pro by the day
findings.problem: In-place plan changes use proration_behavior 'create_prorations' in both directions, take effect immediately, and need no payment confirmation (prorations go to the next invoice). A seller can switch to Pro, use unlimited AI or Live for a few days, then switch back and get credit.
findings.why_costs_money: This leaks Pro value and AI cost.
findings.fix: Apply downgrades at period end (a subscription schedule) and charge upgrades now (proration_behavior: 'always_invoice', payment_behavior: 'error_if_incomplete').

findings.title: No sales tax on seller subscriptions (automatic_tax missing)
findings.problem: Subscription Checkout sets no automatic_tax or tax_id_collection, while buyer checkout does (buyer.ts:1173, guest-checkout.ts:300). Several US states (TX, NY, WA, PA, OH and others) tax SaaS.
findings.why_costs_money: Brandthread owes the uncollected tax out of its own pocket once nexus thresholds are met.
findings.fix: Add automatic_tax: { enabled: true }, customer_update: { address: 'auto' } and tax_id_collection. IAP sales are taxed by Apple and Google.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~6-8% of web subscription revenue in exposed states

findings.title: Subscription prices are hard-coded in five places that must stay in sync
findings.problem: $29/$79/$199 are written into the server catalogue, mobile SELLER_PLANS, DEMO_PERKS, the RevenueCat seed and screen defaults, alongside the App Store Connect and Play prices (which have no code link). Dev hasn't decided prices. ensurePrice creates a new Stripe Price on mismatch, but native prices only change in App Store Connect.
findings.why_costs_money: Web and native drift (wrong amountCents shown, 'per week' maths off), and a price change becomes a multi-file release.
findings.fix: Keep planCatalogue as the only source. Have mobile read prices from /perks (web) and StoreKit (native). Check catalogue against RevenueCat product prices at boot.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect; prevents mispricing errors

findings.title: Promotion consumables give the full face value even though Apple keeps 15-30%
findings.problem: brandthread_boost_25 / brandthread_ad_25 sold at $24.99 grant $25 of reach budget. After Apple's cut Brandthread receives $17.49-21.24 but delivers $25 of inventory. The doc notes this but no price uplift was chosen.
findings.why_costs_money: Every native boost or ad sells inventory below its face value.
findings.fix: Price the store tiers about 18% above budget (for example the $25-budget tier at $29.99), or grant budget equal to Apple proceeds.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: 15-30% of native promotion revenue

findings.title: AI credit packs on iOS are correctly on IAP, but nothing checks for credits after a store purchase
findings.problem: Native packs use RevenueCat consumables (brandthread_ai_credits_500/1500/5000), which complies with 3.1.1. Credits are granted only by the NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE webhook. There is no client verify like iap-promotions has, and the screen silently stops after 12s of polling. If the webhook is misconfigured, the purchase is lost with no message. docs/review-readiness/iap-rails.md row 5 says 'No credit or pay-per-use AI product exists', which is stale.
findings.why_costs_money: Charged but not credited leads to refunds and reviews.
findings.fix: Add POST /ai/credits/purchases/verify-native, which reads the RevenueCat transaction like lookupRevenueCatPurchase, and show 'Purchase pending, credits will appear shortly' after polling times out. Update iap-rails.md.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$50-150/mo in refunds

findings.title: Credit-pack price falls back to the Stripe USD label on native when StoreKit has no product
findings.problem: canBuy on native only checks rc.available. The price shown is `storePrices[...] || formatPackPrice(pack.amountCents)`, so if the App Store product is missing or not approved, the screen shows '$5.99' and the purchase then fails with 'not available in the store yet'.
findings.why_costs_money: A reviewer sees a buy button that errors (2.1 rejection), and sellers lose trust.
findings.fix: On native, show a pack only when its StoreKit price loaded. Otherwise hide the pack list.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Review risk

findings.title: Meta Ads, store domain, email campaigns and push broadcasts have no in-app payment (no IAP exposure)
findings.problem: Meta bills the seller's own ad account, the custom domain is bring-your-own and free, and email and push sends are free with only a daily cap (dailySendCap) and no plan gate. None of these is an IAP problem. Email marketing and push broadcasts are open to unpaid sellers, though, and they cost money to send (Resend).
findings.why_costs_money: Typical upsell features are given away, and unpaid sellers generate email cost. Cross-ref ai-cost and seller-retention-tools.
findings.fix: Gate email campaigns and push broadcasts to Growth or any active entitlement, or set plan-based monthly send quotas in planCatalogue.limits.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-500/mo in upsell plus email cost

findings.title: The RevenueCat webhook secret falls back to SESSION_SECRET
findings.problem: If REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION is unset, 'Bearer ${SESSION_SECRET}' is accepted, and the seed script registers that same value with RevenueCat. The app's session-signing secret is then stored at a third party, and forged webhooks can trigger reconciliation.
findings.why_costs_money: A leaked session secret is a full account-takeover risk. Forged webhooks can only trigger reconciles, not grants.
findings.fix: Require a dedicated REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION in production (move it to REQUIRED_VARS productionOnly). Remove the fallback and rotate it.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Security; indirect

findings.title: Plan status and plan gating fail for team members (/status is owner-only)
findings.problem: useSubscriptionPlan calls /seller/subscription/status, which is requireRole('owner'). For a team member of a Pro store the call returns 403, the hook sets error=true, and Growth/Pro surfaces show locks or upsells even though the server (requirePlan uses the owner's entitlement) would allow them. /perks already exposes currentPlan to any team member.
findings.why_costs_money: Paying Pro stores get a broken experience for the staff they pay team seats for, which drives churn among top-tier sellers.
findings.fix: Have the hook read currentPlan from /seller/subscription/perks, which is not owner-only, or add a minimal /plan endpoint for team members.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Retention of Pro tier; ~$100-400/mo

findings.title: docs/review-readiness/iap-rails.md says 'PASS' for things the code contradicts
findings.problem: The doc says native seller plans PASS (but see the logOut and 5-day trial findings), that there are no AI credit packs (they exist, lib/aiCredits/purchases.ts), that there is no featured-slot product (Stripe-only, featured-slots.ts:295), and that Boost and Ads are FIXED (off by default in production builds).
findings.why_costs_money: Dev may submit believing 3.1.1 is cleared.
findings.fix: Update the table: featured slots FAIL, Boost and Ads FAIL unless the flag is set in EAS production, AI packs IAP PASS. Link this audit.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Prevents a launch-blocking rejection

findings.title: The server's day-4 trial banner is never rendered by the app
findings.problem: /status computes trialBanner (with copy and a 'Manage subscription' CTA) and the API client types it, along with dismissTrialBanner. grep finds no component that reads trialBanner, so the banner is dead.
findings.why_costs_money: A built conversion and transparency surface never reaches sellers.
findings.fix: Render the banner on the seller home dashboard when status.trialBanner.visible is true, with dismiss calling api.seller.subscription.dismissTrialBanner.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small; ~$100/mo

findings.title: Legal footer says 'App Store account settings' on Android and to web subscribers
findings.problem: The auto-renew disclosure is hard-coded to App Store wording for every platform and provider.
findings.why_costs_money: Google Play policy requires accurate cancellation instructions. Wrong instructions lead to 'couldn't cancel' disputes.
findings.fix: Choose the copy by Platform.OS (Google Play subscriptions) and by effectiveProvider (web: brandthread.app billing).

findings.title: If the one-time offer is enabled, it shows a discount but charges full price
findings.problem: handleOfferAccept calls handleSelect(offerPlan), which buys the normal $bt_* package or Stripe price. ONE_TIME_OFFER_PROMO_PRODUCT_ID is never used in a purchase path.
findings.why_costs_money: Advertising a discount and charging full price breaks 3.1.2/5.6 and consumer-protection rules the moment the flag is flipped.
findings.fix: Wire the offer to a real discounted package (RevenueCat promotional offer, Stripe coupon) before the flag can be turned on, and add a test.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Latent; $0 until enabled

findings.title: Exit drawer's per-week maths uses USD catalogue cents next to the localized store price
findings.problem: weeklyEquivalentFor and dailyEquivalentFor use plan.priceCents ($29) in USD while priceLabel is the StoreKit price string. A UK seller sees '£28.99/mo, that's about ~$6.67/wk'.
findings.why_costs_money: Mixed currencies on a paywall are a 3.1.2 'misleading pricing' risk and reduce trust.
findings.fix: Compute from pkg.product.price and currencyCode (RevenueCat exposes pricePerWeekString and pricePerMonthString).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small

findings.title: amountCents in /status for native comes from the USD catalogue, not the store
findings.problem: Native sellers see '$29.00/mo' (catalogue) even when Apple charges $29.99 or a localized price. finance.tsx falls back to formatCents(2900) '/mo' even for sellers with no plan.
findings.why_costs_money: A shown price that differs from the charge brings disputes and 'overcharged' tickets.
findings.fix: Use the RevenueCat package priceString client-side for native. Hide the price line when the status is 'none'.

findings.title: Freelancer job payments use Stripe in-app for possibly digital deliverables (3.1.3(e) gray zone)
findings.problem: Seller-to-freelancer escrow is paid through Stripe Checkout in an in-app auth session. Deliverables can be digital files (logos, designs). Apple allows person-to-person services (3.1.3(d)) but has rejected cases where a digital good is delivered in the app.
findings.why_costs_money: There is some rejection risk. This is only documented, not mitigated.
findings.fix: Keep it, explain it in Review Notes as a real-time person-to-person service marketplace (already in app-store-metadata.md), and make sure deliverables are not presented as app content. Have a fallback plan to hide the feature on iOS if review flags it.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Review risk only

findings.title: Physical-goods checkout, store gift cards, samples and labels correctly use Stripe (keep off IAP)
findings.problem: These are compliant: physical goods (3.1.3(e)) and store gift cards redeemable only for a seller's physical products may not use IAP. A risk only appears if sellers can list digital or downloadable products (grep 'isDigital' or 'digital_download' finds none today), in which case those listings and gift cards for them would need IAP.
findings.why_costs_money: Putting this through IAP would cost 15-30% for nothing. Allowing digital listings later would trigger 3.1.1.
findings.fix: Keep Stripe. Add a policy and a schema guard that listings must be physical, and say so in Review Notes.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Protects ~15-30% of GMV from wrongly going through IAP

findings.title: /status calls Stripe live on every plan check
findings.problem: Every focus of subscription, billing, more or settings, and every invalidatePlanCache, triggers stripe.subscriptions.retrieve with expand. If Stripe is slow or rate-limited, the route returns 500 and the client keeps the default 'Starter $29' card, so a paying seller looks unpaid.
findings.why_costs_money: A paying seller who appears unpaid opens support tickets and may cancel; the extra API load adds latency to paid screens.
findings.fix: Serve status from the webhook-synced users columns, and retrieve from Stripe only on an explicit refresh or once per day.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small

findings.title: Unverifiable social-proof and 'start free' claims on the paywall
findings.problem: 'Trusted by independent brands building on Brandthread' appears on a pre-launch app with no brands yet. The subtitle 'start free' sits above a paid-only plan list.
findings.why_costs_money: These invite Apple 2.3.1 and 5.6 accuracy objections and buyer and seller distrust.
findings.fix: Remove the social proof until there are real counts (pull a seller count from the API). Change the subtitle to 'Try free for N days'.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Review risk only

findings.title: RevenueCat consumable refunds don't revoke boosts or ads, and credit-pack refunds don't claw back credits
findings.problem: There is no handling of RevenueCat CANCELLATION with cancel_reason=CUSTOMER_SUPPORT (refund) for NON_RENEWING products. A seller can buy 5,000 credits or a $500 boost, use it, and get Apple to refund it.
findings.why_costs_money: Refund abuse comes straight out of AI provider cost and ad inventory.
findings.fix: On refund events for credit products, debit purchasedBalance (allowing it to go negative and block). For promo products, end the active boost or ad.

findings.title: Restore Purchases fails silently for a signed-in team member and doesn't say what was restored
findings.problem: sync() returns early unless currentRole==='owner', so restore on a team member's device never reconciles. Owners always see 'Purchases restored' even when nothing was found (no check of customerInfo.entitlements or activeSubscriptions).
findings.why_costs_money: Restore is required by 3.1.1, so App Review taps it. Sellers who reinstall can't tell whether access came back, which brings support tickets and duplicate purchases.
findings.fix: After restore, read customerInfo.activeSubscriptions and show 'No active subscription found on this Apple ID' or the plan name.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small

findings.title: Seller-issued gift cards are paid out of Brandthread's balance when redeemed
findings.problem: issueSellerCard creates a live card with 'no payment, no liability', but on redemption finalizeGiftCardsForGroup -> payoutSellerForOrder transfers the full redeemed amount to the seller from the platform balance, and settledRedemptions never checks the card's source. A seller can issue unlimited $1,000 cards (POST /gift-cards/seller/issue) to an alt account, 'buy' their own items, and receive real money that no one paid. The payout also goes out at payment time, before delivery, so the hold does not protect it.
findings.why_costs_money: This is direct theft of platform cash at up to $1,000 per card with no cap on how many cards a seller issues. Reversal on refund only works while the seller's Stripe balance still holds the funds.
findings.fix: In payoutSellerForOrder, pay out only redemptions of cards with source='purchase'. Seller-issued redemptions should reduce the seller's own net, as a seller-funded discount. Also gate the gift card payout behind payoutMayRelease, the same delivery hold other payouts use.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Unbounded: one bad seller with 10 cards drains $10k. At minimum, every legitimate seller-issued promo card at $50k scale (~$2-5k/mo) is paid by Brandthread.

findings.title: payment_intent.* events not in the managed webhook subscription: in-app checkout orders never created
findings.problem: The default mobile payment path is the one-page PaymentIntent (choosePaymentPath returns 'in_app'). Orders and gift-card activation are created only in the payment_intent.succeeded handler. REQUIRED_EVENTS, which ensureWebhookEvents merges into the Stripe endpoint, lists no payment_intent.* events. Nothing reconciles a succeeded PaymentIntent that has no order: GET /payment-intent/:id only reports status. Unless someone adds the events in the Dashboard by hand, buyers are charged and no order, payout or stock commit ever happens.
findings.why_costs_money: Charged buyers with no orders lead to chargebacks, refunds and lost sellers on day one. Those disputes land on the platform account because the charge is on Brandthread's balance.
findings.fix: Add payment_intent.succeeded, payment_intent.payment_failed, payment_intent.canceled, review.opened and review.closed to REQUIRED_EVENTS. Add a sweep that finds succeeded cart PaymentIntents without orders and calls handleCartPaymentSucceeded.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks all in-app revenue if the Dashboard is not configured by hand: 100% of in-app GMV.

findings.title: Manual seller orders get free shipping labels on Brandthread's Shippo account
findings.problem: POST /api/orders lets a seller create an off-platform order with client-priced custom items (charge_model NULL, status 'pending'). Those orders are label-eligible. The only funds check is order.total_cents (seller-chosen) minus reservations. recordLabelPurchased writes no ledger posting when chargeModel is null, and recoverLabelCost skips anything that is not destination or transfer. The carrier is paid by Brandthread and never recovered.
findings.why_costs_money: Any seller can ship their Etsy/IRL orders on Brandthread's Shippo bill indefinitely.
findings.fix: Refuse label purchase unless the order has a stripe_payment_intent_id and charge_model in (held, transfer, destination). Alternatively, charge manual-order labels to the seller's card or Stripe balance up front.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $8-15 per label. 100 abusive labels a month is about $1k, and it is unbounded.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Shippo webhook can mark orders delivered (payout) or return labels scanned (refund)
findings.problem: verifySharedSecret returns true when SHIPPO_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, and env.ts lists it as optional. Anyone can POST a DELIVERED tracking_status with metadata 'brandthread-order/<id>' or a known tracking number. That starts the 3-day payout clock for a seller who never shipped. A forged scan on a 'brandthread-return-label/<id>' triggers the return refund without goods coming back.
findings.why_costs_money: This defeats the whole hold-until-delivered model. The seller is paid, the buyer later wins a 'not received' chargeback on the platform account, and the platform eats it plus the $15 dispute fee.
findings.fix: Make SHIPPO_WEBHOOK_SECRET required in production (env.ts) and fail closed. Before treating a DELIVERED webhook as truth, re-fetch the track from the Shippo API.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Per fraud event: full order value + $15 dispute fee. A small ring could take $5-20k/mo.

findings.title: Stripe fee (and label cost) on refunds before payout is booked to an orphan 'seller owes' row never collected
findings.problem: For held/transfer orders refunded before the transfer, sellerShare = refund - 5% return. The order's held balance is only gross - fee - processing - labels, so the difference is posted to seller_held with orderId NULL and drop NULL. settleTransferOrder only pays the per-order balance and never nets that row. The finance 'owed' figure only counts negative balances on failed/completed drops, so this debt is invisible and never recovered. delivery-guarantee.md:23 claims the fee 'is charged to the seller's held funds'.
findings.why_costs_money: In hold mode Brandthread pays Stripe's 2.9%+30c, plus any label already bought, on every buyer cancellation, seller cancellation, auto-refund and pre-payout return.
findings.fix: Net seller-level negative seller_held against the seller's next settleTransferOrder or release. Also show it as 'owed' in /finance/summary, and fix the doc.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: At ~$1M GMV and an 8% pre-payout refund rate: $80k x ~3.2% = ~$2.5k/mo, plus unrecovered labels.

findings.title: Plan perks cut commission to 4% (Growth) and 3% (Pro); owner's rule is 5% on every sale
findings.problem: resolveSellerPlatformFeeBps charges 400 bps for growth and 300 bps for pro. The fee is applied to every checkout path (buyer.ts:1035, guest-checkout.ts:250, cartCheckout.ts:279). Sellers in 'trial', 'trialing', 'grace' or 'past_due' status also get the discounted rate, so a free-trial Pro seller pays 3%. The UI still promises 5% everywhere (subscription.tsx:9,343,552).
findings.why_costs_money: Commission revenue on Growth/Pro GMV falls 20-40%, and trial or past-due sellers get the cut without paying for the plan.
findings.fix: Set all PLAN_PERKS platformFeeBps to PLATFORM_FEE_BPS, or have Dev explicitly approve tiered commission. If tiered, only apply it for status 'active' (not trial/past_due/grace).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: If 40% of a $1M GMV is Growth/Pro, the loss is ~$6k/mo (1-2% of that GMV).

findings.title: Commission bypass: 5% is on merchandise only, sellers can move price into shipping
findings.problem: Platform fee = 5% x (subtotal - discounts) and excludes shipping. Shipping is any seller-chosen flat or zone rate with no cap or sanity check. A seller can list a $5 item with $45 shipping and pay 25c commission instead of $2.50.
findings.why_costs_money: This is a classic marketplace fee-avoidance pattern (eBay charges FVF on shipping for this reason). Once known, top sellers use it.
findings.fix: Charge the platform fee on merchandise + shipping, or cap shipping at a multiple of the quoted label cost and flag outliers.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: If 10% of GMV shifts to shipping: $1M x 10% x 5% = ~$5k/mo.

findings.title: Dispute on an already-paid-out order: no transfer reversal, platform eats chargeback
findings.problem: When charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn hits a transfer/held order whose funds are 'released' (paid at delivery+3 days), recordDisputeWithdrawal only posts platform_funds_advanced (seller owes). No transfers.createReversal is attempted and nothing collects the debt later. Chargebacks typically arrive 2-8 weeks after payment, which is after the hold window.
findings.why_costs_money: In hold mode every charge is on the platform account, so Stripe debits Brandthread for 100% of each post-payout chargeback.
findings.fix: On funds_withdrawn for released orders, reverse the order's transfer (stripe_transfer_id or release transfer) up to the disputed amount. If the seller balance is short, net it from the next payouts. Re-transfer on funds_reinstated.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: At a 0.5% dispute rate on $1M GMV with ~70% post-payout: ~$3.5k/mo.

findings.title: Hold mode makes Brandthread merchant of record: no on_behalf_of, all risk on platform
findings.problem: PAYOUT_MODE defaults to 'hold', and the one-page checkout always uses 'transfer', so every sale is a platform charge with no on_behalf_of or transfer_data. Brandthread is the settlement merchant. The platform's descriptor appears on statements, every dispute and refund debits the platform, Radar and dispute ratios count against Dev's single Stripe account, and Stripe can impose a reserve on the delayed-fulfilment GMV (18+ days). money-flow.md section 8 lists confirmations that are still open.
findings.why_costs_money: A dispute rate above about 0.75% on one account can freeze ALL marketplace funds. A Stripe reserve could lock 10-25% of GMV right when cash is needed.
findings.fix: Before launch, get written Stripe sign-off on separate charges and transfers with an ~18-60 day hold, and on reserve terms. Consider on_behalf_of so sellers are merchant of record, and set the platform's own payout schedule so held GMV isn't swept to Dev's bank.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Tail risk: an account freeze blocks all revenue. A typical 10% reserve on $1M GMV ties up ~$100k.

findings.title: Platform account payout schedule not addressed: held GMV may be auto-paid to Dev's bank
findings.problem: The hold model keeps up to ~18 days (regular) or 60+ days (preorder) of seller money on the platform balance. Nothing configures or documents that the platform account must be on manual payouts. Thread Cash top-ups and gift-card payouts are transfers without source_transaction, so they draw from available platform balance and fail with balance_insufficient if Stripe already paid it out.
findings.why_costs_money: Seller money could be swept to Dev's bank, and later transfers would fail or push the platform negative. Commingled funds are also a money-transmission risk.
findings.fix: Set the platform Stripe account to manual payouts and add a launch checklist item. Add a reconciliation job that alerts when available balance is below total seller_held.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Operational: failed seller payouts, support load, possible account review. Exposure is the full held balance (~$500k at $1M GMV).

findings.title: Auto-refund is refund-by-default when no 'delivered' signal: delivered goods get refunded
findings.problem: Any item without delivered_at at day 15 (60 for pre-orders) is fully refunded with restock:false. Delivered is set only by a mapped Shippo carrier scan or the signed-in buyer tapping 'I received it'. Unknown carriers (shippoCarrierToken null), local delivery, hand-typed tracking typos and guest orders (no in-app confirm) all refund automatically even when the parcel arrived. The buyer keeps the goods.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers lose goods and revenue and will churn. Brandthread loses its 5% (returned via platformFeeRefundCents) and eats the Stripe fee (see orphan-owed finding).
findings.fix: Before refunding a shipped order with valid accepted/in-transit scans, require a buyer 'not received' claim (or at least an email confirm prompt) instead of refunding by default. Keep auto-refund for 'never shipped / no scan'.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: If 2% of shipped orders lack a delivered scan: $1M x 2% = $20k GMV refunded/mo, costing ~$1k platform fees and Stripe fees plus seller churn.

findings.title: Pre-order ship date and drop deadline (180d) exceed the 60-day auto-refund
findings.problem: Drops may have a fulfillment deadline up to 180 days out, and validatePreorderListing only checks the ship date is in the future (no max). Each pre-order item's deliver_by is fixed at paid_at + 60 days, so a drop shipping on day 90 auto-refunds every buyer at day 60. By then the seller has often paid the manufacturer bulk card from held funds (pay-from-wallet).
findings.why_costs_money: Refunds exceed what is held. The shortfall is 'owed' by the seller but never collected, so Brandthread funds the buyers' refunds.
findings.fix: Cap preOrderEstShipDate and fulfillmentDeadlineAt so delivery fits in 60 days, or set preorder deliver_by = promised ship date + 15 days (max 180).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: One mis-dated $20k drop with bulk paid costs Brandthread up to the bulk amount (e.g. $8-12k).

findings.title: Seller can drain held pre-order money to any 'manufacturer' at any price
findings.problem: The seller alone creates a bulk production order with a self-chosen priceCents against any manufacturer id, then pays it from the drop wallet. Nothing requires the manufacturer to accept or quote, checks that the manufacturer isn't controlled by the seller, or caps the amount below collected pre-order money. The money leaves as a Stripe transfer before any buyer item ships.
findings.why_costs_money: A seller with an alt manufacturer account converts buyers' held pre-order cash into withdrawable money. When the drop fails, buyers are refunded and the shortfall is uncollected, so Brandthread pays.
findings.fix: Require manufacturer acceptance of the quote, a verified manufacturer, and no shared identity, bank or Stripe person with the seller. Cap wallet-funded bulk at a % of held funds, or release it to the manufacturer only on shipment proof.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Fraud exposure equals pre-order GMV per drop. One incident could cost $10k+.

findings.title: Platform-wide loyalty and referral points are deducted from the seller's payout and the fee basis
findings.problem: Brandthread loyalty points (100 on signup, 500 per referral, 1 per $1 at any store) are redeemed against any seller's order. The code treats them as 'seller-funded': they reduce both the 5% fee basis and the seller's payout (no top-up, unlike Thread Cash).
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers pay for Brandthread's own buyer-referral program, which contradicts 'referral rewards for buyers, paid by Brandthread' and creates seller disputes. The platform also loses 5% on each redeemed dollar.
findings.fix: Treat loyalty like Thread Cash: exclude it from the fee basis and top up or add it to seller_held from a platform loyalty-expense account. Alternatively, fold loyalty into Thread Cash.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~1% of GMV earn-back = ~$10k/mo shifted to sellers once redeemed, plus 5% of that in lost fee.

findings.title: No sales-tax collection unless each seller registers in Stripe Tax; platform is facilitator
findings.problem: Tax is calculated on the seller's connected account (stripeAccount: seller), which returns $0 unless that Express seller added state registrations. POST /taxes/enable only sets tax_behavior. Brandthread is the charging party (hold/transfer) and a marketplace facilitator under most US state laws once state thresholds are met, so the platform, not the seller, owes the uncollected tax. Collected tax is passed to sellers inside their transfer.
findings.why_costs_money: Uncollected sales tax becomes a platform liability plus penalties, and collected tax handed to sellers may also be owed by Brandthread as facilitator.
findings.fix: Calculate tax on the platform account with Brandthread's facilitator registrations, keep the tax portion out of seller transfers, and remit centrally. Get a CPA opinion before launch.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~7% of taxable GMV once thresholds are crossed: on $1M/mo, ~$70k/mo of potential liability accrual.

findings.title: Seller debts ('owed') are displayed but never collected
findings.problem: Drop shortfalls, failed label recoveries, external refunds and dispute withdrawals are recorded as platform_funds_advanced or negative seller_held. The doc says 'collection policy is an owner decision', and no code nets them against future transfers or uses account debits.
findings.why_costs_money: Every seller debt becomes a platform write-off, and sellers learn they can walk away.
findings.fix: Add owed-netting to settleTransferOrder and executeOrderRelease, and block cash-outs while owed > 0. For large debts, use Stripe account debits (Custom) or invoices.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Sums the leaks above: likely $3-8k/mo at scale.

findings.title: Connect events (account.updated, payout.paid) need a Connect endpoint and secret; neither exists
findings.problem: Connected-account events are delivered only to a Connect webhook endpoint (a separate endpoint with its own signing secret). The server verifies with a single STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and manages one account endpoint, and payout.paid isn't in REQUIRED_EVENTS. users.stripe_account_status is refreshed only when the seller opens GET /connect/status. payout.failed is not handled at all.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers who finish Stripe onboarding outside the app stay 'pending' and can't sell. Restricted sellers keep selling while transfers fail. Failed bank payouts go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a Connect webhook endpoint with STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET (try both secrets), and subscribe account.updated, payout.paid, payout.failed and capability.updated.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Lost first sales from new sellers stuck in 'pending'. 5% of onboarded sellers stuck = ~$2-5k GMV/mo.

findings.title: Seller-typed tracking numbers are not verified against destination, so any delivered parcel unlocks payout
findings.problem: A seller can type any real tracking number (e.g. one of their own delivered parcels). The hourly poll maps DELIVERED to delivered_at and payout_release_at, and the seller is paid in 3 days. Nothing checks the Shippo track's destination ZIP or city against the order address.
findings.why_costs_money: The buyer never receives the goods and files a chargeback on the platform account after the payout.
findings.fix: Compare the track's address_to ZIP or city with the order shipping address before accepting delivered. Otherwise require buyer confirmation for manual tracking.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Fraud: full order value + $15 per incident. A few % of bad sellers could cost $2-10k/mo.

findings.title: Hold delays all seller payouts ~18+ days with no explanation in payout screens
findings.problem: Payouts and finance screens show Stripe available/pending balance, but most seller money now sits on the platform until delivery + 3 days. Neither payouts.tsx nor finance.tsx contains any 'delivery' or 'hold' copy. Sellers see $0 available for weeks after their first sales.
findings.why_costs_money: New sellers think they're not being paid, which means support tickets, churn before the first payout, and bad reviews.
findings.fix: Show a per-order 'Paid after delivery + 3 days' timeline and a 'held for delivery' total on payouts.tsx, using /finance/summary held, and set expectations during onboarding.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: If 10% of new sellers churn over the payout delay: ~$5k GMV/mo lost early.

findings.title: Buyer refund request with photos always fails (local file URIs sent as evidence)
findings.problem: The screen sends ImagePicker asset URIs (file://) as evidenceUrls. The server only accepts URLs starting with the buyer's evidence upload prefix, so any request with photos gets a 400 and the generic 'Could not submit' alert. The request also goes to /returns, which rejects orders that aren't shipped or delivered.
findings.why_costs_money: Buyers who can't request a refund in-app file chargebacks instead ($15 fee + amount on the platform account).
findings.fix: Upload photos via POST /returns/evidence first and send the returned URLs. Route pre-shipment cases to the buyer cancel endpoint.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Every chargeback that replaces a refund costs an extra $15. ~30/mo = ~$450 + dispute-ratio risk.

findings.title: $15 Stripe dispute fee not modelled, always borne by Brandthread
findings.problem: The dispute fee is stored on dispute_events.payload.feeCents but never posted to the ledger or charged to the seller. In hold mode the dispute fee is debited from the platform balance.
findings.why_costs_money: Every chargeback costs Brandthread $15, whether won or lost (Stripe refunds it only on some wins).
findings.fix: Post the fee as a seller debit (seller_held or platform_funds_advanced) and recover it from the next release, or price it into policy. Document the decision.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$15 per dispute. At ~50 disputes/mo (0.5% of 10k orders), ~$750/mo.

findings.title: Connect Express platform fees ($2/active account, 0.25%+25c per payout) unmodelled
findings.problem: Sellers are Express accounts where the platform pays Connect's per-active-account and per-payout fees. Nothing in fees.ts, ledger or seller pricing accounts for them. Sellers can pick a 'daily' payout schedule, which maximises per-payout fees.
findings.why_costs_money: These costs come straight out of the 5%. 0.25% of payout volume is 5% of Brandthread's commission, plus $2 per active seller per month.
findings.fix: Default sellers to weekly payouts, model the Connect fees in the ledger, and price them into plans or pass them through.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $1M payouts: 0.25% = $2.5k + 25c x ~4k payouts = $1k + $2 x 500 sellers = $1k, so ~$4.5k/mo.

findings.title: Gift card purchases: platform pays Stripe processing, takes no commission on that payment
findings.problem: Gift-card PaymentIntents are charged on the platform with no fee recorded. At redemption, the full face value is transferred to the seller. The ~2.9%+30c Stripe fee on the gift card purchase is never passed on, and unredeemed balances sit as platform liability (escheat/unclaimed-property exposure).
findings.why_costs_money: Every purchased gift card costs Brandthread ~3% plus 30c.
findings.fix: Deduct the processing fee from the seller's gift card payout at redemption, or charge the buyer a fee. Track breakage and escheat by state.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $20k/mo of gift card sales x 3.2% = ~$640/mo.

findings.title: Gift card seller payout ignores the delivery hold and partial refunds
findings.problem: The gift-card portion is transferred to the seller as soon as the order webhook runs, not after delivery and the buffer. It is reversed only on a FULL refund. A partial or auto refund of undelivered items leaves the seller with the gift card money, and the reversal fails if the seller already cashed out.
findings.why_costs_money: Hold-mode protection is bypassed for the gift-card share, so refund losses fall on the platform.
findings.fix: Book the gift card amount into seller_held for the order and release it with settleTransferOrder. Reverse proportionally on partial refunds.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small at launch (<$500/mo), but it multiplies the seller-issued-card exploit.

findings.title: Platform returns its 5% on every refund, including seller-fault auto-refunds
findings.problem: platformFeeRefundCents returns Brandthread's commission proportionally on every refund reason: not_delivered (seller failed to ship), seller_cancelled, oversold and drop_failed. The platform still paid Stripe processing and support costs on that sale.
findings.why_costs_money: Brandthread earns $0 on seller-caused failures while bearing the costs, which is not standard (Etsy and eBay keep fees on seller cancellations).
findings.fix: Keep the platform fee on seller_cancelled, not_delivered, oversold and drop_failed refunds (charge it to the seller's held money). Return it only on buyer_cancelled or approved returns.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~5% of seller-fault refunds: $40k/mo x 5% = ~$2k/mo.

findings.title: Returns have no return window and can arrive after payout, so clawback depends on seller balance
findings.problem: POST /returns accepts any shipped or delivered order with no time limit. The payout goes out at delivery + 3 days. A later return refund reverses the transfer only if the seller's Stripe balance covers it. On failure it just logs, and the remainder goes to the orphan seller_held row (never collected).
findings.why_costs_money: With Express accounts the platform bears negative balances, so refunds on returns after payout leak to Brandthread.
findings.fix: Enforce a return window (e.g. 14 or 30 days from delivery) and set PAYOUT_RELEASE_BUFFER_DAYS to that window, or keep a rolling reserve. Recover failed reversals from the next transfers.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~1-2% of GMV returned post-payout x ~20% unrecoverable = ~$2-4k/mo.

findings.title: Webhook 'transfer' ledger can be unbalanced if quoted fee differs from webhook split
findings.problem: For transfer orders, recordOrderPaid uses split.sellerNetCents (computed with split.platformFeeCents) but posts platform_revenue = decidedPlatformFee (the checkout-time fee). If the two differ (Stripe discount rounding, coupon capped, fee capped at preTaxTotal vs gross), the postings don't sum to zero. The deferred balance trigger then rejects the whole order transaction, so the webhook fails forever and the buyer is charged with no order.
findings.why_costs_money: Silent order loss on edge cases leads to chargebacks.
findings.fix: Recompute sellerNet = gross - decidedPlatformFee - processing in the transfer/held branch, as the destination branch already does.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Rare. Each occurrence costs a full order + a $15 dispute.

findings.title: Production boots with Stripe test keys; no live-mode guard
findings.problem: env.ts requires STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in production but accepts sk_test_. Only staging is checked (refusing live keys). EXPO_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY has no mode check against the server key either.
findings.why_costs_money: Launching on test keys means 'orders' take no real money until someone notices.
findings.fix: In production, refuse to boot unless STRIPE_SECRET_KEY matches sk_live_ or rk_live_. Add a /health check comparing the publishable key mode.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks all revenue for the duration of the mistake.

findings.title: Connect accounts hard-coded to US individual Express
findings.problem: accounts.create always uses country 'US' and business_type 'individual'. LLC or corporate sellers must onboard as individuals (wrong 1099/W-9 entity), and non-US brands cannot onboard at all. The account is created the first time the seller taps, so a wrong prefill sticks.
findings.why_costs_money: Lost non-US sellers, KYC friction, and tax reporting errors for business sellers.
findings.fix: Ask country and entity type before creating the account (or omit business_type so Stripe asks). Support Canada/UK if marketing reaches them.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: If 10% of seller signups are LLCs or non-US: ~10% of new seller GMV at risk.

findings.title: 'Stripe files your 1099' claim unconfigured; 1099-K thresholds outdated
findings.problem: The UI tells sellers 'W-9 on file. Stripe files your 1099'. Stripe only does that if the platform enables Connect tax reporting (per-form fees billed to the platform), and as charging party (hold mode) Brandthread is the filer of record. The threshold table shows $2,500 (2025) and $600 (2026+). Federal law since July 2025 (OBBBA) restored $20,000 and 200 transactions (verify).
findings.why_costs_money: IRS penalties for missed or incorrect 1099-K filings (~$310 per form). Over-filing at $600 means paying Stripe per-form fees for hundreds of tiny sellers.
findings.fix: Enable Stripe Connect 1099 reporting with the correct thresholds, budget per-form fees, and correct the copy and threshold table.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Annual: ~$3-5 per form x sellers over threshold. The penalty tail is far larger.

findings.title: Radar: docs assume destination charges; rules not configured, review events not subscribed
findings.problem: radar-rules.md describes Connect destination charges, but production uses platform charges (hold or transfer). Every rule in it is Dashboard-only, with nothing in code verifying it. review.opened and review.closed are not in REQUIRED_EVENTS, so the seller 'Review before shipping' pill never updates from Radar reviews. Radar for Fraud Teams is needed for any custom rule and is not budgeted.
findings.why_costs_money: Card-testing and stolen-card fraud land as platform chargebacks ($15 fee + goods + dispute-ratio risk).
findings.fix: Update the doc for platform charges, enable Radar for Fraud Teams with B1-B5, R1 and S3, and add review events to REQUIRED_EVENTS.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Radar Teams ~$0.02-0.07/txn x 10k = $200-700/mo, versus fraud losses of several $k/mo.

findings.title: Thread Cash top-up failures on destination orders are retried only on webhook redelivery
findings.problem: If transfers.create fails (insufficient platform balance, network), the code logs 'will retry on next webhook delivery'. The webhook still returns 200, so Stripe never redelivers, and no sweep exists for missing top-ups.
findings.why_costs_money: The seller is permanently short-paid by the Thread Cash amount (immediate mode), which drives support cost and churn.
findings.fix: Add top-ups to moneySweep: orders where thread_cash_applied_cents > 0 AND stripe_thread_cash_transfer_id IS NULL.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small. Only relevant in immediate mode.

findings.title: Buyer cancel within 21 days (pre-ship) refunds in full; platform eats Stripe fee
findings.problem: Buyers can cancel any unshipped order for 21 days, getting a full refund including shipping. In hold mode the non-refundable Stripe fee plus the returned 5% leave a negative orphan seller_held that is never collected.
findings.why_costs_money: Brandthread pays ~3.2% of every buyer-cancelled order and earns nothing.
findings.fix: Charge the processing fee to the seller's held funds (or to the buyer as a cancellation fee), shorten the window to 24-48h pre-shipment, and net seller debts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: 3% cancel rate x $1M x 3.2% = ~$1k/mo.

findings.title: Label bought, then order auto-refunded: label cost and fees fall to platform
findings.problem: In hold mode a label is paid from the order's held funds. If the parcel never gets a delivered scan, auto-refund returns the full charged amount (items + shipping). Held funds no longer cover it, and the gap (label + Stripe fee) goes to the orphan seller-level row.
findings.why_costs_money: Brandthread funds the label and the Stripe fee on every undelivered-but-labelled order.
findings.fix: Net seller-level debt from future transfers. If no carrier scan occurred within N days, void the unused label via Shippo refundTransaction automatically.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$10 per occurrence. 200/mo = ~$2k/mo.

findings.title: Pre-order buyer dispute window (120d after expected delivery) exceeds held period
findings.problem: Card networks allow 'not received' or 'not as described' disputes up to 120 days after expected delivery. Hold mode releases at delivery + 3 days, and there is no rolling reserve (PAYOUT_POLICY_ENFORCED=false, payoutPolicy.ts:55).
findings.why_costs_money: Late disputes are paid by the platform (see the no-reversal finding).
findings.fix: Enable the reserve mode (RESERVE_BPS 10% for 30-90 days) for new or high-risk sellers, and wire PAYOUT_POLICY_ENFORCED.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Reduces dispute leakage (~$3k/mo) by about half.

findings.title: Webhook idempotency solid; external dashboard refunds booked as uncollected seller debt
findings.problem: Refunds issued in the Stripe Dashboard on released or destination orders are booked to platform_funds_advanced ('seller owes') without reversing the seller transfer. Any ops refund made in the Dashboard is therefore paid by Brandthread.
findings.why_costs_money: Support staff refunding via the Dashboard leak 100% of the refund amount.
findings.fix: Add an admin refund endpoint that uses refundOrder, and block or alert on Dashboard refunds.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Every Dashboard refund is a 100% loss: ~$500-2k/mo depending on ops habits.

findings.title: Seller payout status 'active' requires charges_enabled although hold mode needs only transfers
findings.problem: Accounts request card_payments, and checkout requires stripeAccountStatus 'active' (charges_enabled && payouts_enabled). In hold mode the platform charges and only transfers is needed, so the extra card_payments KYC requirements delay or block sellers from their first sale.
findings.why_costs_money: Slower time-to-first-sale, so more sellers abandon onboarding.
findings.fix: In hold mode, gate selling on the transfers capability (payouts can come later, as the transfer waits) and request card_payments only if destination mode is used.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: A few % more activated sellers: ~$2k GMV/mo.

findings.title: Stripe Tax calculation on every quote: per-call cost on the platform
findings.problem: POST /quote (called on address changes and wallet-sheet updates) and POST / each call stripe.tax.calculations.create for every seller group. Stripe Tax API usage is billed, and for Express accounts Connect fees are billed to the platform. It is not cached by address and cart.
findings.why_costs_money: Several billable tax calculations per completed checkout (quotes x seller groups), most of which never convert.
findings.fix: Cache calculations per (cart hash, ZIP) for 10-30 minutes, and only call Stripe Tax at final create when the address hasn't changed.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Assuming ~$0.05+ per call x ~5 calls per checkout x 10k checkouts = ~$2.5k/mo (verify current Stripe Tax pricing).

findings.title: Free-shipping discount codes reduce the 5% fee basis by the shipping amount
findings.problem: discountCodeAmountCents includes the waived shipping amount, and merchandiseCents = subtotal - combinedDiscount. A free-shipping code lowers the commission basis by the shipping cost even though merchandise wasn't discounted.
findings.why_costs_money: This is lost commission on every free-shipping code order.
findings.fix: Use merchandiseDiscountCents (exclude shippingDiscountCents) for the fee basis in both buyer.ts and cartCheckout.priceCartGroup.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$8 shipping x 5% x 3k free-ship orders = ~$1.2k/mo.

findings.title: Stripe key missing: checkout returns 503 silently; payouts screen hides it
findings.problem: With no STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (allowed outside NODE_ENV=production), every money route returns 503 STRIPE_NOT_CONFIGURED. connect/status returns 'provider_unavailable' instead of erroring. There is no alert or health signal, so a misconfigured deploy looks healthy.
findings.why_costs_money: Silent revenue outage.
findings.fix: Expose stripeConfigured in /health and page on it. Make APP_ENV=production (not just NODE_ENV) enforce the key.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Outage minutes x GMV rate.

findings.title: Fee schedule and quote API always show 5%, ignoring plan rate and BNPL fees
findings.problem: getFeeSchedule and quoteSale use PLATFORM_FEE_BPS and 2.9%+30c for everyone. Actual charges use plan bps (3-5%) and Stripe's real fee, including BNPL (Klarna/Afterpay ~6%+30c) passed to sellers in transfer mode.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers who see more deducted than quoted file support tickets and churn. Mismatched 'fees' copy also risks App Store and FTC fee-transparency issues.
findings.fix: Make the fee quote seller-aware (plan bps) and show BNPL as a separate line, or absorb or limit BNPL.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Support and churn: hard to size, <$1k/mo.

findings.title: Processing estimate (2.9%+30c on pre-tax) undercharges in immediate mode; variance eaten by platform
findings.problem: With PAYOUT_MODE=immediate, application_fee = 5% + 2.9% x pre-tax total + 30c. Stripe's real fee is on the tax-inclusive total plus +1.5% international and +1% FX, and BNPL is ~6%. The difference is posted to processing_fee_variance and absorbed by Brandthread.
findings.why_costs_money: Roughly 0.2-0.5% of GMV in immediate mode, more with international or BNPL buyers.
findings.fix: Keep hold or transfer as the only mode, or charge the actual fee by computing application_fee after the charge.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Only if Dev flips to immediate: ~$2-5k/mo at $1M GMV.

findings.title: Sample/bulk manufacturer charges: 5% application fee must absorb Stripe's fee
findings.problem: Seller card payments for samples and bulk are destination charges with application_fee_amount = 5% only. On destination charges Stripe debits the platform for processing (2.9%+30c, plus 1.5% for international cards), so Brandthread nets ~2%. Bulk orders paid from held funds carry 0% fee. Refunds and disputes on these charges also hit the platform.
findings.why_costs_money: Thin or negative margin on large B2B tickets.
