findings.fix: Add the processing estimate to application_fee_amount (as for buyer orders) and take the fee on wallet-funded bulk too.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $50k/mo bulk volume x ~3% = ~$1.5k/mo.

findings.title: Instant payout fee constant 1%: Stripe US instant payout pricing likely 1.5%
findings.problem: INSTANT_PAYOUT_FEE_BPS=100 is used for the seller quote and the maxInstantPayoutCents cap. If Stripe charges more (current US pricing is 1.5%, min $0.50, verify) or bills Express instant-payout fees to the platform, quotes are wrong and payouts can fail for insufficient balance.
findings.why_costs_money: Failed cash-outs or platform-borne instant fees.
findings.fix: Verify against stripe.com/pricing and the Connect fee settings, read the fee from Stripe's payout balance transaction, and add a platform margin if desired.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: 0.5% of instant volume: $100k instant = $500/mo.

findings.title: Statement CSV download opens an unauthenticated URL (401)
findings.problem: handleDownloadStatement calls Linking.openURL on /api/finance/statement.csv without the Clerk bearer token, and the route requires auth. Sellers get an error page.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers can't reconcile payouts or taxes, which adds support load and erodes trust.
findings.fix: Fetch with auth and share the file via expo-sharing, or mint a short-lived signed download URL.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Support cost only.

findings.title: Shipping labels sold at cost: no margin, and Shippo fees absorbed
findings.problem: The label price shown and charged is exactly rate.amount from Shippo. Shippo per-label or plan fees and failed or voided label costs are not passed on, and there is no markup.
findings.why_costs_money: Shipping is a common marketplace profit line (Etsy and Poshmark keep label margin), and Brandthread currently loses money on it.
findings.fix: Add a small markup (e.g. 25-50c or 5%), or at least pass through the Shippo plan fee.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: +$0.40 x 8k labels = ~$3.2k/mo upside.

findings.title: Return labels on paid-out orders recovered by transfer reversal that can fail
findings.problem: Return labels are bought on Brandthread's Shippo account and recovered by reversing the order's transfer. On a paid-out order, a reversal that fails for insufficient seller balance is only logged as 'owed', which is never collected.
findings.why_costs_money: Brandthread pays return shipping for sellers who withdrew their money.
findings.fix: Require the seller's held or available balance to cover the label before purchase, or charge the seller's card on file.

findings.title: Payout policy (reserve, international hold) is built but disabled and not wired to hold mode
findings.problem: PAYOUT_POLICY_ENFORCED=false, and the doc says the delivery guarantee's PAYOUT_MODE is 'a separate mechanism and not wired into this policy'. International orders get no extra hold even though cross-border fraud and dispute rates are higher.
findings.why_costs_money: International orders carry higher dispute and fraud rates with no extra hold.
findings.fix: Wire holdReleaseDate with extraHoldUntil = payout_release_at and enforce the international hold, or delete the dead config.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small until international volume grows.

findings.title: Docs claim in-stock orders are destination charges paid instantly; code defaults to hold
findings.problem: The money-flow rules table and the escrow.ts header still say 'In-stock orders are paid straight to the seller (destination charge)'. Since PAYOUT_MODE=hold, every in-stock order is a platform charge. cartCheckout.ts also says the seller 'stays the liable party' for tax, which is untrue for platform charges.
findings.why_costs_money: Dev and future engineers make Stripe, tax and legal decisions from stale docs.
findings.fix: Rewrite money-flow.md sections 1-2 and the code headers to describe hold/transfer as the primary path.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect.

findings.title: Payment methods saved off_session on platform customer with no recurring use
findings.problem: Hosted checkout always sets setup_future_usage: 'off_session'. This can trigger extra SCA/3DS friction, and for some wallets and BNPL methods it narrows which payment methods Checkout offers.
findings.why_costs_money: Small conversion loss at checkout.
findings.fix: Use on_session, or only save cards when the buyer opts in (as one-page checkout does with saveCard).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: <1% checkout conversion.

findings.title: USD-only charges for international buyers: FX and international card fees passed to seller
findings.problem: Everything is charged in USD. International cards add 1.5%, plus 1% if converted, to Stripe's fee. In transfer mode the seller bears it without any quote showing it, and international buyers see USD prices plus bank FX markup.
findings.why_costs_money: Lower international conversion, and seller complaints about unexplained fees.
findings.fix: Show the international fee in the seller fee quote. Consider Adaptive Pricing or local currency later.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small at launch (US-focused).

findings.title: Connect state-signing secret falls back to STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
findings.problem: If CONNECT_STATE_SECRET is unset, the HMAC for the unauthenticated /onboard/refresh redirect is keyed with the Stripe secret key. That reuses the most sensitive credential for another purpose, and rotating it invalidates links.
findings.why_costs_money: Security hygiene: a key-reuse finding in audits or Stripe's partner review.
findings.fix: Require a dedicated CONNECT_STATE_SECRET in production.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: n/a (risk).

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Seller cash-out converts ALL Thread Cash (incl. platform rewards) into real Stripe money
findings.problem: cashOutThreadCash checks getBalanceCents (the SUM of every ledger row) instead of only 'live_gift'/'send_received' earnings, then issues a platform-funded stripe.transfers.create 1:1 (RATE_BPS 10_000, FEE_BPS 0 at cashOut.ts:40-41). Daily check-in, streak bonus, referral credit and refund credit in a seller's own wallet are all cashable. Route is not feature-flagged; requirePermission('payouts') passes for every store owner.
findings.why_costs_money: Every reward Brandthread grants becomes withdrawable cash for anyone who connects Stripe; there is no cap, minimum, hold or velocity check, so rewards turn into direct cash outflow.
findings.fix: Compute a cashable balance = live_gift + send_received from verified purchases only (or remove cash-out entirely until legal sign-off); add a feature flag (default off), daily cap, 7-day hold and manual review over a threshold.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Unbounded; at least $10 per new seller (referral) + ~$7/mo per seller check-in streak, and ~$1,500/mo per seller via the send ring (see next finding)

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Farm ring: alt accounts -> 'send' to seller -> cash out = $1,500/month per seller
findings.problem: sendableBalanceCents treats daily_checkin/streak/referral credit as sendable; send requires only mutual follow + 24h account age; seller receive cap is 5000c per rolling 24h (streaks.ts:33). cashOut.ts:3 explicitly documents 'send_received' as cashable. A seller with ~5 alt accounts (each seeded with the $10 referral credit) can move $50/day of platform-funded credit into a cashable seller wallet.
findings.why_costs_money: Converts free platform credit into Stripe transfers out of Brandthread's balance: $50/day x 30 = $1,500/month per seller account, repeatable across any number of seller accounts.
findings.fix: Make send_received NOT cashable (or only cashable when the sender's spent balance came from card-funded sources), block sends to accounts with a Stripe Connect account, and require the sender to have a paid order.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Up to $1,500/mo per abusing seller; 10 abusers = $15k/mo (30% of the $50k target)

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: New sellers get $10 referral Thread Cash on signup, cashable immediately
findings.problem: Seller onboarding calls api.referrals.apply, and applyReferralCode credits the invitee REFERRAL_INVITEE_REWARD_CENTS=1000 with no purchase and no role check. Because seller cash-out uses the whole balance, a new seller who types any invite code can withdraw $10 once Connect is linked.
findings.why_costs_money: Pays $10 cash per seller account created; business model says referral rewards are buyer-only.
findings.fix: Reject /referrals/apply for accounts with accountType seller or a Stripe account; and fix cash-out source filtering.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $10 per seller signup; 500 seller signups = $5,000 one-off plus inviter rewards

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Default payout mode makes the SELLER fund Thread Cash, not Brandthread
findings.problem: PAYOUT_MODE defaults to 'hold' so in-stock orders use chargeModel 'transfer'. recordOrderPaid sets sellerNet = split.sellerNetCents = gross (card amount after Thread Cash) - fee - processing, and applyThreadCashSellerTopup returns early unless chargeModel==='destination'. buyer.ts:718 only blocks 'held'. A $50 item paid with $49.50 Thread Cash leaves the seller ~$0.
findings.why_costs_money: Breaks the core promise 'seller still gets full price'; once threadCashCheckoutDiscount is on, sellers are silently underpaid, leading to churn, disputes and support load.
findings.fix: For 'transfer' orders compute sellerNet on the pre-Thread-Cash gross and post a thread_cash_seller_topup expense, or block Thread Cash for transfer orders. Add an integration test with PAYOUT_MODE=hold.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks enabling checkout credit; if flipped as-is, sellers lose 100% of each Thread Cash amount

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: No self-purchase block: seller can buy own product with Thread Cash or gift card
findings.problem: Neither hosted checkout (buyer.ts, sellerId resolved at :657) nor one-page checkout checks buyerId !== sellerId. With PAYOUT_MODE=immediate (destination) the platform top-up pays the seller the full Thread Cash amount for buying their own item; gift card payout has the same hole.
findings.why_costs_money: Self-dealing turns farmed credits into seller payouts paid from Brandthread's balance.
findings.fix: Reject checkout when buyerId === sellerId or buyer is a team member of the store; flag orders where buyer and seller share device/payment fingerprint.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Equal to farmed balance; blocks safely enabling Thread Cash checkout

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Referral invitee gets $10 on join with no purchase, unlimited per inviter
findings.problem: applyReferralCode credits 1000c to the invitee immediately. REFERRAL_MAX_PAID_PER_INVITER=50 caps only the inviter's reward; invitee credits per code are unlimited. /referrals/apply has no rate limit, no account-age window and no device check (only email canonicalisation at policy.ts:83).
findings.why_costs_money: Every fake account farms $10 that is sendable (and then cashable via a seller) or spendable at checkout once enabled.
findings.fix: Grant the invitee credit only as a discount on their first paid order (min $25), cap invitees per code per day, and require phone verification.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $10 per fake signup; 1,000 fake signups = $10k

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Peer send flag was turned ON by default without the legal sign-off migration 085 required
findings.problem: Migration 085 says threadCashSend stays OFF 'until Dev confirms with a lawyer that peer-to-peer Thread Cash transfer does not trigger money-transmitter / App Store rules'. Migration 088 flips it ON citing only technical hardening. Combined with seller cash-out it is a P2P value-to-cash rail.
findings.why_costs_money: Money-transmitter exposure and App Review risk; it also powers the cash-out farm.
findings.fix: Set threadCashSend false for launch until legal sign-off; at minimum block sends to accounts with Stripe Connect.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Regulatory/rejection risk; enables the $1.5k/mo per-seller leak

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Cost model: up to $7.29/user/month; about $34k/month accrued at 20k MAU
findings.problem: Arithmetic: daily 10c x 30 = $3.00; bonus 100c x (30/7 = 4.29) = $4.29; perfect-streak max = $7.29/user/mo ($87.50/yr). Blended at 20k MAU: 20% streakers x $7.29 = $1.46 + 30% casual (8 claim days, no bonus) x $0.80 = $0.24 -> $1.70/MAU -> $34k/mo accrued. Referrals: if 500 of ~2,000 new users/mo use a code -> $5k invitee + about 50% qualify -> $2.5k inviter. Total about $41.5k/mo of credit issued.
findings.why_costs_money: At 60% redemption this is about $25k/mo of real cash, half the $50k revenue target. Covering it needs $500k GMV/mo at 5% commission.
findings.fix: Before launch, cut the bonus, set expiry 60-90 days, cap per-order redemption, add a monthly budget, and re-model with real retention data.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $25k-$41k/mo at 20k MAU; $146k/mo ceiling if every MAU streaks

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Doc says Thread Cash checkout is 'implemented'; tests cover only destination charges
findings.problem: The todo doc claims the plan is built and covered end to end, but every test uses chargeModel 'destination' while money-flow.md says 'hold'/transfer is now the default. The default path is untested and wrong (see previous finding).
findings.why_costs_money: An operator could flip the flag on the strength of the doc and underpay every seller.
findings.fix: Update the doc to 'NOT safe under PAYOUT_MODE=hold' and add transfer-model tests before sign-off.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Prevents a launch-day payout incident

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Daily 7-minute reward is spoofable by a script in seconds
findings.problem: 'Use' is a client-reported activeSeconds (>=420) plus >=6 heartbeat rows; heartbeats are not time-spaced (each POST increments heartbeat_count, wallet.ts:193) and activeSeconds is taken from the claim body. A script can POST 6 heartbeats then /daily/claim with activeSeconds=420 instantly.
findings.why_costs_money: Bots earn the full reward (and 7-day streak bonus) per account without engaging, multiplying cost by every scripted account.
findings.fix: Server-measure time: require heartbeats >=50s apart (store last_heartbeat_at) and compute active seconds server-side; add App Attest / Play Integrity on claim.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $7.29/mo per scripted account; 1,000 bot accounts = $7.3k/mo

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Device cap is optional and client-supplied: omit deviceId to bypass
findings.problem: The per-device cap only runs `if (award.deviceId)`; deviceId is a random UUID in AsyncStorage the client chooses to send. Omitting it or rotating it defeats maxCheckInsPerDevicePerDay=3 (streaks.ts:35). No server-side device fingerprinting exists.
findings.why_costs_money: Multi-account farming is unbounded by device.
findings.fix: Require a deviceId attested via App Attest/DeviceCheck (iOS) and Play Integrity (Android); reject claims without it.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Multiplies per-account cost by number of accounts per phone

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Referral loyalty points (500 = $5) uncapped and paid on join, not purchase
findings.problem: The inviter earns REFERRAL_JOIN_POINTS=500 ($5 of loyalty discount) for every invitee that joins, regardless of purchase and outside the 50-referral cap.
findings.why_costs_money: Fake signups generate $5 discount each, spendable at any store and funded by sellers (loyalty reduces the seller transfer and the 5% fee basis).
findings.fix: Move the points to the qualifying-order hook and include them in the 50 cap.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $5 per fake invitee charged to sellers + 5% lost commission on the discount

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Referral program is not buyer-only: sellers can invite and be invited
findings.problem: applyReferralCode and qualifyReferralForOrder never check accountType/role; seller onboarding applies codes and sellers can generate codes via GET /referrals/code.
findings.why_costs_money: Contradicts the 'buyers only' business rule and, combined with cash-out, pays sellers cash.
findings.fix: Enforce buyer accountType on both inviter and invitee server-side.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $10-$20 per seller referral pair

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Self-referral only blocked by same Clerk id/email; alt accounts pass
findings.problem: Checks are inviter===invitee and canonical email equality. No device, payment-card fingerprint, IP or shipping-address match.
findings.why_costs_money: Users refer themselves from a second email on the same phone (8 accounts allowed) for $10 + $10 + 500 points.
findings.fix: Compare Stripe card fingerprint and shipping address of the qualifying order with the inviter's, and device id at apply time.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $20+$5 per self-referral

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Buyers can 'pay' sellers in chat with Thread Cash and skip the 5% commission
findings.problem: ChatAttachThreadCash is wired into buyer and seller conversations; the seller history labels send_received as 'Message payment' and cash-out treats it as cashable. This is a payment for goods outside orders.
findings.why_costs_money: Platform-funded credit pays sellers directly with no order, no 5% commission, and no buyer protection.
findings.fix: Remove the attach button from buyer-seller conversations, or route chat payments through a real order.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: 100% of the amount sent plus lost 5% commission

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Live gifts (when flag on) make platform rewards cashable with no follow gate
findings.problem: sendLiveGift moves the viewer's reward balance (checkin/referral) to the host as 'live_gift'. There is no account-age check (unlike send), no mutual-follow check, and the host receive cap only counts live_gift, so it stacks with the separate $50/day send_received cap. Currently gated OFF by 'live_tips'.
findings.why_costs_money: When turned on, any alt account can gift its $10 referral credit to a seller's live within minutes of signup.
findings.fix: Keep live_tips off for launch; when on, only allow gifting purchased value and apply minAccountAgeHoursForSend and a combined receive cap.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Another $50/day per seller host when enabled

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Buyer-facing copy says Thread Cash can't be cashed out; code lets it be cashed out
findings.problem: UI and route header state 'Thread Cash is not money: it can't be withdrawn, cashed out, or sent as cash' while the same wallet (shared by buyers and sellers, thread-cash.tsx:154) is cashed out at 1:1 via /cash-out.
findings.why_costs_money: Misleading terms create consumer-protection and App Review exposure, and weaken the legal position that Thread Cash is a non-cash reward.
findings.fix: Separate buyer reward credit and seller earnings into two ledgers/balances and keep the copy true.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Legal/review risk; enables misclassification of liabilities

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Buyer rewards and seller earnings share ONE balance per Clerk user
findings.problem: getBalanceCents sums all thread_cash_entries for the user id; there is no separate seller-earnings bucket, so expiry, spend, send and cash-out logic all act on mixed funds.
findings.why_costs_money: Root cause of reward-to-cash leakage and makes liability accounting impossible.
findings.fix: Split into thread_cash_entries (rewards, non-cashable) and seller_earnings (cashable), or add a 'cashable' column enforced in every debit.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Underlies the P0 leaks above

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Thread Cash is not booked as a liability anywhere in the money ledger
findings.problem: ledger.ts states Thread Cash is tracked only as SUM(thread_cash_entries), not as a balance-sheet liability; the sign-off item 'confirm accounting treatment' is still open. Awards post nothing to the ledger; only top-ups and cash-outs do.
findings.why_costs_money: Finance can't see outstanding obligations (potentially tens of thousands/month accrued) and books will understate liabilities at launch.
findings.fix: Post thread_cash_liability on every award/expiry/spend (debit marketing expense, credit liability) and add a daily outstanding-balance report.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$34k/mo accrued liability at 20k MAU not visible (see cost model)

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: No global budget cap or spend kill switch on platform-funded credits
findings.problem: No monthly/daily program budget, no per-user lifetime cap, no circuit breaker on awards, referral credits, top-ups or cash-outs (grep 'budget' in lib/threadCash and lib/referrals: no hits).
findings.why_costs_money: A viral spike or bot wave grows cost with no ceiling.
findings.fix: Add a thread_cash_budget table with monthly cap; awards and top-ups refuse (or reduce to 0) once exceeded; alert at 80%.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Caps worst-case exposure (e.g. hold to $5k/mo)

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: The 'threadCash' kill switch is client-only; earn endpoints ignore it
findings.problem: Only the mobile tracker reads useFeatureFlag('threadCash'). /check-in, /daily/heartbeat, /daily/claim, and referral credits never call isFeatureEnabled('threadCash'), so flipping the flag off does not stop scripts from earning.
findings.why_costs_money: There is no working server-side off switch during an abuse incident.
findings.fix: Check isFeatureEnabled('threadCash') in every earn path (and referral credit) and fail closed.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Lets ops stop a bleed in minutes instead of a deploy

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Deprecated /check-in still pays without the 7-minute activity gate
findings.problem: POST /api/thread-cash/check-in (kept for older clients) calls awardDailyCheckInOnce, which has no heartbeat or activeSeconds requirement, so one tap/request earns the daily reward and the streak bonus.
findings.why_costs_money: Makes the '7 minutes of use' rule meaningless; trivial for scripts.
findings.fix: Remove /check-in before launch (no older clients exist pre-launch) or return 410.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Same as full reward cost for every scripted account

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Thread Cash never expires by default: liability grows forever
findings.problem: expiryDays defaults to null ('never'); the expiry job exists (jobs/threadCashExpiry.ts) but does nothing without a value.
findings.why_costs_money: No breakage: every cent ever awarded stays a future cost, and dormant farm balances never lapse.
findings.fix: Set expiry_days to 60-90 before launch (rules must be stated in the app at award time).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Breakage of 30-50% of awarded credit, roughly $10-17k/mo at 20k MAU

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: No per-order cap: Thread Cash can pay all but $0.50 of an order
findings.problem: maxRedemptionPerOrderCents defaults to null, so maxRedeemableCents leaves only the 50c Stripe minimum. docs/review-readiness/reviewer-access.md:97 claims it is 'a capped checkout discount'.
findings.why_costs_money: Lets farmed balances buy goods almost free, maximizing platform top-up per order; doc misleads reviewers/ops.
findings.fix: Set max_redemption_per_order_cents (e.g. $5 or 20% of merchandise) and require a minimum card spend.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Limits per-order platform cost to a known amount

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Refund double-dip if top-up reversal fails (only logged, never retried)
findings.problem: refundThreadCashSpend credits the buyer back first; if createReversal throws (seller balance empty, account closed), it logs 'needs review' and moves on. Buyer gets credit back AND the seller keeps the platform top-up. No sweep job retries reversals.
findings.why_costs_money: Platform pays twice for one refunded order.
findings.fix: Record a pending reversal row and retry in moneySweep; debit future seller payouts if reversal is impossible.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Each failure costs the full Thread Cash amount

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Cash-out has no minimum, hold period, daily limit or Stripe status check
findings.problem: Any amount >= 1c is cashed out instantly as a separate Stripe transfer; only stripeAccountId presence is checked (not stripeAccountStatus 'active'). Credits received minutes ago are immediately withdrawable.
findings.why_costs_money: Fraud gets cashed out before review; many tiny transfers add cost and noise.
findings.fix: Minimum $10, 7-day maturity on credits, daily cap, require active Connect status.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Reduces fraud loss and ops cost

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Earning is live while spending is OFF, so a liability builds up to land at flag-flip
findings.problem: threadCash (earn) ships ON; threadCashCheckoutDiscount ships OFF. Buyers accumulate never-expiring balances they can't use at checkout (they can only send them, which feeds the cash-out leak). When checkout is enabled, months of backlog become spendable at once.
findings.why_costs_money: Sudden cash outflow at the flag flip plus a weak buyer value prop at launch (credit with nowhere to spend).
findings.fix: Either launch both together with caps, or don't accrue (or show 'coming soon' without accruing) until checkout spend is safe.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Backlog of ~$34k per month of delay at 20k MAU

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Loyalty points are platform-wide but seller-funded: sellers pay for rewards earned elsewhere
findings.problem: Points are earned on any store's order (1pt/$1, webhooks.ts:1396), on signup (100, auth.ts:163) and on referral (500), and redeemed at any store as a discount that reduces that seller's transfer and the fee basis ('correct for loyalty points (seller-funded rewards)').
findings.why_costs_money: Seller B pays for points that Brandthread gave away or that seller A generated, and Brandthread also loses 5% on the discounted amount. Sellers will see unexplained payout cuts.
findings.fix: Make loyalty platform-funded (top-up like Thread Cash) or per-store, or remove it and fold it into Thread Cash.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~1% of GMV shifted to sellers plus 5% of that lost in commission; seller churn risk

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Gift card expiry as short as 1 month conflicts with CARD Act 5-year minimum
findings.problem: saveGiftCardSettings allows expiryMonths 1-120. US federal CARD Act/Reg E requires gift cards not expire within 5 years of issue/load, and several states (e.g. CA) ban expiry.
findings.why_costs_money: Regulatory fines and chargebacks; Brandthread holds the funds (gift_card_liability) so it is the exposed party.
findings.fix: Minimum 60 months for purchased cards (or no expiry); allow shorter only for seller-issued promotional cards with clear disclosure.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Legal exposure; blocks responsible launch of gift cards

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Seller can void a customer-PURCHASED gift card; Brandthread keeps the money
findings.problem: voidCard zeroes any card of the seller including source='purchase'; no refund of the purchaser's payment and no liability release posting.
findings.why_costs_money: Purchasers file chargebacks (platform pays + $15 dispute fee); ledger liability is left unreconciled.
findings.fix: Only allow voiding seller_issued cards; purchased cards may only be voided with an automatic refund of the remaining balance.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Card value + $15 per dispute

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Gift cards paid with stolen cards: code released instantly, platform eats chargeback
findings.problem: Purchase is a PaymentIntent on Brandthread's balance up to $1,000 per card with no velocity limit, no 3DS requirement, no Radar review hold; the code is emailed and returned the moment payment succeeds and can be redeemed immediately, triggering a seller payout.
findings.why_costs_money: Gift cards are the top carding target; a chargeback hits Brandthread after the seller was paid.
findings.fix: Require 3DS, cap per-buyer daily gift card volume (e.g. $200), hold code delivery 24h for new accounts, and enable Radar rules for gift cards.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Full card value + $15 fee per fraud; typical carding bursts are $5-20k

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: 8 accounts per device allowed; 4 can earn daily Thread Cash on one phone
findings.problem: MAX_ACCOUNTS = 8 per device with Clerk multi-session; device cap counts OTHER buyers >= 3 so 4 accounts per device per day still earn, plus 100 signup loyalty points each.
findings.why_costs_money: One user can quadruple daily rewards and referral credits by switching accounts.
findings.fix: Set maxCheckInsPerDevicePerDay to 0 (one earning account per device) and only grant rewards to the first account seen on a device.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Up to 4x reward cost for power users (~$22/mo extra per gaming user)

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Inviter $10 not clawed back when the qualifying order is refunded
findings.problem: qualifyReferralForOrder pays on the paid webhook; refunds.ts reverses loyalty and Thread Cash spend but nothing reverses the 'referral' inviter entry. Buy $10, get $10, refund the order.
findings.why_costs_money: Free $10 per alt account loop at the cost of only processing fees.
findings.fix: Delay inviter credit until the order is delivered + return window, or post a negative referral entry on full refund.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $10 per abuse loop; ~$1k/mo at modest abuse

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Existing accounts can claim the 'new customer' $10 any time
findings.problem: The only newness check is 'no orders yet'. A dormant account months old can apply a code and get $10; there is no apply window after signup.
findings.why_costs_money: Lets existing users and bulk-made dormant accounts claim welcome credit.
findings.fix: Allow apply only within 7 days of users.createdAt.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $10 per dormant account

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: No admin UI/API to freeze a wallet or change Thread Cash config
findings.problem: Freeze columns exist (migration 088) and config is a DB row, but no route writes thread_cash_streaks.frozen or thread_cash_config (grep 'frozen' in routes: none). Changing caps needs raw SQL in production.
findings.why_costs_money: Slow response to fraud; operators may avoid tightening caps.
findings.fix: Add admin endpoints (requireModerator) to freeze/unfreeze wallets, edit config, and view top earners/senders.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Shortens fraud windows; hard to quantify

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Destination-mode Thread Cash order may fail: application fee exceeds the discounted charge
findings.problem: application_fee_amount is computed on the full pre-Thread-Cash price while the Stripe charge can be reduced to 50c. Stripe rejects an application fee larger than the charge, so large Thread Cash orders under PAYOUT_MODE=immediate likely fail to pay (needs Stripe test confirmation).
findings.why_costs_money: Failed checkouts lose the sale and the buyer's trust.
findings.fix: Require card portion >= application fee (like the gift card feeFloorCents in giftCards/checkout.ts:71).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Lost orders when used; small until flag is on

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Partial refunds: Thread Cash not returned and seller top-up not reversed
findings.problem: Thread Cash restoration and top-up reversal run only when fullyRefunded. On a partial refund the seller keeps the full platform top-up for refunded items, and the buyer loses their pro-rata Thread Cash.
findings.why_costs_money: Platform pays the seller for goods that were refunded; buyers complain about lost credit.
findings.fix: Pro-rate: reverse top-up and return Thread Cash proportionally to the refunded merchandise.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Proportional to partial-refund volume on Thread Cash orders

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Streak bonus is 10x the daily reward and makes up 59% of program cost
findings.problem: Daily 10c, bonus 100c every 7th consecutive day (no cap). Per perfect week 70c + 100c = 170c; the bonus is 100/170 = 59% of cost and is easiest for bots (scripted daily claims) to hit.
findings.why_costs_money: Cost is concentrated in automated or habitual claimers, not in buyers who purchase.
findings.fix: Tie the streak bonus to a purchase or engagement action (e.g. bonus only spendable on next order with a min spend), or lower to 30c.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Cutting the bonus to 30c lowers the max from $7.29 to $4.29/user/mo (-41%)

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Loyalty redemption has no per-order cap and no flag
findings.problem: Discount only needs to be below the order total by 1 cent; redemption is not feature-flagged. A buyer with farmed signup/referral points can take almost the whole item from one seller.
findings.why_costs_money: Concentrates loss on single sellers; platform fee goes to near 0 on those orders.
findings.fix: Cap loyalty at e.g. 10% of merchandise and minimum 500 points; add a flag.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Bounded by points farmed; $5 per fake referral

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Gift card float/breakage has no escheat or stored-value compliance handling
findings.problem: Brandthread holds gift card money as gift_card_liability with no unclaimed-property (escheat) process, no handling when a seller closes their store, and no reporting.
findings.why_costs_money: State unclaimed-property audits and stored-value licensing questions; stranded balances when sellers churn.
findings.fix: Add a policy: on store closure, refund remaining balances; get legal advice on escheat; add a liability report.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Compliance exposure grows with volume

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: IAP-bought boosts can't be refunded on admin rejection
findings.problem: refundPromotionPayment refunds only via Stripe checkoutSessionId; IAP purchases (iap-promotions.ts, gated by IAP_PROMOTIONS_ENABLED) have none, so 'rejection refunds in full' returns nothing_to_refund and the seller is charged for a rejected boost.
findings.why_costs_money: Seller complaints and Apple refund requests; possible review issue.
findings.fix: For IAP-sourced boosts, issue a credit for a future boost or direct the seller to Apple refund with clear copy.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Value of rejected IAP boosts ($5-$500 each)

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: iap-rails doc misses that reward Thread Cash is cashable
findings.problem: The doc marks Thread Cash PASS and calls gift cashability a future risk, but today daily check-in/referral credit is cashable through /cash-out and the send flow. App Review could see 'earn cash for time in app' as an incentive mechanic.
findings.why_costs_money: A wrong review-readiness verdict before an App Store-only launch.
findings.fix: Update the doc after fixing cash-out source filtering; keep reward credit non-cashable.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Rejection risk at launch

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Guests/demo can't earn (verified), but signed-in sellers also earn buyer rewards
findings.problem: router.use(requireAuth) blocks guests and demo fixtures are client-only. However the earn endpoints don't check role, so seller accounts (and team members acting as the owner via teamContext) can call /daily/claim directly and accrue cashable rewards.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers farm buyer rewards into cashable balance.
findings.fix: Restrict earn endpoints to buyer accounts and to the actor (not the rewritten owner id).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$7/mo per seller account plus multi-account multiples

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Cash-out idempotency lookup is not scoped to the seller
findings.problem: The existing-entry lookup filters only by idempotencyKey (globally unique) without buyerId, so a key that collides with another user's entry returns that user's transfer id as a 'success' response.
findings.why_costs_money: Confusing false-success responses and info leak; no direct loss.
findings.fix: Add eq(threadCashEntries.buyerId, sellerId) to the lookup and namespace keys per seller.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Negligible direct $

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Timezone is client-chosen per request, which allows an extra day's claim
findings.problem: normalizeTimezone accepts any zone each call; switching between UTC-12 and UTC+14 opens a ~26h window, so a user can claim two local dates back to back. Comment at :140 acknowledges the shift.
findings.why_costs_money: Minor extra claims and streak gaming.
findings.fix: Persist the timezone on the first claim and allow changes at most once per week.

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Signup grants 100 loyalty points to every account (farmable via 8 accounts/device)
findings.problem: Every new Clerk user gets 100 points ($1) at /auth/sync with no verification.
findings.why_costs_money: Small, but farmable at scale and funded by whichever seller is redeemed against.
findings.fix: Grant signup points on first paid order instead.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $1 per account; ~$2k at 2k signups/mo

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Loyalty earn uses order total including tax and shipping
findings.problem: points = floor(order.totalCents / 100) uses the Stripe total including tax and shipping, while the docs say '1 point per $1 spent'.
findings.why_costs_money: Over-awards about 10-15% vs merchandise-based earning, funded by sellers.
findings.fix: Base points on merchandise subtotal minus discounts.

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Giveaway entries come from follows: bot follows inflate entries, no fraud checks
findings.problem: Entries are derived from follows/comments; only blocked accounts and the sponsor are excluded. Multi-accounts (8/device) and fresh accounts can enter, so real buyers lose to farms.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers' prize spend goes to fake accounts, so sellers see no return and churn from the feature.
findings.fix: Exclude accounts younger than 7 days or without a verified email/phone, and dedupe by device.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect; seller retention

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Seller discount codes shrink the 5% commission base
findings.problem: discountCodeAmountCents feeds combinedDiscountCents, which reduces merchandiseCents for the platform fee. Seller-funded promos therefore also cut Brandthread's commission (expected), with no floor.
findings.why_costs_money: A seller running a 50% off code halves platform revenue on those orders; 100%-off codes (to 1 cent) yield ~0 fee while the platform still carries risk.
findings.fix: Set a minimum platform fee per order (e.g. $0.50) or compute the fee on list price for codes over X%.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~5% x promo volume

findings.area_label: Thread Cash, referrals, gift cards & incentive abuse
findings.title: Buyer wallet history labels cash_out/live_gift_sent as 'Adjustment'
findings.problem: historyLabel has no case for live_gift, live_gift_sent or cash_out, so they render as 'Adjustment' in the shared buyer/seller wallet.
findings.why_costs_money: Confusing statements lead to support tickets and erode trust in rewards.
findings.fix: Add labels for all ledger sources (share one map with thread-cash-history.tsx).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Minor support cost

findings.title: Unlimited free logo generation via /api/onboarding-sample/generate
findings.problem: logoRouter, including its paid POST /generate handler, is also mounted at /onboarding-sample with only requireAuth: no requirePlan, no seller/onboarding check and no credit rule, because the credit regex only matches /logo/... So POST /api/onboarding-sample/generate gives any signed-in account, buyers included, unlimited gpt-image-1 high-quality logos. Each call runs up to 2 generations plus 2 QA calls. The only brake is an in-memory 5/min per-process Map, and the path is outside the 'expensive' rate-limit regex.
findings.why_costs_money: At $0.17-0.34 per call, 5/min comes to 7,200 calls a day per account per instance, about $1.2k-2.4k a day. Signing up is free.
findings.fix: Mount only the /logo handler at /onboarding-sample (a separate router with just POST /logo), or add requirePlan plus a catalogue rule for /onboarding-sample/generate. Add 'onboarding-sample' to EXPENSIVE_PATH.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $36k-73k/mo worst case from one abusive free account (7,200/day x $0.17-0.34 x 30)

findings.title: Credit prices are 5-20x below real gpt-image-1 cost
findings.problem: The catalogue assumes 1 credit = about $0.01, so bg_remove = 2 credits ($0.02), logo/mockup = 5, photoshoot = 8. Every tool actually calls gpt-image-1 at quality 'high' (about $0.167 output per 1024px image, plus input-image tokens on edits). generateWithVisualQa can regenerate once, so one call costs $0.19-0.39.
findings.why_costs_money: Growth ($79) grants 4,000 credits, which buys 2,000 background removals costing $380-780 in provider fees. Every credit tool loses money at list price, and packs ($5.99 for 500 credits, before Apple's 15-30% cut) lose more.
findings.fix: Re-price credits from measured cost: bg_remove 20-40, logo/mockup 20-35, photoshoot 25-40, mockup-to-model per reference. Or switch bg removal and drafts to quality 'low'/'medium' and price from ai_usage_events.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: At 300 Growth sellers using half their allowance: about 300 x 2,000cr / 2 x $0.10 = ~$30k/mo provider cost against $23.7k revenue

findings.title: Mockup-to-Model and Outfit Swap charge 8 credits for up to 10 image generations
findings.problem: /photography/mockup-to-model runs one generateWithVisualQa (up to 2 gpt-image-1 high edits plus 2 QA calls) for each of up to 5 reference images. /outfit-swap does the same for up to 4 garments. Both are billed a flat 8 credits, and partial success returns 200, so nothing is refunded.
findings.why_costs_money: Worst case per call is 10 edits, about $1.90, billed at $0.08. A Pro seller (400 'generations' a day ceiling) can burn about $760 a day.
findings.fix: Charge per reference or garment (for example 30 credits each), or debit after the run using the number of successful outputs. Count references, not requests, toward the Pro daily ceiling.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $1.9 of cost per $0.08 charge; one heavy Pro user is about $20k/mo

findings.title: Retry endpoints bypass the credit gate entirely
findings.problem: The credit rule /^\/photography\/(mockup-to-model|outfit-swap)$/ does not match /mockup-to-model/retry or /outfit-swap/retry. Both run a full generateWithVisualQa (up to 2 high-quality edits plus QA) with no debit. The mobile app calls retryOutfitSwap.
findings.why_costs_money: A Growth or Pro seller can loop the retry endpoint for free high-quality generations, about $0.39 each, limited only by 30/min.
findings.fix: Extend the regex to (mockup-to-model|outfit-swap)(\/retry)? with a per-image cost, and add a regression test listing every POST route under the growth-gated mounts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: 30/min x $0.39 is up to $16k/day per account; realistic abuse is $1-5k/mo

findings.title: Trailing slash or uppercase path skips the credit debit
findings.problem: findToolRule tests req.path against case-sensitive regexes anchored with $. Express 5 routers default to caseSensitive:false and strict:false, so POST /api/photography/generate/ or /api/PHOTOGRAPHY/generate still reaches the handler but matches no rule: no debit, no Pro ceiling, no global cap. The EXPENSIVE_PATH rate-limit regex is also case-sensitive, so the request falls back to the 120/min mutation policy. (Found by reading the code; could not run it because node_modules is not installed.)
findings.why_costs_money: A paying Growth or Pro account gets unlimited free image generation, and the global emergency cap never sees it.
findings.fix: Normalise in the gate: path = req.path.toLowerCase().replace(/\/+$/, ''). Or create routers with { strict: true, caseSensitive: true }. Better still, debit inside each route via a helper instead of matching paths.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Unbounded: about 120 req/min x $0.2-1.9 per paying abuser

findings.title: Trials and past_due subscriptions get full AI allowance (Pro unlimited) from day one
findings.problem: getEffectiveEntitlement treats 'trial', 'trialing' and 'past_due' as active. resolvePlan therefore returns growth or pro, and lockAccount grants the full 4,000 credits (Growth) or unlimited use (Pro, 400 generations a day) as soon as the 5-day trial starts. A seller can burn it all and cancel before the first charge.
findings.why_costs_money: One Pro trial is about 2,000 generations; at mockup-to-model's $1.90 worst case that is up to $3.9k per trial. Growth is 4,000 credits, about $400-950 of provider cost. Card-required trials don't stop this with prepaid or virtual cards.
findings.fix: Grant a small trial allowance (for example 100 credits, Pro capped at 20 a day) and the full monthly grant only on the first paid invoice. Exclude past_due from AI tools after a 3-day grace period.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: 100 trial abusers/mo x ~$500 = $50k/mo; even 10 is $5k

findings.title: /store/ai/* has no input size limit and no plan gate, so one gpt-4.1 call can cost $1-2
findings.problem: /store/ai/generate and /from-social JSON.stringify the client 'answers' object straight into a gpt-4.1 prompt. app.ts allows 10MB bodies on /api/store/ai, which is roughly 1M tokens of context. These routes are 'text' (free) on every plan and only need sign-in. Buyers can call them too. Nothing checks for a seller.
findings.why_costs_money: About 900k input tokens x $2/M is about $1.80 per call. The shared 500/day text ceiling allows about $900 a day from one free account.
findings.fix: Validate answers with a zod schema (whitelisted keys, each string <= 500 chars, total <= 4KB). Lower the body limit to 64KB except for the image routes, and require a seller account.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Up to $27k/mo per abusive free account; normal use is $0.03/call

findings.title: Support chat sits before the AI gate, so it has no daily ceiling
findings.problem: /support-chat is mounted above router.use(aiCreditsGate), and support-chat has no AI_TOOL_RULES entry anyway, so the 500/day text ceiling never applies. The only brake is the 30/min 'expensive' policy. Each call sends up to 12 x 3,000 chars plus the system prompt to gpt-5.4-mini with up to 800 output tokens.
findings.why_costs_money: 30/min x 1,440 is 43,200 calls a day per account, at about $0.01 each, so about $500 a day from one free buyer account. It also does not count toward the global AI spend cap or alerts.
findings.fix: Add a text rule for /support-chat/message and move the mount below the gate (or call allowTextRequest in the route). Cap support chat at about 50 messages per user per day.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Up to ~$15k/mo per abusive account (assumes gpt-5.4-mini at $0.75/$4.50 per M)

findings.title: Hardcoded gpt-image-1 retires Oct 23, 2026 per an in-repo comment (pre-launch)
findings.problem: aiImageProviders/config.ts says 'gpt-image-1 is retired Oct 23, 2026' and adds getOpenAiImageModel() (OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL, default gpt-image-2.5-flare). Nothing imports aiImageProviders. The shared client every route uses still sends model: 'gpt-image-1'.
findings.why_costs_money: If the date is right, every paid AI image feature (the Growth/Pro selling point and the credit packs) stops working one week before the Oct 31 launch. The successor model also needs new pricing in aiPricing.ts and in the credit catalogue.
findings.fix: Confirm the date on OpenAI's deprecations page. Make the shared client read OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL, benchmark the successor's cost, and re-price credits before Oct 23.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks all AI-tool revenue (Growth upsell, packs) if the retirement date holds

findings.title: Starter is sold 1,000 credits/mo and packs, but every credit tool needs Growth
findings.problem: Every 'credits' rule points at /logo, /mockup, /photography, /bg-removal, /lifestyle or /techpack, and all of those are mounted behind requirePlan('growth'). Starter still gets monthlyAllowance 1000 and packsEligible true, and the paywall shows '1,000 AI credits per month'. Starter credits and any purchased pack can never be spent. The gate debits, requirePlan returns 403, and the gate refunds.
findings.why_costs_money: Selling consumable packs that cannot be used invites refunds, chargebacks and App Store 3.1.1/5.6 complaints, and the advertised perk is false.
findings.fix: Either open bg-removal and mockup to Starter (credits become the limiter and the upgrade path) or set Starter's allowance to 0 with packsEligible false and change the copy. Opening them is the better monetisation lever.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks pack revenue from Starter and creates refund and review risk on every Starter sale

findings.title: Worst-case monthly AI and third-party exposure summary
findings.problem: One abusive FREE account (email signup) today: onboarding-sample logos about $36-73k, store-ai at 500 text calls a day with 1M-token prompts about $27k, support chat about $15k, places per IP about $6k, which is roughly $85k/mo, more than the $50k revenue target. 1,000 normal no-plan sellers: chat about 30 msgs ($0.18), helpers ($0.04), store AI ($0.09), onboarding logo ($0.25, once), support ($0.03), places ($0.05), so about $0.5-0.65 each, or $500-650/mo. If those 1,000 are in Growth trials using about 30 images each: +$5-11k/mo.
findings.why_costs_money: With these holes, a single bad actor can wipe out a month of revenue.
findings.fix: Fix the P0s first (onboarding-sample route, retry/slash bypass, support-chat ceiling, store-ai input cap, trial grants, re-pricing), then add dollar-based global caps and an OpenAI project budget.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Worst case ~$85k/mo from one free account; ~$0.6k/mo for 1k normal free sellers (assumes gpt-5.4-mini $0.75/$4.50 per M, gpt-image-1 high $0.167/img)

findings.title: AI chat accepts an unbounded client brandMemory/context, inflating prompt tokens
findings.problem: brandMemory (Record<string,string>) and context.* (productName, customerName, ...) come from the request body and are interpolated into the system prompt with no size limit. Messages are capped at 40 x 4,000 chars, but the global JSON limit is 45MB. The snapshot and help docs add several thousand tokens on every turn.
findings.why_costs_money: Up to the model context (hundreds of thousands of tokens) per call, at about $0.30 each with gpt-5.4-mini. The 500/day ceiling allows about $150 a day per free account.
findings.fix: Load brandMemory server-side from the DB (it is derivable through /brand-memory/rebuild). Whitelist context keys and truncate to 200 chars, and cap the total system prompt at about 6k tokens.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Up to ~$4.5k/mo per abusive account

findings.title: Any signed-in account, buyers included, can use the free text AI tools
findings.problem: /ai/chat, /ai/chat/stream, /ai/brand-memory/rebuild, /store/ai/* and /ai-helpers/* only require auth plus teamContext. No seller account type or plan is checked, and text is free on every plan with a 500/day ceiling.
findings.why_costs_money: Brandthread pays for AI usage by accounts that will never pay. It also gives away a feature that could drive Starter and Growth upgrades.
findings.fix: Require accountType = seller. Give no-plan sellers a small daily text quota (for example 20/day) and show 'Upgrade for more'.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Normal free use is ~$0.3-0.6/seller/mo; the cap removes the abuse tail of ~$5-27k/mo per bad actor

findings.title: Spend cap and alerts only see credit tools, not text, captions or support
findings.problem: ai_spend_daily (global scope) only grows when debitCredits runs. Free text tools, /support-chat, /onboarding-sample/*, /store/ai, whisper captions and the photography retry routes never add to it, so AI_GLOBAL_DAILY_CREDIT_CAP and the 50/80/100% alerts never fire for the biggest exposures. Alerts also need AI_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL or AI_ALERT_EMAIL to be set.
findings.why_costs_money: Runaway spend through the uncovered routes is invisible until the OpenAI invoice arrives.
findings.fix: Build the global cap and alerts from ai_usage_events cost_micros (dollars) instead of credits, and set an OpenAI or Replit project hard budget limit. Make the alert env vars mandatory in production.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Turns a multi-thousand-dollar incident into a capped one

findings.title: The AI usage meter misses several providers and most models
findings.problem: Only openai.chat.completions.create, images.generate and images.edit on the shared client are metered, and streaming calls are skipped (client.ts:63), so /ai/chat/stream goes unrecorded. store-ai.ts builds its own OpenAI client, so it is unmetered. Whisper audio.transcriptions is unmetered. The price table has no gpt-5.4-mini (chat, agent, helpers, support) and no gpt-5 (store AI), so those rows record cost 0 with priced=false. Image input tokens are priced at the $5 text rate instead of $10.
findings.why_costs_money: The admin AI spend dashboard under-reports most text spend, so pricing decisions are made blind.
findings.fix: Wrap audio.transcriptions, request stream_options.include_usage, reuse the shared client in store-ai, and add current prices for gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5 and gpt-image-*.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect: enables the re-pricing fixes above

findings.title: Pro 'Unlimited AI': 400 gens/day and a fair-use queue that never stops anything
findings.problem: Pro has no balance. The hidden ceiling is 400 requests a day (not images). Past 10,000 credits-worth a month, jobs go to a 2-slot FIFO queue, but a waiter that outlasts 10 minutes 'runs anyway', so the queue only adds delay.
findings.why_costs_money: 400 a day x 30 is 12,000 requests a month. At $0.2-1.9 each, that is $2.4k-23k of cost against $199 of revenue.
findings.fix: Give Pro a real monthly allowance (for example 15,000 credits) with 'unlimited' text only, or a hard fair-use stop with an upsell to packs. Count images, not requests.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: One power user can cost $2-20k/mo; at 50 Pro sellers that is real money

findings.title: AI text and image chat refunds on 4xx let abusers make paid generations free
findings.problem: The gate refunds any response with status >= 400. Responses that come after the provider has already been paid include ImageQualityError 422 (2 generations plus 2 QA calls already spent), AI_OUTPUT_BLOCKED 422 from output moderation, and 502 when QA is unavailable.
findings.why_costs_money: Prompts that reliably fail QA or moderation burn about $0.39 per attempt at zero credit cost to the user, and output moderation becomes a free retry loop for policy-violating prompts.
findings.fix: Charge a partial fee (for example 50%) when the provider ran, or count failed attempts against a per-day failure cap (for example 20) after which the tool locks.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $0.39 per failed attempt; a few hundred dollars a month at modest abuse

findings.title: Google Places autocomplete is unauthenticated, has no session token and no cache
findings.problem: GET /api/places/search is public and calls Places Autocomplete (New) once per keystroke query whenever GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY is set. There is no sessionToken (so every request is billed rather than per session), no server cache, and the only limit is public-read 240 per 5 min per IP.
findings.why_costs_money: At about $2.83/1k requests, a scripted IP can cost about $195 a day, and rotating IPs is unbounded. Normal typing also bills 5-10 requests per place tag.
findings.fix: Require auth, pass a sessionToken (shared with the follow-up Details call), cache q+bias for 24h in Redis, debounce to 3+ chars, and set a Google Cloud quota cap.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$6k/mo per abusive IP; ~$50-300/mo normal at launch scale

findings.title: Background removal uses gpt-image-1 high instead of a cheap segmentation model
findings.problem: /bg-removal/remove runs an image edit with background:'transparent' at quality high and no size, so OpenAI may pick 'auto' (up to 1536px), plus a gpt-4o-mini QA pass and possibly a second generation. The output is a regenerated image, not a mask cutout.
findings.why_costs_money: $0.19-0.39 per cutout, against about $0.01-0.05 for dedicated APIs (remove.bg, Photoroom, fal birefnet) or near zero self-hosted. This is the most-used tool for product photos.
findings.fix: Use a segmentation model for /remove, keep gpt-image only for /replace, and set size explicitly.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: At 20k removals/mo: ~$5k with gpt-image-1 vs <$500 with a segmentation API

findings.title: Every image tool hardcodes quality 'high' with no draft or preview tier
findings.problem: generateImageBuffer and editImages default to quality:'high' and no route passes anything lower, including iterative design drafts (design-text-to-design refine/variation) and 4-up sketch variations.
findings.why_costs_money: High costs about $0.167 per 1024px image versus about $0.042 for medium and $0.011 for low, so drafts cost 4-15x more than they need to.
findings.fix: Generate drafts or variations at low/medium and offer 'Upscale to HD' as a separate higher-credit action (also an upsell surface).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~60-70% cut of image spend; several $k/mo at scale

findings.title: Sketch-to-design fires 4 parallel generations and discards them all if one fails
findings.problem: generateN uses Promise.all over 4 /mockup/generate calls (20 credits, $0.7-1.4 of provider cost). /mockup has an in-memory limit of 5 per minute, so a second attempt inside a minute gets 429s on some calls. Promise.all then rejects and the successful, already-charged images are thrown away.
findings.why_costs_money: Users pay credits and Brandthread pays OpenAI for images the user never sees, which drives retries (more cost) and churn.
findings.fix: Use Promise.allSettled, show partial results, refund only the failed ones, and send a single n=4 request instead.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Roughly 10-25% of design-studio image spend wasted

findings.title: Brand screen makes 3 logos per tap, shows no cost, no upsell without a plan
findings.problem: handleGenerateLogo fires 3 parallel /api/logo/generate calls (15 credits, about $0.5-1.0) on every tap. Non-Growth sellers get 403 PLAN_REQUIRED on all three and see only 'Generation failed'.
findings.why_costs_money: This misses the clearest Starter-to-Growth upsell moment and spends 3x per tap without telling the user.
findings.fix: Show '15 credits' on the button. Detect PLAN_REQUIRED via getEntitlementRejection and open /plans?highlight=growth.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Upsell conversion: even 2% of 1k Starter sellers upgrading is about $1k MRR

findings.title: Most AI tool screens show no credit cost and no upgrade path on 402/403
findings.problem: Only design-mockup-to-model and design-ai-photoshoot render AiCreditsChip/AiToolButtons (grep 'credit' finds 0 hits in the other screens). ai-studio lists 5 tools with no Growth lock badge or cost. design-bg-removal uses raw fetch(), which bypasses api.ts's surfaceAiCreditsError, so a 402 shows 'Not enough AI credits' with no link to buy, and a 403 shows 'Plan required' text with no button.
findings.why_costs_money: Pack sales and plan upgrades are lost exactly when intent is highest.
findings.fix: Add AiCreditsChip and per-action cost labels to every AI screen, route design-bg-removal through api.bgRemoval, and add a shared PLAN_REQUIRED handler that opens /plans.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Credit packs plus upgrades: an estimated $1-3k/mo at target scale

findings.title: Credit packs are loss-making after Apple's cut
findings.problem: Packs are $5.99/500, $14.99/1,500 and $44.99/5,000 credits, about 1.2c per credit, and native purchases go through RevenueCat (Apple/Google keep 15-30%). Real provider cost is about 4-20c per credit-equivalent (see the re-pricing finding), so a 500-credit pack spent on bg removal costs about $47-97 against about $4.20-5.10 of net revenue.
findings.why_costs_money: Each pack sold increases losses.
findings.fix: After re-pricing credits from measured cost, re-derive pack prices with at least 60% gross margin after store fees.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Each pack loses ~$40-90 at current pricing

findings.title: Pack credits are not clawed back on refund or chargeback
findings.problem: grantRevenueCatCreditPurchase and the Stripe checkout fulfilment grant credits, but no handler deducts them on a RevenueCat REFUND/CANCELLATION or a Stripe charge.refunded/dispute. grep found no reversal path for credit packs.
findings.why_costs_money: A user can buy a pack, spend it, and get an Apple refund, so Brandthread pays the provider cost plus the dispute fee.
findings.fix: Handle refund/dispute events by inserting a 'pack_refund' ledger row that debits purchased_balance (allow it to go negative and block AI until settled).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~1-3% of pack revenue plus provider cost of the refunded usage

findings.title: Shared free text ceiling is 500 requests a day per user, which is far too high
findings.problem: AI_TEXT_DAILY_LIMIT_PER_USER defaults to 500 across chat, agent, store AI and helpers on every plan, including no plan. Combined with the unbounded prompts above, that is the multiplier for the store-ai and chat abuse cases.
findings.why_costs_money: Each request can cost $0.005-1.80, so 500 a day for every free account is a large open liability.
findings.fix: Make the ceiling plan-aware (free 20, Starter 100, Growth 300, Pro 500) and show the remaining count in the app as an upsell.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Caps the per-account text tail from ~$27k/mo to <$50/mo

findings.title: Unlimited forced Whisper re-captioning per video post
findings.problem: POST /posts/:id/captions/generate with {force:true} skips the 'ready' check and re-runs the ffmpeg extract plus whisper-1 on up to 15 minutes of video. The only limits are an in-process inFlight set per post and 30/min. It is gated by the autoCaptions DB feature flag.
findings.why_costs_money: At $0.006/min, a 15-minute video is $0.09 per run, and many posts in parallel could reach about $3.9k a day. ffmpeg on the API host adds CPU.
findings.fix: Allow force at most once per post per 24h (store the last force timestamp) and count it in the AI spend ledger.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $0 while the flag is off; up to ~$100k/mo theoretical with it on; normal ~$50/mo

findings.title: Mobile client times out at 90s while generations keep running and stay charged
findings.problem: EXPENSIVE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS is 90s, but mockup-to-model (5 refs at concurrency 2, each up to 2 high edits) or any 2-attempt QA run can take longer. The client aborts and shows 'Request timed out', while the server finishes, pays OpenAI, and returns 200 to a closed socket. The gate's 'finish' handler sees no error, so credits stay debited.
findings.why_costs_money: The user pays credits for nothing and retries, so Brandthread pays the provider twice.
findings.fix: Make long generations async (job id plus poll or push), or set the client timeout above the worst-case server time and propagate req 'close' to an AbortController passed to the OpenAI call.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Duplicate spend on an estimated 5-15% of heavy generations

findings.title: FFmpeg video compose runs on the API server with no concurrency limit
findings.problem: /posts/compose-video accepts up to 12 clips, 1.5GB and 600s and runs ffmpeg inline in the API process. It has only the generic mutation limit (120/min) and no queue or concurrency cap. Avatar video, captions and thumbnails also shell out to ffmpeg.
findings.why_costs_money: A few concurrent composes saturate the API instance's CPU, so it needs larger instances or autoscaling and slows checkout for everyone.
findings.fix: Move transcoding to a queue or worker with concurrency 1-2 per instance, or a managed service (Mux or Cloudflare Stream at about $1/1k min). Rate-limit compose to about 10 per user per hour.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $100-500/mo extra compute, plus checkout latency risk

findings.title: Media is served through the API with no CDN by default
findings.problem: downloadObject streams GCS objects through the Node API (createReadStream) for /api/posts/media and the other media paths. CDN_BASE_URL is off unless configured, and the doc says 'Nothing here requires one'.
findings.why_costs_money: Every video view pays GCS egress (about $0.12/GB) plus API bandwidth and CPU. A feed of video posts at 1k DAU can easily push TBs a month.
findings.fix: Put Cloud CDN or Cloudflare in front of the bucket before launch and set CDN_BASE_URL plus EXPO_PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL. Serve via signed CDN URLs, not API proxying.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-1,200/mo egress at launch scale (1-10TB); >50% saved with a CDN

findings.title: Gate debits before requirePlan, so non-Growth requests churn the ledger and the global cap
findings.problem: aiCreditsGate runs on /logo, /mockup and the other tools before requirePlan('growth'). Starter or free sellers with any balance get a debit, then a 403, then a refund, and each request takes row locks on ai_credit_accounts and the global ai_spend_daily row (FOR UPDATE).
findings.why_costs_money: Extra DB contention on a single hot row that every paid generation serialises on. It also inflates the alert counters briefly.
findings.fix: Run requirePlan before the gate for these mounts (or have the gate skip when the plan is below the route's minimum), and shard the global counter.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect: DB load and latency

findings.title: Global emergency cap is shared by all users, so abusers can lock out paying sellers
findings.problem: Once 250,000 credits are spent in a UTC day, every seller, Pro included, gets 503 'AI limit reached'. There is no per-plan reservation and no per-user share.
findings.why_costs_money: A handful of abusive Pro or trial accounts can take AI offline for all paying customers for the rest of the day, which drives churn and refunds.
findings.fix: Add per-user daily dollar caps (for example Growth $5/day, Pro $20/day) and reserve global headroom for paid plans.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Churn risk on an AI-led seller base

findings.title: In-memory per-route limiters key on req.auth?.userId and may collapse to 'anon'
findings.problem: The limiters read (req as any).auth?.userId and fall back to 'anon'. requireAuth uses getAuth(req) and sets req.clerkUserId. With @clerk/express ^2.x, where req.auth is callable, the property read can be undefined, so either every user shares one 5/min bucket (throttling paying users) or the limit is effectively per-process only. Maps are never pruned and don't span instances. (Needs a runtime check.)
findings.why_costs_money: Either throttles legitimate paid usage or fails to cap cost when scaled horizontally.
findings.fix: Use req.clerkUserId and the Redis-backed rateLimit middleware with a dedicated 'image-gen' policy.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect

findings.title: ai-helpers comment says the tools are 'priced in AI_TOOL_RULES', but they are free text
findings.problem: The mount comment says caption, description and size chart are priced, but the catalogue marks them 'text' (free, never debited). product-description sends up to 4 product images (low detail) to gpt-5.4-mini.
findings.why_costs_money: Misleading docs, and a missed chance to meter the image-bearing helper.
findings.fix: Fix the comment. Either charge 1 credit for product-description with images or cap it per day for no-plan sellers.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small: ~$0.003/call

findings.title: Store AI vision routes use gpt-5 for store theme JSON with no caching
findings.problem: from-logo, from-moodboard and from-social call gpt-5, a reasoning model at $1.25/$10 per M, with max_completion_tokens 1500. The output is a simple JSON theme. Results aren't cached and the client can re-run them freely. Errors leak String(err) to the client.
findings.why_costs_money: About 5-10x the cost of gpt-5-mini or 4.1-mini for the same output. Reasoning tokens can also eat the 1,500 budget and return empty JSON, which drives retries.
findings.fix: Switch to gpt-5.4-mini or gpt-4.1-mini with json_schema, cache by image hash, and return generic errors.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$0.02-0.03 per call saved; small at scale

findings.title: Seller snapshot rebuilt from about 12 DB queries on every chat message
findings.problem: buildSellerSnapshot(userId) runs fresh for every /ai/chat and /chat/stream turn, and the full snapshot JSON plus help docs is resent as the system prompt every turn. OpenAI prompt caching only helps if the prefix is identical, and the snapshotAt timestamp changes it every time.
findings.why_costs_money: Extra DB load and full-price input tokens on every message.
findings.fix: Cache the snapshot for about 60s per user, move snapshotAt after the static help docs (stable prefix first) so prompt caching applies, and send the snapshot only on the first turn.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~30-50% of chat input-token cost

findings.title: Shopify store-URL import is unmetered: up to 400 fetches plus a gpt-4.1 call per job
findings.problem: POST /shopify-imports and /:id/continue each start a job that makes up to 400 outbound requests (8MB each) and a gpt-4.1 copy call. The only gates are requireRole('manager') and the generic mutation limit (120/min). There is no plan check and no per-day job cap.
findings.why_costs_money: Bandwidth, CPU and token cost per job, plus a risk of being used as a scraping proxy against third-party stores.
findings.fix: Limit to about 5 jobs per seller per day, and add the path to EXPENSIVE_PATH.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$0.05-0.2 per job; abuse in the low hundreds per month

findings.title: 1:1 Agora video calls are free for every user with no duration or daily cap
findings.problem: POST /call/token issues a 15-minute publisher token to any DM participant (buyers included), and a new token can be requested freely. Ordinary DMs have no per-day minute cap and no plan gate.
findings.why_costs_money: Agora bills about $3.99 per 1,000 user-minutes for HD video. Two colluding accounts calling around the clock cost about $345/mo, and normal buyer-seller calls are unpriced.
findings.fix: Cap call minutes per user per day (for example 60), use audio-only by default for buyer DMs, and consider making seller video calls a Growth perk.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$345/mo per abusive pair; normal usage likely <$100/mo

findings.title: Live streams have no maximum duration; every stream records 720p to cloud storage
findings.problem: Pro hosts can stay live indefinitely (token TTL 2h, renewable). Every stream starts Agora mix-mode cloud recording at 720x1280, 1,130 kbps, and stores HLS+MP4 forever. Agora also bills every viewer-minute.
findings.why_costs_money: A 24/7 stream is about 43k host-minutes, about $170 of RTC plus about $260 of recording plus about 360GB of storage a month, more than the $199 Pro price. A 1,000-viewer hour is about $240.
findings.fix: Cap streams at 4h, auto-end on host idle, expire replays after 90 days unless pinned, and price viewer-heavy usage (for example via live commission).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Low until live is popular; each viral stream costs $100s

findings.title: Email marketing has no plan gate and a 1,000/day per-seller cap
findings.problem: Any seller with the marketing permission, including no plan or Starter, can send up to EMAIL_DAILY_SEND_CAP (default 1,000) emails a day through Resend. grep for requirePlan or plan in the route found nothing.
findings.why_costs_money: 30k emails a month per seller at about $0.0009 each is about $27/mo per active seller. Email is also a standard paid-tier feature that is being given away.
findings.fix: Gate campaigns to Growth+ (or a plan-based monthly send quota: Starter 500, Growth 10k, Pro 50k) and show the quota as an upsell.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: At 1k free/Starter sellers sending: up to ~$27k/mo; also an upsell lever

findings.title: SMS OTP sign-in exposes the Clerk account to SMS pumping fraud
findings.problem: sign-in offers phone-code sign-in whenever Clerk allows it (signIn.phoneCode.sendCode). The app adds no country allowlist, CAPTCHA or per-number throttle. Protection depends entirely on Clerk dashboard settings.
findings.why_costs_money: International SMS pumping can run to thousands of dollars per incident, and Clerk bills SMS beyond the included US/CA volume.
findings.fix: In the Clerk dashboard, restrict SMS to launch countries, enable bot protection, and consider email-first OTP with phone as optional.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $0 normally; $1-10k per pumping incident

findings.title: Design Studio gives every signed-in account 2GB of cloud storage with no plan tiering
findings.problem: /design-studio requires auth plus teamContext only, and MAX_OWNER_ASSET_BYTES is 2GB for every account regardless of plan. Background-removal results are also saved to GCS forever (bg-removal.ts saveToGCS) with no retention policy.
findings.why_costs_money: Storage grows without bound across free accounts, and plan-based storage is a common upsell that is being missed.
findings.fix: Tier storage (free 100MB, Starter 1GB, Growth 5GB, Pro 20GB) and add lifecycle deletion for bg-removal results after 30 days.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$0.04/GB-mo; small but grows; upsell lever

findings.title: Review-readiness doc says no AI credit product exists, but credit packs are live
findings.problem: iap-rails.md row 5 says 'No credit or pay-per-use AI product exists ... PASS'. The code now sells 3 consumable packs (RevenueCat on native, Stripe on web) and needs App Store Connect consumable products brandthread_ai_credits_500/1500/5000.
findings.why_costs_money: Review notes and App Store Connect setup will be wrong. Missing IAP products leave the pack section hidden on iOS (lost revenue), or the review gets rejected over an undeclared consumable.
findings.fix: Update the doc, create the 3 consumables in ASC and Play, and attach them to the review submission.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Pack revenue blocked on iOS until the products exist

findings.title: Pro ceiling counts requests, not images, with no per-user concurrency limit
findings.problem: The proDailyGenerations ceiling increments by 1 per request, whether that request is one bg removal or a 5-reference mockup-to-model run (up to 10 edits). Requests have no per-user concurrency limit.
findings.why_costs_money: The ceiling understates real spend by up to 10x.
findings.fix: Increment by the number of output images (or by credit cost) and cap concurrent jobs per user at 2.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Part of the Pro exposure above

findings.title: Expensive-path rate-limit regex misses several paid AI routes
findings.problem: EXPENSIVE_PATH covers ai|logo|mockup|photography|lifestyle|techpack|bg-removal|store/ai|support-chat/message. It does not match /ai-helpers (the regex needs '/ai/' or '/ai' at the end), /onboarding-sample, /posts/:id/captions/generate (which adds it explicitly), /brandthread-agent (which has its own policy), /shopify-imports or /places. It is also case-sensitive.
findings.why_costs_money: Uncovered routes fall back to the 120/min mutation policy, 4x looser.
findings.fix: Replace the regex with explicit per-router rateLimit('expensive') middleware, or make it case-insensitive and list every AI mount.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Multiplier on the abuse cases above

findings.title: Techpack PDF is billed 4 credits for one gpt-4.1 text call costing about $0.01
findings.problem: techpack/generate makes one generateText call (default gpt-4.1, about 2-3k tokens) and renders the PDF locally with PDFKit. It is priced at 4 credits and gated to Growth.
findings.why_costs_money: No loss here, but Starter sellers, who would value tech packs for manufacturers, can't use it at all.
findings.fix: Consider opening tech packs to Starter at 4 credits as a reason to subscribe, since it is profitable per call.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Upsell lever, ~$0.01 cost per call

findings.title: Brandthread Agent chat has sensible limits (reference point)
