findings.problem: The agent has no tool loop. It uses 16 history messages, 2,000-char inputs, max_completion_tokens 300, the agent-chat limit (20/min) and the 500/day text ceiling. Cost is about $0.002 per message.
findings.why_costs_money: Low exposure. It is listed so it is not mistaken for an unbounded agent loop.
findings.fix: No change needed beyond plan-aware text ceilings.

findings.title: Image moderation and prompt moderation use free OpenAI moderation (no cost issue)
findings.problem: omni-moderation-latest is free. The one cost is the extra round trip per AI request. The guard skips signed-out traffic.
findings.why_costs_money: No direct cost.
findings.fix: Keep it. Make sure AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_API_KEY is set in prod so moderation actually runs.

findings.title: analytics-insights and product-seo make no paid AI calls despite their names
findings.problem: grep for openai, generateText and completeJson finds no hits in either file. Insights are SQL-based, and /advanced is gated by requirePlan('pro'). SEO fields are entered manually.
findings.why_costs_money: No cost. This is a monetisation gap: AI SEO title/description generation is a cheap (~$0.002) feature that would justify paid tiers.
findings.fix: Add an AI SEO suggestion through ai-helpers (credit-priced or Starter+).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Upsell lever only

findings.title: Credit ledger cannot go negative and debits atomically before the call (verified working)
findings.problem: debitCredits locks the account row, checks total >= cost, debits rollover, then monthly, then purchased, and fails closed (503) if billing errors. Free/no-plan accounts get 0 monthly credits. Refunds are idempotent. For matched paths the gate design is sound; the leaks are unmatched paths and the pricing.
findings.why_costs_money: None directly. Fixes should reuse this ledger rather than replace it.
findings.fix: Keep it. Move cost into the route (a debit helper) so path regexes can't drift.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: n/a

findings.title: Simple product (no size/color options) is saved with zero variants and no price; it cannot be bought
findings.problem: For a product with no options, localVariants is [], so productVariantsForServer is [] and serverCreatePayload has no price field (products has no price column). The server inserts the product with no product_variants rows. Buyers see lowestPrice 0 ($0.00), findVariant returns undefined, and addToCart returns early (line 851). Checkout prices only from product_variants. The "In stock" stepper (stockStr) is also never sent. A seller who lists a one-size tee or a print gets a "Product published! … is now live" sheet for an item nobody can buy.
findings.why_costs_money: This is the most common first listing for a new brand. Every one of those listings produces $0 GMV, and therefore $0 commission, while the seller believes they are live.
findings.fix: Additive: in handlePublish, when localVariants is empty, send one default variant { sku: auto, priceCents: pricing.priceCents, stock: parseInt(stockStr) || 0 }. Add a server-side guard too: if status=active and there are no variants, create a default variant from a new priceCents body field.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks commission on every no-options listing; likely 30-50% of first listings, so tens of $k GMV/month and roughly $1-3k/mo commission at target scale

findings.title: Sellers can activate products and publish the store before Stripe Connect; buyer checkout then fails
findings.problem: Product create and store publish do not check stripeAccountStatus. Discover and feed show the products. Only at checkout does the buyer get SELLER_PAYMENTS_UNAVAILABLE / "Seller payment account is not yet active".
findings.why_costs_money: Each buyer who reaches checkout on an unconnected seller is a lost sale and a worse buyer impression of the platform.
findings.fix: Additive: (1) a "Payouts not set up — buyers can’t check out yet" interstitial on add-product (status=active) and on launch-publish; (2) a buyer-facing "Notify me when available" on product detail when the seller is not connected. Don’t hard-block publishing.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$2-4k/mo of GMV commission plus lost buyers on early sellers who list before connecting

findings.title: Shipping-label from-address falls back to the buyer’s address
findings.problem: fulfill-order sends fromAddress = order.fulfillment.fromAddress ?? order.customer.shippingAddress. adaptApiOrder never sets fulfillment.fromAddress, so it is always undefined and the buyer’s own address becomes address_from on the Shippo shipment. Rates are quoted buyer-to-buyer (wrong price), and the purchased label shows the buyer as sender, so undeliverable returns go to the buyer.
findings.why_costs_money: The first order is mis-shipped or mis-priced. Seller support and refunds follow, and the label cost charged against the seller balance may not match the real shipment.
findings.fix: Additive: add a ship-from address step (reuse /locations) before the first label, map it into fulfillment.fromAddress, and have the server reject /rates when fromAddress equals shippingAddress.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: every first order that buys a label is affected; refunds and churn on first sales

findings.title: Funnel count: ~15 screens/~40 taps to first listing; ~25 screens/~75 taps to get paid
findings.problem: Path to the first listing (email signup): native splash and splash.tsx (auto-advance after 2.5s, 0 taps), then onboarding WELCOME (1), ACCOUNT_TYPE (2: card + Continue), AUTH (about 9 inputs: first, last, email, username, password, confirm, DOB, terms, Create; then a 6-digit code and Verify, about 11), NAME (1, already prefilled), BRAND_NAME (2), BRAND_STAGE (1), GOALS (1, Skip), PLAN preview/sample (1), PLAN pick (1), LOADING (auto), NOTIFICATIONS (2 with the OS prompt), SUCCESS (1). That is 13 onboarding screens and about 25 taps. The dashboard then auto-opens the setup walkthrough sheet and a 3-step FirstRunTip tour (about 4 taps to clear). Add product (1), photo (about 4), name (1), price (1), status pill set to Active (2), Save (1). Total: about 15 screens and about 40 taps to a "published" product, and that product cannot be bought (see the no-variant finding). To actually get paid, add the Stripe Connect banner (1), Stripe hosted Express onboarding (about 8-12 external screens, about 25 taps), Launch card, Publish, Publish (3) and variant/stock setup (about 6). That is about 25+ screens and about 75 taps.
findings.why_costs_money: Every extra required screen before the first live, buyable listing costs signups. Industry onboarding drop-off is roughly 5-10% per required step, and two of the steps here (duplicate NAME, plan screen with no purchase) add friction without adding value.
findings.fix: Keep the flow but add nothing new to it. Auto-advance NAME when it is already prefilled, route SUCCESS straight into add-product, and put a single "Get paid" CTA on the add-product success sheet so the money path is one continuous track.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$3-6k/mo: a 15-25% lift in sellers reaching a live, buyable product directly scales both subscription and 5% commission revenue

findings.title: New product variants default to stock 0 with tracking on; "published" listings show as sold out
findings.problem: trackInventory defaults to true. Generated variants start with qty "" and are sent as stock 0. validateForPublish only checks name, price and photo. An Active product can be saved with every variant at 0 stock, and buyers see it as out of stock (inStock requires inventoryQuantity > 0). There is no warning at Save.
findings.why_costs_money: The first listing looks live to the seller but cannot convert. The seller sees traffic and no sales and churns.
findings.fix: Additive: add a validateForPublish warning ("All variants have 0 in stock — buyers will see Sold out. Publish anyway?") when status=active and total stock is 0.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo of lost first-week GMV commission plus seller churn

findings.title: New products default to Draft, and the success sheet offers no "Publish now" or share step
findings.problem: storeSettings.status defaults to "draft". The only way to go Active is a small header status pill and an action sheet. If the seller just fills the form and taps Save, the sheet says "Draft saved!" with "View product" and "Done". Nothing on it offers "Publish now" or "Share your product".
findings.why_costs_money: Drafts earn $0. New sellers often don’t notice the pill and leave their first product invisible.
findings.fix: Additive: when kind=created and status=draft, add a primary "Publish now" action to the SuccessSheet (it calls api.products.update with status active). When published, add a "Share product" action.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo: recovers first listings stuck in draft

findings.title: "Add your first product" checklist task completes on a draft, and the server launch checklist counts drafts/archived
findings.problem: completeSetupTaskAfter("first_product") uses the default confirmsSuccess=()=>true, so a draft ticks the task. The server launch checklist uses count(*) over products with deletedAt null, which includes draft and archived. Both checklists say the product step is done when nothing is buyable.
findings.why_costs_money: Inaccurate progress removes the nudge exactly when the seller still needs it.
findings.fix: Pass confirmsSuccess: () => finalStatus === "active" in add-product, and add `AND status = 'active'` to the launch-checklist product count.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1k/mo: keeps the nudge alive for sellers whose only product is a draft

findings.title: No seller alert when a buyer is blocked at checkout because the seller has no payouts
findings.problem: When checkout throws SELLER_PAYMENTS_UNAVAILABLE, nothing notifies the seller. A grep of lib, routes and jobs finds no "lost sale" or "seller_not_ready" publishNotification.
findings.why_costs_money: This is the strongest possible activation nudge ("A buyer just tried to pay you $48 — finish payouts to get it"), and it goes unsent.
findings.fix: Additive: on SELLER_PAYMENTS_UNAVAILABLE, call publishNotification({ userId: sellerId, type: "checkout_blocked_no_payouts" }), throttled to once per 24h per seller, with a deep link to /payouts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo: converts blocked buyers into connected sellers and recovered sales

findings.title: No activation nudge jobs: nothing fires for 0 products, unfinished payouts, or abandoned onboarding
findings.problem: The jobs directory has buyer cart recovery, trial-day-4 and team-invite reminders, but no seller activation job. Searches for activation, nudge, drip, "first product" and "finish setup" found nothing. A seller who signs up and has 0 products after 24h, a product but no Stripe after 48h, or a Clerk account but onboarding_complete=false gets no push or email.
findings.why_costs_money: Activation is the biggest lever on a subscription business. Sellers who list in week 1 are far more likely to stay.
findings.fix: Additive: add a jobs/sellerActivationNudges.ts modeled on sellerTrialReminder.ts (lease plus event table): T+24h with 0 active products, T+48h with no stripe active, T+72h with no publish, and incomplete onboarding at T+2h and T+24h by email.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$3-5k/mo: a 10-20% activation lift on the signup cohort

findings.title: Buyer-to-seller conversion is impossible in-app: account-type-settings has no entry point
findings.problem: account-type-settings.tsx exists, but no buyer settings menu or other screen links to it (it is only referenced in parentFallback and SellerGlobalTabBar). If a buyer did reach it, it only PATCHes accountType and says "Restart the app". Local AsyncStorage user_role stays "buyer", and AuthGate trusts the local role first, so they stay in (buyer). No brandName or brandStage is collected either, which the server requires for seller completion (auth.ts:663-667).
findings.why_costs_money: Buyers who make things are the cheapest seller acquisition channel, and that path is closed.
findings.fix: Additive: add a "Start selling on Brandthread" row to the buyer settings catalog that opens onboarding in an add-seller mode (BRAND_NAME → BRAND_STAGE → PLAN → finishSeller), updates the local user_role, and routes to /(tabs).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo: even 1% of buyers converting to subscribing sellers is meaningful at scale

findings.title: Seller onboarding ends on the dashboard rather than the value moment (add product)
findings.problem: finishSeller does router.replace("/(tabs)/"). On first open the dashboard stacks the StripeConnectWarning banner, the auto-opened SetupWalkthroughSheet, the anchored 3-step FirstRunTip tour, the new-seller card and the LaunchChecklistCard. That is five competing prompts before the seller lists anything.
findings.why_costs_money: Choice overload at the first touch lowers first-product completion.
findings.fix: Additive: on firstCompletion route to /add-product?from=onboarding, and suppress FirstRunTip and the walkthrough auto-open until after the first product.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo via higher day-0 listing rate

findings.title: Launch checklist orders Payouts last, after Publish; buyers arrive before payment works
findings.problem: Step order is name, logo/banner, accent, socials, first_product, preview, publish, payouts. "Next:" on the dashboard card walks the seller through publishing (and the "You’re live — share link" moment) before payouts.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers share a store they cannot get paid from, and every early buyer hits SELLER_PAYMENTS_UNAVAILABLE.
findings.fix: Reorder LAUNCH_STEP_IDS so payouts comes before publish (an additive reorder of the array, no UI change).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo of early GMV that currently fails at checkout

findings.title: launch-publish "You’re live" screen has no payouts warning
findings.problem: publish() calls publishStore and then shows the "You’re live" share/QR screen. It never reads checklist.steps.payouts, and StripeConnectWarning is not on this screen. It is mounted only on the dashboard, payouts, seller-settings and billing-access.
findings.why_costs_money: The share burst after going live sends traffic to a store that cannot take money.
findings.fix: Additive: render <StripeConnectWarning /> at the top of the live state, and show a "Set up payouts so buyers can pay" row when payouts is not done.

findings.title: publishStore() swallows the server publish error and still reports "You’re live"
findings.problem: publishStore saves publishStatus="published" to local AsyncStorage and then calls `try { await api.store.publish(); } catch { /* no-op */ }`, returning success:true either way. On a network or 5xx failure the seller sees the "You’re live" celebration, but the server storefront stays draft, and the server-derived checklist still says unpublished.
findings.why_costs_money: The seller shares a store that the server considers unpublished, and the visible state contradicts the checklist.
findings.fix: Have the catch return { success:false, message:"Couldn’t publish — try again" } instead of swallowing the error (additive error handling).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo of lost launches plus support tickets

findings.title: Storefront draft is cached device-wide (bt:store:v1), not per user, and never cleared on sign-out
findings.problem: getStorefront and saveStorefront use one AsyncStorage key that is not scoped to the user, and local storage is treated as "local truth". saveStorefront then fire-and-forgets api.store.save with the local copy. A second seller on the same device inherits and can push the previous seller’s storefront. A reinstall or new device starts from defaults, and the next save overwrites the server design.
findings.why_costs_money: Lost storefront work makes sellers re-setup or churn, and the cross-account leak is a trust and privacy problem.
findings.fix: Scope the key to the userId the way setupStore does (@brandthread/setup_state:<userId>), clear it on sign-out in AuthGate, and hydrate from api.store.get() when no local copy exists.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1k/mo of churn and support; also a privacy risk

findings.title: Three different store URLs are shown to the seller
findings.problem: store-publish confirms "live at https://<storeUrl>.brandthread.app" (a subdomain). share-store uses https://brandthread.app/store/<handle>. When the username is missing, share-store falls back to a slug of the brand name, which store/[handle] cannot resolve. launch-publish uses buildStoreUrl, which returns null with no handle and hides the link.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers paste whichever URL they saw. If the subdomain or the brand-name slug does not resolve, all their launch traffic is lost.
findings.fix: Additive: use buildStoreUrl() everywhere. In share-store, when there is no username, show "Set your @handle to get a link" instead of a made-up slug.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1k/mo of misdirected launch traffic

findings.title: CSV/Etsy/Shopify imports don’t tick "first product" and land as drafts with no bulk publish
findings.problem: Imports never call completeSetupTask("first_product"). CSV and Etsy commits force status "draft". The bulk-edit screen only exposes archive and draft (runStatus("archived"|"draft")), even though the server /product-bulk/status already accepts "active". A seller migrating 80 products must open and publish each one.
findings.why_costs_money: Migrating sellers are the highest-value cohort (existing catalog and buyers), and they get stuck at 0 live products.
findings.fix: Additive: add a "Publish selected" action to products-bulk-edit calling productBulk.status({ status: "active" }), add a "Publish all imported" button to ProductImportPreview, and complete first_product on a successful commit.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo: catalog sellers drive disproportionate GMV

findings.title: Dashboard keeps saying "List your first product" until the first sale, even with products live
findings.problem: newSeller is everSoldCount <= 0, so a seller with 30 active products and 0 orders still sees "List your first product / Add a product". This is the moment a "Share your store" loop should replace it.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers who have listed but not sold need traffic, not more products. The wrong CTA delays the first sale.
findings.fix: Additive: when the active product count is > 0 and everSoldCount is 0, render a "Share your store to get your first sale" card (share-store, QR, copy link) in place of the add-product card.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo: earlier first sale lifts retention and commission

findings.title: No "share your store/product" loop after the first product is created
findings.problem: Share prompts exist only on launch-publish and in the dashboard traffic panel (onShareStore). Creating the first Active product, the strongest share moment, gives "View product / Done".
findings.why_costs_money: This loses the free-distribution loop that brings the first buyers, especially before Meta Ads or Boost.
findings.fix: Additive: add a "Share" action (Share.share with the product URL) to the SuccessSheet when kind=created and status=active.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo of organic first-sale traffic

findings.title: No checkout shipping charge unless the seller configured rates; sellers eat label costs
findings.problem: With no shipping zones and no active shipping_rate, checkout charges shippingCents = 0. The add-product "Shipping cost" field (estimatedShippingCostCents) is not used at checkout. Shipping setup is a non-blocking checklist item, so a new seller’s first orders ship free, and labels are then paid from their balance (FUNDS_RESERVED_FOR_LABELS).
findings.why_costs_money: First-order margin is negative for the seller ($5-10 per label), which is a common reason sellers quit after the first sale.
findings.fix: Additive: in add-product, or when publishing the first Active product, show "Buyers currently pay $0 shipping — set rates" with a link to /shipping, plus a dashboard row when there are 0 shipping rates.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1.5k/mo of seller margin and retention

findings.title: Money features are buried: More tab unreachable, Subscription excluded from Studio menu
findings.problem: The More screen (with its "Money" section: Payouts, Subscription) has href:null, and nothing pushes to it except back-fallbacks. The Studio radial menu explicitly excludes "subscription". Subscription and Compare plans are reachable only through Profile, the settings gear, seller-settings and then the "Plan/subscription" section (about 4 taps, below the fold). Payouts is reachable from the Studio menu.
findings.why_costs_money: Self-serve upgrades need a visible path. Burying the plan cuts upgrade revenue.
findings.fix: Additive: add a "Plan" row and badge to the dashboard header or profile top bar, and add "subscription" back into CARD_ORDER of the Studio menu.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo of self-serve upgrades

findings.title: Trial reminder job exists, but no trial is ever started in the seller funnel
findings.problem: sellerTrialReminder sends a day-4 push to sellers on a live trial. Because onboarding never starts a trial, the job has nothing to act on. That is wasted engineering, and the docs and code suggest a working trial funnel that does not exist.
findings.why_costs_money: The conversion reminder, the last lever before auto-renew, never fires.
findings.fix: This resolves automatically once the PLAN step triggers the trial. Cross-ref subscription-iap.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: part of the trial-conversion loss above

findings.title: Welcome email tells new sellers "Your style space is ready… discover brands" (buyer copy)
findings.problem: sendWelcomeEmail fires on the first /auth/sync (created=true), which runs during the AUTH step before accountType is saved. finishSeller sets accountType later (onboarding.tsx:2406-2411). user.accountType is null, so roleLabel is "buyer" and the body is the buyer text. The CTA is a generic https://brandthread.app instead of a deep link to add-product.
findings.why_costs_money: The one guaranteed seller email is spent on the wrong message with no activation CTA.
findings.fix: Additive: also send a seller-specific welcome at POST /auth/onboarding/complete firstCompletion when accountType=seller (idempotency key welcome-seller/<id>), with a CTA deep link to add-product, and skip the generic welcome when accountType is null.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo through better first-week activation

findings.title: Invite-only flag gates buyers and sellers alike; no seller-only or buyer-only mode
findings.problem: inviteOnlySignup is a single global flag, and getAccessStatus does not look at accountType. It is OFF by default (migration 241), so organic seller signups are not blocked at launch. If Dev turns it on to throttle seller quality, it also blocks every organic buyer. The doc does not mention this.
findings.why_costs_money: Turning it on at launch would cut buyer acquisition, and therefore GMV, to zero for non-invited users.
findings.fix: Additive: add an inviteOnlySellerSignup flag and check it only when accountType=seller in onboarding/complete and access/status. Document in invite-only.md that the current flag is all-roles.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: would block all organic GMV if flipped; ~$0 while OFF

findings.title: Seller NAME step re-asks the first name already captured on the auth form
findings.problem: The seller auth form requires formFirstName (canSubmit line 1202) and passes it in with onFirstNamePrefill. The next screen is a full NAME step asking "What should we call you?" with the same value prefilled. It is a non-skippable extra tap and screen.
findings.why_costs_money: This is one redundant required step in the highest-drop-off part of the funnel.
findings.fix: Auto-advance past NAME when firstName.trim().length >= 2 came from the auth form or OAuth (keep the step for OAuth users with no name).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-700/mo: a few % fewer onboarding drop-offs

findings.title: Plan/price screen comes before any value moment
findings.problem: The price wall ($29/$79/$199) is step 7 of 10, before the seller has a workspace, a product or a storefront. The only value preview is one AI logo sample (SellerPreviewStep). Today it is harmless because nothing is charged. Once the trial is wired it will sit before value.
findings.why_costs_money: If the trial goes live here, conversion to trial is likely lower than after the first product. A card-required trial converts best right after an "aha" moment.
findings.fix: Option A: keep the recommendation step but launch the purchase sheet after the first product is published, as an additive post-publish sheet. Option B: keep it in onboarding but show the sample storefront and logo inside the paywall. A/B test both.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$2-4k/mo swing in trial starts depending on placement

findings.title: Launch checklist cannot reach 8/8 without an Instagram or TikTok account
findings.problem: The socials step is required for checklist completion (hasSocial needs instagram or tiktok), and store-setup-socials disables Continue until one valid handle is entered. There is no skip. Sellers with no IG/TikTok, or who sell through Pinterest or offline, never finish, so the "Launch your store" card stays forever.
findings.why_costs_money: A permanently incomplete checklist reads as "not ready", and it is a forced step that could be deferred.
findings.fix: Additive: add a "Skip for now" link on store-setup-socials that records socials_skipped_at, and treat that as done in deriveLaunchChecklist.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-500/mo through cleaner launch completion

findings.title: Store publish has no product/payout gate; an empty store can go "live"
findings.problem: validateStore blocks only on store name, sections and URL. It does not check active product count or payouts. The server /store/publish has no checks at all.
findings.why_costs_money: An empty live store shared to followers wastes the seller’s one launch moment.
findings.fix: Additive: add warnings (not errors) in validateStore for "No active products yet" and "Payouts not connected — buyers can’t pay", fed from api.seller.launchChecklist.get().

findings.title: Two parallel setup checklists on the dashboard with different steps, order and data sources
findings.problem: The local setupStore has 9 tasks in AsyncStorage (payments is #2, includes domain and first video). The server launch checklist has 8 steps (payouts is #8, includes socials and accent). Both render on the dashboard (SetupContinueBanner and LaunchChecklistCard) with different percentages and different "Next" items.
findings.why_costs_money: Conflicting guidance makes the next step unclear, and sellers stall.
findings.fix: Additive: have the setup walkthrough read its done flags from the server launch checklist where they overlap (first_product, payouts, publish), and hide SetupContinueBanner while LaunchChecklistCard is visible.

findings.title: Setup checklist makes "Connect a domain" and "Post your first video" required; it rarely reaches 100%
findings.problem: connect_domain ("a custom domain you already own") and first_post are not marked optional. isSetupComplete needs completed, not skipped, on every required task, so skipping keeps the banner up forever and SetupCelebration never fires. The celebration also has only a dismiss button, with no share CTA.
findings.why_costs_money: This forces steps that could be deferred and shows a nag banner forever. The celebration moment is wasted without a share loop.
findings.fix: Mark connect_domain and first_post optional:true, count skipped tasks as done in isSetupComplete, and add a "Share your store" primaryAction to SetupCelebration.

findings.title: Products empty state offers only "Add your first product"; import options are hidden in the menu
findings.problem: The empty state has one action (add-product). CSV, Shopify and Etsy import only appear inside the header "…" action sheet. Sellers with an existing catalog don’t discover them at the moment they matter.
findings.why_costs_money: This slows activation for sellers who already have a catalog elsewhere.
findings.fix: Additive: add a secondaryAction "Import from Shopify/CSV" to the all-filter EmptyState.

findings.title: Orders tab empty state has no CTA (no share-store or add-product)
findings.problem: The empty Orders shows "No orders yet. Orders show up here once a buyer checks out." with no action.
findings.why_costs_money: This is a dead end at the exact point the seller should be driving traffic.
findings.fix: Additive: add actionLabel "Share your store" and onAction router.push("/share-store") (or "Add a product" when there are 0 active products).

findings.title: New-order alert is push-only; sellers who skipped notifications miss the first order
findings.problem: new_order_received goes through publishNotification (push and in-app feed). No seller email is sent for a new order (brandthreadEmail has no seller order template). Onboarding lets sellers skip the push permission.
findings.why_costs_money: A missed first order means late shipment, buyer cancellation or refund, and a bad first-sale experience.
findings.fix: Additive: send a seller "You made a sale" email (sendBrandthreadEmail) on new_order_received, at least for the first 10 orders or when push is not granted.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo of saved first orders

findings.title: AI store generator (store-generate/from-logo/from-social) is outside the new-seller path
findings.problem: The headline "AI builds your store" flows are reachable only from store-editor’s menu. The setup task customize_store routes to /store-builder, and the launch checklist routes to store-setup-brand. New sellers never see the differentiating feature during setup.
findings.why_costs_money: The differentiator that justifies the subscription stays hidden during the trial window.
findings.fix: Additive: add a "Let AI design my store" secondary CTA on store-setup-brand that pushes /store-generate.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1k/mo of trial-to-paid lift

findings.title: Onboarding tests lock in "seller success → tabs" with no plan purchase assertion
findings.problem: onboarding.ux.test.ts asserts the seller success routes to tabs. No test asserts that a trial or purchase starts at the PLAN step. The e2e test has no "plans", "purchase" or "trial" assertions.
findings.why_costs_money: Regressions in the revenue-critical step will pass CI.
findings.fix: Add a test asserting the PLAN Continue button navigates to /plans?fromOnboarding=true (or calls the purchase) before finishSeller.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: guards the subscription funnel

findings.title: Invite gate appears only after full Clerk signup and email verification
findings.problem: AuthGate checks api.access.status() only once isSignedIn is true. With the flag on, a seller fills the full auth form and verifies email, then gets bounced to /access-code. The public POST /api/access/validate endpoint exists but nothing in the app calls it, so there is no "have a code?" step before account creation.
findings.why_costs_money: Users who already invested about 11 taps hit a wall, which hurts waitlist conversion when the flag is on.
findings.fix: Additive: when access status is unavailable pre-auth, show an optional invite-code field on the WELCOME/ACCOUNT_TYPE step that calls api.access.validate(), and stash the code for redeem after signup.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: only matters if invite-only is enabled

findings.title: Waitlist invites are never emailed; admin must copy each code and send it by hand
findings.problem: POST /admin/access/waitlist/:id/invite creates the code and returns it to the admin. It sends no email (no sendBrandthreadEmail call), and the runbook says "send it to them".
findings.why_costs_money: With invite-only on, every waitlisted seller needs manual work. Invites go stale and sellers are lost.
findings.fix: Additive: call sendBrandthreadEmail with the code and an app deep link inside the invite transaction’s success path (idempotency key waitlist-invite/<id>).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: only matters if invite-only is enabled

findings.title: Under-18 sellers fill the whole wizard, then get a generic "check your connection" error
findings.problem: The server returns 403 AGE_RESTRICTED from onboarding/complete for 13-17 sellers. finishSeller’s catch only special-cases username conflicts and shows "We couldn’t save your brand profile. Check your connection" with Retry, which loops forever. bandMaySell and AGE_RESTRICTED_COPY exist, but onboarding never uses them after the DOB is entered.
findings.why_costs_money: This wastes support time. A teen who could be routed to the buyer flow (and buy) is stuck instead.
findings.fix: Additive: after the auth step records the DOB, check bandMaySell. If false on the seller flow, show AGE_RESTRICTED_COPY with a "Continue as a buyer" button.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small; mostly support cost and lost buyer conversions

findings.title: Account-type card promises "AI-powered design studio", but AI routes 403 for non-Growth sellers
findings.problem: The seller card leads with "AI-powered design studio". /logo, /mockup, /photography, /bg-removal, /lifestyle and /techpack are mounted with requirePlan("growth"). A new seller (Starter fallback, no trial) gets PLAN_REQUIRED on first use.
findings.why_costs_money: Feature-promise mismatch at the first touch hurts trust, but it is also an upsell moment if handled well.
findings.fix: Additive: add "(Growth plan)" to that bullet, or make sure the Growth trial starts in onboarding so the promise holds during the trial.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: minor; mostly trust

findings.title: Setup checklist progress is device-local; reinstall or new device resets it
findings.problem: Setup state is stored only in AsyncStorage (@brandthread/setup_state:<userId>). Only verify_account and connect_payments re-derive from server data. A seller who switches phones sees "Add your first product" again even with 40 products.
findings.why_costs_money: Inaccurate nudges erode trust and hide the real next step.
findings.fix: Additive: on getSetupState, merge done flags from api.seller.launchChecklist.get() (first_product, publish, payouts) and from the shipping-rates count.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small

findings.title: Analytics tab with no data has no next step
findings.problem: Visits and Revenue tiles show 0, and the chart shows "No revenue data yet". There is no CTA to share the store or create a post.
findings.why_costs_money: A missed loop to drive the first traffic.
findings.fix: Additive: when summary.visits === 0, render a small card with "Share your store" (/share-store) and "Post to the Thread" (/create-post).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small

findings.title: Guided setup screen (/setup) is orphaned
findings.problem: setup.tsx renders a full guided-setup checklist, but the only link to it is the navigation-isolation probe. The dashboard uses SetupWalkthroughSheet instead.
findings.why_costs_money: This is dead code that confuses audits, though it is not user-facing.
findings.fix: Either link it from SetupContinueBanner "See all" or delete it later. No user impact today.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: none directly

findings.title: Preview/demo fixtures are correctly gated away from real accounts (verified)
findings.problem: isPreviewDemoMode and isSellerDevPreview return false in release native builds (IS_PROD_NATIVE), when !__DEV__ && !NAVIGATION_ISOLATION_TEST, and on production hosts. Demo data needs an explicit &demo=1. No demo seller data leaks into real seller accounts. Residual risk: an exported web build with EXPO_PUBLIC_NAVIGATION_ISOLATION_TEST=1 on a non-production host would show preview data.
findings.why_costs_money: No direct loss. This is listed so the team does not re-audit it.
findings.fix: Optional: add a CI check that the production web export has EXPO_PUBLIC_NAVIGATION_ISOLATION_TEST unset.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: none

findings.title: No dead routes in funnel screens (verified by script)
findings.problem: A script checked every literal router.push/replace/route/nav target in app/, components/ and lib/ against the expo-router file tree. The only unmatched target was a template-built /u/<handle>, which resolves to app/u/. Button-level dead ends are listed in the other findings.
findings.why_costs_money: None.
findings.fix: None.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: none

findings.title: Guest checkout unreachable: cart and Shop-sheet push /thread-checkout, which is not a guest route
findings.problem: GUEST_TOP_LEVEL allows 'buyer-checkout' but not its alias 'thread-checkout'. The cart's startCheckout always pushes /thread-checkout?source=cart, and Shop sheet Buy now pushes /thread-checkout. AuthGate then sees a signed-out user on a protected route and router.replace()s to /sign-in with no returnTo, so the cart context is lost.
findings.why_costs_money: Guest checkout (routes/guest-checkout.ts) is built but no signed-out buyer can reach it from the two main buy paths. Every guest impulse purchase turns into a forced signup.
findings.fix: Add 'thread-checkout' (and 'thread-product-detail', see next finding) to GUEST_TOP_LEVEL in lib/guestRoutes.ts. This is a one-line additive change. Add a test asserting every alias re-export of a guest route is itself guest-allowed.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$5-10k/mo: guests are typically 20-40% of first-time mobile commerce buyers, and at the $50k target this path is fully blocked

findings.title: Guests tapping any product in feed/search/discover/category are bounced to sign-in
findings.problem: thread-product-detail.tsx re-exports buyer-product-detail, but only 'buyer-product-detail' is in the guest allow-list. Discover tiles, search results, category/trending grids, Shop sheet 'View details', saved items and recently viewed all push /thread-product-detail, so a guest gets replaced to /sign-in.
findings.why_costs_money: 'Browse as a guest' (WelcomeStep, sign-in) leads to Discover, where the first product tap hits a sign-in wall. That is the forced-signup-before-browsing pattern the guest mode was built to avoid, and it is a Guideline 5.1.1(v) rejection risk.
findings.fix: Add 'thread-product-detail' to GUEST_TOP_LEVEL. Also add a CI test that walks every push('/x') target in buyer components and asserts it is either guest-allowed or protected by requireSignIn.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all guest browsing-to-PDP; plausibly $3-8k/mo plus App Review rejection risk

findings.title: Hosted checkout returns to unregistered 'mobile://' scheme via openBrowserAsync
findings.problem: successUrl and cancelUrl are 'mobile://checkout/return…', but the app scheme is 'brandthread'. The flow uses WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync, not openAuthSessionAsync, so the redirect never closes the browser. The buyer must tap Done, which returns type 'cancel', and the code shows 'Payment cancelled' and returns before verifySession runs. In a multi-seller loop, the remaining sellers are never processed. The hosted path is used for every guest, every pre-order/drop, every Thread Cash or loyalty order, and whenever EXPO_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is missing.
findings.why_costs_money: Buyers who paid are told they cancelled. That drives duplicate attempts, support tickets and chargebacks, and multi-store hosted carts only pay the first seller. Drops and pre-orders are a core format and always take this path.
findings.fix: Use WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync(url, 'brandthread://checkout/return') (or Linking.createURL) and set success/cancel URLs to the brandthread:// scheme or an https universal link. Treat 'cancel' as 'verify first, then decide'.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all guest + pre-order + Thread Cash revenue; likely 30-50% of GMV at launch

findings.title: PDP: one-size / no-option products can never be added to cart or bought
findings.problem: allSelected = product.options.length > 0 && …, so a product whose variants have no size and no color (accessories, bags, one-size, and every CSV/bulk-imported product, whose default variant has no size/color: api-server routes/products.ts:643-650) is never 'allSelected'. Add to cart silently returns, and Buy now shows 'Select options' with no options rendered. ShopProductSheet handles this case correctly (ShopProductSheet.tsx:672-674).
findings.why_costs_money: A whole class of listings is unbuyable from the full product page, which is where search, category, saved and recently-viewed traffic lands.
findings.fix: Change to allSelected = product.options.length === 0 || Object.keys(selections).length === product.options.length, and auto-select when there is exactly one variant (mirroring ShopProductSheet.tsx:611-623).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all sales of no-option products from PDP; easily $1-3k/mo

findings.title: Shared product link opens the SELLER's admin screen, not the buyer PDP
findings.problem: The canonical product share URL https://brandthread.app/store/product/{id} router.replace()s to /product-detail?id=, which is the seller's 8-tab management screen. It reads getProduct() from the seller's own local product list, so for any recipient it is not found. product-detail is also not guest-allowed, so a signed-out recipient is bounced to sign-in.
findings.why_costs_money: A seller sharing a product to IG/TikTok/SMS is the #1 acquisition path for an indie-brand marketplace, and every such tap dead-ends.
findings.fix: Redirect to /buyer-product-detail?productId=… (or /thread-product-detail). Keep /product-detail for the seller's own products only, by checking ownership before redirecting.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks share-driven sales; ~$3-8k/mo at target

findings.title: Category and Trending 'see all' pages are not guest-allowed
findings.problem: Discover's 'Shop by category' chips push /buyer-category, and 'See all' trending pushes /buyer-trending. Neither is in GUEST_TOP_LEVEL, and both only read public endpoints (api.publicDiscovery.*), so guests get bounced to sign-in.
findings.why_costs_money: These are the highest-intent browse taps on Discover, and guests lose them.
findings.fix: Add 'buyer-category' and 'buyer-trending' to GUEST_TOP_LEVEL. Both screens already use public APIs only.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo of guest browse sessions that currently dead-end

findings.title: Guest hosted checkout drops discount codes (doc claims fixed)
findings.problem: The signed-in hosted branch passes discountCode per group. The guest branch (api.guest.checkout.createSession) passes no discountCode, and routes/guest-checkout.ts does not read one. docs/payments/multi-store-cart.md says 'The hosted Stripe fallback loop … now passes each group its own code', which is true only for signed-in buyers.
findings.why_costs_money: Influencer and creator codes are the main traffic driver for indie brands. A guest who arrives from an IG code and sees no discount applied abandons the purchase or files a dispute.
findings.fix: Accept discountCode in POST /api/guest/checkout/session (reuse priceCartGroup/discount validation) and pass it from the guest branch.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo of code-driven guest orders

findings.title: Guest hosted checkout makes the buyer re-enter address and card on the Stripe page
findings.problem: The app collects contact (email AND phone required) plus full address, then opens Stripe Checkout with shipping_address_collection enabled and no prefilled shipping. The guest types the address a second time, then the card, in a separate browser. Per seller.
findings.why_costs_money: Double data entry is one of the top causes of mobile checkout abandonment, and guests are the least committed buyers.
findings.fix: Drop shipping_address_collection on the guest session (the address is already validated server-side and stored on checkoutSessions) or prefill it via customer + payment_intent_data.shipping. Better still, route guests through the in-app PaymentIntent path (checkout-intent.ts) with Apple Pay.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo guest conversion lift

findings.title: Guests never get native Apple Pay / Google Pay sheet
findings.problem: choosePaymentPath returns 'hosted' for !signedIn, so the in-app ExpressPay (PlatformPayButton with live shipping/tax re-pricing) is only offered to signed-in buyers. Guests, the users who most need one-tap pay, get a web redirect.
findings.why_costs_money: Apple Pay usually lifts mobile conversion significantly. Withholding it from guests wastes the guest-checkout investment.
findings.fix: Let the PaymentIntent route (routes/checkout-intent.ts) accept a guest email + guestAccessToken like guest-checkout.ts does, and allow in_app for guests in choosePaymentPath.

findings.title: Pre-orders, Thread Cash and loyalty force the per-seller hosted loop
findings.problem: hasPreOrder, threadCashApplied and loyaltyApplied each force path 'hosted' (separate Stripe Checkout per seller, browser redirect, no Apple Pay sheet), and this inherits the broken return URL above.
findings.why_costs_money: Drops/pre-orders are the brand-launch format, and Thread Cash is the retention hook. Both are pushed onto the worst-converting payment path.
findings.fix: Extend checkout-intent.ts to support held (transfer) charge plans and the Thread Cash/loyalty tokens, then remove those clauses from choosePaymentPath.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$2-5k/mo across drops + Thread Cash orders

findings.title: Imported products get a default variant with stock 0 (born sold out)
findings.problem: Bulk/CSV import inserts one default variant with stock: 0 and no size/color, so every imported product shows Sold Out (PDP inStock false) and hits the no-option bug above.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers onboarding via import (the fastest catalog path) launch with an entirely unbuyable catalog and do not know why.
findings.fix: Import the row's stock/quantity column (or default to a seller-set quantity), and show a post-import 'set inventory' prompt.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: seller catalog dead-on-arrival; indirect but large

findings.title: No Share button on the buyer product page
findings.problem: grep for 'Share' in buyer-product-detail.tsx finds nothing. Buyers cannot send a product to a friend; the only product share link in the app is the seller-side one (product-detail.tsx:241).
findings.why_costs_money: Word-of-mouth shares are free acquisition, and 'send to a friend for opinion' is a standard fashion purchase step. Cross-ref growth-loops.
findings.fix: Add a share icon in the PDP header that shares https://brandthread.app/store/product/{id} (after fixing the redirect), with referral code appended for signed-in buyers.

findings.title: PDP returns/cancellation policy is hardcoded, not the seller's actual policy
findings.problem: adaptApiProductToBuyerProduct hardcodes cancellationPolicy 'All sales final. Returns accepted only for damaged or incorrect items.' and refundPolicy 'Contact the seller within 7 days…' for every product, although users.return_policy / cancellation_policy exist and sellers edit them in store-policies/refund-policy screens.
findings.why_costs_money: 'All sales final' on every listing suppresses conversion for sellers who offer returns. For sellers who don't, it misstates their terms. Both cases create disputes.
findings.fix: Return the seller's returnPolicy/cancellationPolicy from GET /api/public/products/:id (public.ts:483) and render them, falling back to a neutral 'See seller's policy' link.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo conversion + dispute reduction

findings.title: Shop sheet shows placeholder 'Ships in 2-3 days' and 'Easy returns' / 'Fast shipping' to every buyer
findings.problem: SHIPPING_ESTIMATE_COPY is marked '// PLACEHOLDER' and shown on all products. The trust row hardcodes 'Easy returns' and 'Fast shipping', while the PDP for the same product says 'All sales final'. DEFAULT_RETURNS_COPY 'Free returns within 14 days' is shown when refundPolicy is empty.
findings.why_costs_money: Fabricated shipping/returns promises create chargebacks (item 'not as described') and FTC/consumer-protection exposure. Pre-orders show 'Ships in 2-3 days' too.
findings.fix: Additive: replace the constants with the seller's shipping-zone processingDays (shippingZones.processingDays) and the seller's returnPolicy from the product API, and hide the trust cues the seller hasn't earned.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: dispute/chargeback exposure; ~$500-1.5k/mo

findings.title: No shipping cost or estimated delivery date anywhere before checkout
findings.problem: The PDP has no shipping line. The cart computes calculateCartSummary(cart.items) with shippingTotalCents defaulting to 0, so it displays 'Shipping & fees $0.00' and 'Est. tax $0.00' with a footnote. The real shipping first appears on the checkout screen.
findings.why_costs_money: Unexpected shipping cost is the #1 cited reason for cart abandonment. Showing $0.00 and then a higher number is worse than showing nothing.
findings.fix: Additive: fetch fetchShippingRateDetails per seller group in the cart (already used by createCheckoutSession) and render 'Shipping from {seller}: $X / Free over $Y'. On the PDP, show a 'Shipping $X · Free over $Y · Arrives by {date}' line from the seller's zone.

findings.title: Delivery guarantee (15-day / 60-day auto-refund) is never shown before purchase
findings.problem: The guarantee line (guaranteeLine) only renders in DeliveryTrackerCard on buyer-order-detail, after payment. grep 'guarantee' finds nothing in buyer-product-detail, ShopProductSheet or components/checkout. BuyerProtectionNote quotes generic Terms text only.
findings.why_costs_money: 'Delivered in 15 days or automatic refund' is a strong trust signal for unknown indie brands, and it is unused at the moment of decision.
findings.fix: Add one line to BuyerProtectionNote and the checkout order summary: 'Delivered by {paid+15d} or automatic refund' ('60 days' for pre-orders).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo conversion lift on unknown-brand trust

findings.title: No post-delivery review request (push or email)
findings.problem: grep for review_request / 'leave a review' / 'how was your' across routes, lib and jobs finds nothing. The 'delivered' push says only 'Your order was delivered!'. The review form exists only inside buyer-order-detail behind status=delivered.
findings.why_costs_money: Without solicitation most products will have 0 reviews at launch, and new buyers see no social proof.
findings.fix: Add a job: N days after deliveredAt with no review, publishNotification type 'review_request' deep-linking to buyer-order-detail?id=…&review=1, plus an email.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo via social proof on repeat traffic

findings.title: Home 'For You' is chronological; the built ranking engine is never called
findings.problem: getThreadPostsPage('for-you') reads /api/public/posts ordered by createdAt desc. GET /api/feed/for-you (lib/ranking/forYou.ts, using style interests, not_interested, purchases) exists, and the client wrapper getForYouFeedPage exists, but no screen calls it (grep finds only its definition).
findings.why_costs_money: Onboarding collects style interests and brand likes, and the home feed ignores them. Relevance drives shop-clicks per session.
findings.fix: Additively, for signed-in buyers, use getForYouFeedPage as the first source in getThreadPostsPage 'for-you' mode, falling back to /public/posts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$2-4k/mo from higher shop-click rate

findings.title: Empty Home For You is a dead end ('No posts yet / Check back soon') with no CTA
findings.problem: When there are no seller posts (likely at launch with few sellers, since preview content is __DEV__-only: feed.tsx:2456), the For You empty state shows 'Check back soon for new drops' with no button. Only the Following tab gets a 'Find friends' CTA.
findings.why_costs_money: A new buyer whose first screen is empty churns immediately. Dev builds always look full, which hides this.
findings.fix: Add a 'Shop products' CTA to /(buyer)/discover and a 'Trending products' rail (api.publicDiscovery.trendingProducts) inside the empty state.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo day-1 retention

findings.title: Onboarding notifications 'Continue' does not request push permission
findings.problem: The 'Never miss what matters' soft-ask has Continue and Not now, but onEnable just calls transitionTo(SUCCESS). No OS prompt is ever shown. The first real prompt waits for a first order/follow/friend action.
findings.why_costs_money: A buyer who said yes gets no pushes. Abandoned-cart pushes (1h), price-drop, back-in-stock and drop alerts all depend on a token, so the re-engagement stack goes silent for most new buyers.
findings.fix: On Continue, call Notifications.requestPermissionsAsync() (the user opted in on the soft-ask), then register the token after onboarding completes. Keep Not now silent.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$2-3k/mo of push-driven recovery and repeat sales

findings.title: Add-to-cart is not a push-permission trigger, so abandoned-cart pushes miss first-time buyers
findings.problem: requestContextualPushPermission fires after order, follow and friend events, but not after add-to-cart. A first-time buyer who adds to bag and leaves has no push token, so the 1-hour abandoned-cart push goes to nobody and only the 24h email remains.
findings.why_costs_money: Cart-recovery push is one of the highest-ROI messages, and it is lost for exactly the buyers who haven't converted yet.
findings.fix: Call requestContextualPushPermission(userId, api) after a successful addToCart for signed-in onboarded buyers (it is already rate-limited to once per user).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo recovered carts

findings.title: Thread Cash at checkout is flag-off, and when on it forces hosted checkout and a single store
findings.problem: threadCashCheckoutDiscount defaults false, so buyers earn daily Thread Cash (ThreadCashActiveTimeTracker in (buyer)/_layout.tsx:162) but cannot spend it. When enabled it is single-store only ('Rewards need one store') and routes to the hosted path with the mobile:// return bug.
findings.why_costs_money: An earn-only currency with no spend path frustrates buyers, and the 'checkout credit' promise in the business model is not delivered at launch.
findings.fix: Complete the sign-off and flip the flag after fixing hosted return. Medium term, support Thread Cash on the in-app PaymentIntent path and split across stores.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: retention lever; ~$1-3k/mo repeat purchases

findings.title: Apple Pay depends on an unverified prod env key and merchant setup
findings.problem: The plugin config is correct (merchant.com.brandthread.mobile, enableGooglePay). But stripePaymentAvailable() silently returns false when EXPO_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is missing, and eas.json production sets no env (it relies on the EAS 'production' environment). If the key or the Apple merchant ID/Stripe Apple Pay cert (new LLC Stripe account) is missing, every signed-in buyer silently falls to hosted checkout with the broken return.
findings.why_costs_money: A silent fallback converts the best payment path into the worst one with no error.
findings.fix: Add a launch check: production build logs/Sentry-alerts when stripePaymentAvailable() is false, and confirm the merchant ID and Apple Pay certificate on the new Stripe account (docs/launch/dev-only-tasks.md).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: guards all in-app card revenue

findings.title: Seller verified badge dropped on PDP although API returns it
findings.problem: GET /public/products/:id returns sellerVerified, but adaptApiProductToBuyerProduct never copies it, and the seller card renders only name/initials. ShopProductSheet does show it (ShopProductSheet.tsx:1545,1615). sellerHandle is also hardcoded ''.
findings.why_costs_money: Identity-verified seller is a key trust cue for small brands, and it is missing on the page with the highest purchase intent.
findings.fix: Map row.sellerVerified into BuyerProduct and render the existing verified badge next to sellerName.

findings.title: No star rating / review count near the price; renderStars helper unused
findings.problem: renderStars() is defined but never called. Reviews render only at the bottom via ProductReviewsSection (hidden when 0). The public product payload has no avgRating/reviewCount, so grids and cards can't show stars either.
findings.why_costs_money: Above-the-fold ratings are one of the strongest PDP conversion levers, and buyers won't scroll past description/video to find them.
findings.fix: Add avgRating/reviewCount to GET /public/products/:id and list endpoints, and render '★ 4.6 (128)' under the price (tap scrolls to reviews).

findings.title: Size chart missing from Shop sheet (main buy surface)
findings.problem: The PDP renders the size chart table/image, but ShopProductSheet (the in-feed Shop sheet, where most Buy now taps happen) never references sizeChart or sizeChartImageUrl.
findings.why_costs_money: Size uncertainty is the top reason for apparel returns and abandonment, and buyers must leave the sheet to find it.
findings.fix: Add a 'Size guide' link next to the size chips in the sheet that opens the existing SizeChartViewer / image modal.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1k/mo + fewer returns

findings.title: Dev builds hide cold-start emptiness: all preview content is __DEV__-gated
findings.problem: FASHION_PREVIEW_POSTS, preview catalog and preview discover posts fill the UI whenever __DEV__ and the API returns little. In production none of this renders, which is correct, but every QA/demo run sees a full app.
findings.why_costs_money: The launch-day buyer experience (sparse catalog) is untested, and empty rails/feeds will ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Before launch, run a production-mode build against a near-empty staging DB and review every buyer surface. Also add a seller-seeding plan (minimum N live products) as a launch gate.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: risk control; prevents dead-app first impression

findings.title: No abandoned-checkout recovery for guests
findings.problem: The cart server sync requires auth, so guest carts live only in AsyncStorage and are never recoverable. Guest Stripe sessions capture email, but checkout.session.expired only releases loyalty, and after_expiration.recovery / a follow-up email is not used.
findings.why_costs_money: Guests who typed their email and then bailed are the cheapest recoverable revenue.
findings.fix: Set after_expiration.recovery on guest sessions and, on checkout.session.expired with guest metadata, send a 'complete your order' email with the recovery URL.

findings.title: Cart summary shows 'Shipping & fees $0.00' and 'Est. tax $0.00'
findings.problem: SummaryCard always receives shipping 0 and tax 0 (tax hardcoded 0 in calculateCartSummary), so the cart total equals the subtotal and the checkout total is higher.
findings.why_costs_money: A price jump between cart and pay screen breaks trust and causes drop-off.
findings.fix: Show 'Calculated at checkout' text instead of $0.00 when unknown, and show real per-seller shipping once fetched (see shipping finding).

findings.title: Klarna/Afterpay hidden on iOS/Android; on web only shown to buyers with saved cards
findings.problem: bnplAvailable = Platform.OS === 'web' && …, and the BNPL row renders only when savedCards.length > 0, so first-time buyers (no saved cards) never see it even on web. Native apps never offer BNPL.
findings.why_costs_money: BNPL lifts AOV and conversion on $100-500 fashion items, the price band in the catalog.
findings.fix: Show the BNPL row whenever the quote offers it (not gated on saved cards). Add Klarna/Afterpay via the Stripe RN SDK confirmPayment with the matching paymentMethodType on native.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo AOV lift

findings.title: Address autocomplete is auth-only and env-gated, so guests get none
findings.problem: /api/buyer/address-suggestions sits behind router.use(requireAuth) and returns 503 without GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, so guests (the users without saved addresses) type every field manually.
findings.why_costs_money: Manual address entry on mobile is slow and error-prone, which means abandonment and mis-deliveries (auto-refund cost).
findings.fix: Expose a rate-limited public variant (e.g. /api/guest/address-suggestions) and confirm GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is set in production env.

findings.title: Google Pay sheet total is pre-shipping/pre-tax estimate
findings.problem: googlePay.amount is amountCents before any address quote (only Apple Pay re-prices via onShippingContactSelected). The intent is then created for the quoted total, so the amount the buyer approved differs from the charge.
findings.why_costs_money: Mismatched amounts produce 'I was overcharged' disputes on Android and can violate Google Pay display rules.
findings.fix: Quote first from the default/saved address before opening Google Pay, or label the amount as an estimate and re-confirm.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: dispute risk; ~$200-500/mo

findings.title: Guest 'Track order' and 'View receipt' bounce to sign-in
findings.problem: After a guest pays, the pinned 'Track order' button pushes /buyer-order-detail, which is not guest-allowed (it uses authenticated buyer endpoints), so the guest's first post-purchase tap lands on a sign-in wall.
findings.why_costs_money: A confusing post-purchase moment produces 'where is my order' tickets and disputes, and the guest never builds a relationship with the app.
findings.fix: For guests, render the confirmation's own order summary and an 'Email me tracking' line, or add a token-authenticated guest order view (the guestAccessToken already exists).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-600/mo support/dispute cost

findings.title: Guest orders not linked to the account created afterwards
findings.problem: 'Create an account to track orders faster' goes to /sign-in, but no server code claims orders by orders.guest_email on signup (grep guestEmail shows only admin/email usage). The new account shows no orders, no review eligibility and no Thread Cash/referral credit.
findings.why_costs_money: The best guest-to-account conversion moment yields an empty account, and repeat-purchase loops (Buy again, reviews) never start.
findings.fix: On first sign-in with a verified email, attach orders where buyer_id IS NULL AND guest_email = email. Route the CTA to onboarding with returnTo.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1k/mo repeat purchases

findings.title: Sign-in wall from AuthGate drops returnTo; 'Create an account' drops it too
findings.problem: useSignInGate passes returnTo, but the AuthGate route-level redirect (router.replace('/sign-in')) does not. On sign-in, 'Create an account' replaces to /onboarding without carrying returnTo, so a guest who signs up from an action lands on the explainer and then Home, not the product.
findings.why_costs_money: Intent is lost at the exact moment the user commits to an account.
findings.fix: Pass returnTo=current path in the AuthGate redirect and forward it through onboarding (store in AsyncStorage and consume after thread-explainer).

findings.title: Cold open to paid order takes about 17 taps plus ~6s of forced animation for a new buyer
findings.screen: splash → onboarding → thread-explainer → feed → sheet → checkout
findings.problem: Path: splash (2.5s auto) → Welcome 'Get started' (1) → account type (2-3) → Apple sign-in (4-5) → name (6) → style (7) → sizes (8) → brands (9) → loading (~3.2s auto) → notifications (10) → success (11) → thread-explainer (12) → Home → Shop on post (13) → size (14) → Buy now (15) → Apple Pay (16) → confirm (17). The guest path is 1 tap (the 'Browse as a guest' ghost button) to Discover, but then hits the walls above.
findings.why_costs_money: Each extra pre-value step loses a share of installs. Style, sizes, brands, notifications, success and explainer are 6 screens before any product.
findings.fix: Additive: show 'Browse as a guest' as a secondary (not ghost) button, make Sizes and Notifications skippable in one tap, and merge Success with thread-explainer. Do not change existing screen styles.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo from install→first-session retention

findings.title: Search 'no results' state has no product fallback
findings.problem: No-results shows 'Try a different spelling' plus 'Clear search' only. No trending products, categories or 'request this' CTA (fuzzy pg_trgm search exists server-side: api-server/src/routes/public.ts:543-585).
findings.why_costs_money: Zero-result searches are high-intent sessions that end with nothing to buy.
findings.fix: Add a 'Trending now' DiscoveryProductGrid (api.publicDiscovery.trendingProducts) under the empty state, and log zero-result queries for sellers/waitlist-demand.

findings.title: Guest Profile and Inbox tabs hard-redirect to sign-in instead of an inline prompt
findings.problem: GUEST_BUYER_TABS excludes 'profile', 'inbox', 'orders', 'activity', so tapping those tab-bar slots as a guest replaces the whole navigator with /sign-in and throws away the browse stack. ('search' is listed but no (buyer)/search route exists.)
findings.why_costs_money: An abrupt wall on a tab tap reads as forced signup and makes users quit rather than convert.
findings.fix: Allow these tabs for guests and render an inline 'Sign in to see your orders/messages' card (existing EmptyState + requireSignIn).

findings.title: Out-of-stock / payment-unavailable sellers still let buyers fill the cart
findings.problem: When a seller's Stripe account isn't ready, the PDP says 'You can still add this item to your cart', and the cart then blocks checkout for the whole selection with an Alert ('Payments unavailable'). Guests skip the payment check entirely and fail at the hosted session (guest-checkout.ts:176-178).
findings.why_costs_money: Buyers invest effort and are then blocked late. Inactive-Connect sellers are a launch reality, since onboarding sellers lag.
findings.fix: Exclude payment-unready sellers from public listings (or label 'Not accepting orders yet' on cards), and in the cart only block that seller's group, not the full checkout.

findings.title: Back-in-stock waitlist and price-drop alerts require sign-in and push
findings.problem: Restock/price-drop notifications are wired server-side (good), but 'Notify me' requires an account and the delivery is in-app/push. Waitlisted buyers without push permission (see onboarding finding) only see an Activity row they won't open.
findings.why_costs_money: Restock alerts convert at very high rates, and delivery quality decides the revenue.
findings.fix: Add an email channel to notifyBackInStock/notifyPriceDrop, and allow a guest email for the waitlist.

findings.title: No buyer win-back / re-engagement job
findings.problem: Jobs exist for abandoned carts, drops, live reminders, seller trial and thread-cash expiry, but nothing targets lapsed buyers (no 'new from brands you follow' digest, no 7/30-day inactivity nudge). grep for winback/re-engage/inactive finds nothing buyer-facing.
findings.why_costs_money: Repeat purchase is where marketplace GMV compounds, and without nudges buyer retention decays to organic.
findings.fix: Add a weekly digest job: new products from followed sellers + saved-item price drops, via email (+push if granted), respecting notification prefs.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo repeat GMV

findings.title: Onboarding style interests are not used to personalize Home
findings.problem: buyer_style_interests and likedBrandIds feed only buyer-recommended-brands (the BrandsYouMightLikeRow on Discover). The Home feed (/api/public/posts) is identical for every buyer.
findings.why_costs_money: Buyers answer survey steps and see no payoff, which wastes the onboarding cost (6 screens).
findings.fix: Wire Home to /api/feed/for-you (see ranking finding), which already consumes these signals.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: covered by ranking finding

findings.title: Hosted-path multi-seller cart makes the buyer pay N separate times
findings.problem: In the hosted path (guests, pre-orders, rewards) the code loops deliveryGroups, opening a separate Stripe Checkout browser per seller. Any cancel mid-loop leaves a partially paid cart.
findings.why_costs_money: A cart with 3 brands means 3 card entries, and most buyers abandon after the first.
findings.fix: Route these cases to the one-PaymentIntent cart path (checkout-intent.ts) as noted above. Until then, show 'You'll pay each store separately (N payments)' before Pay.

findings.title: Inbox 'Message filters' is a coming-soon placeholder; story-create has dead controls
findings.problem: inbox shows snackbar 'Message filters — coming soon'. story-create has a Pressable with onPress={() => {}} and a 'More tools … coming soon' Alert.
findings.why_costs_money: Dead buttons read as unfinished, and App Review flags placeholder features (Guideline 2.1/2.2).
findings.fix: Hide these controls until implemented (additive conditional render).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: review-risk only

findings.title: Phone number mandatory for every checkout
findings.problem: contactPhone is required by client readiness and by the zod schemas of all three checkout routes. Apple/Google Pay also force PhoneNumber in required fields.
findings.why_costs_money: Each required field costs conversion, and privacy-sensitive buyers abandon at a phone requirement for a fashion purchase.
findings.fix: Make phone optional (still collected when the carrier requires it) in the schemas and readiness checks.

findings.title: Recently viewed is buried at the bottom of an infinite Discover list
findings.problem: RecentlyViewedRow is passed as ListFooterExtra of the For You grid (loads up to 120 posts), so it is effectively never seen. It is also on the cart page.
findings.why_costs_money: Recently-viewed is the cheapest repeat-visit conversion surface.
findings.fix: Render RecentlyViewedRow in the Discover header (after DiscoverFeaturedRail) for signed-in buyers with ≥1 item.

findings.title: Discover infinite scroll stops at 120 and refetches the whole list each page
findings.problem: onEndReached increments forYouLimit by 30 and refetches all rows via composeDiscoverPosts (limit grows to 120, then stops). The grid ends silently at 120 posts and each page re-downloads everything.
findings.why_costs_money: Browsing dead-ends for engaged buyers, and server/bandwidth cost scales quadratically per session.
findings.fix: Paginate with offset/cursor and append, and remove the 120 cap.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small; cost + engagement

findings.title: Feed 'See all' drops push the buyer into the seller (tabs) group
findings.problem: JustDroppedRailPage onSeeAll pushes '/(tabs)/following'. For signed-in buyers AuthGate then router.replace()s to /(buyer)/following (double navigation, back stack broken). For guests, (tabs) is protected, so it goes to sign-in.
findings.why_costs_money: A broken drop discovery path means fewer drop sales.
findings.fix: Push '/(buyer)/following' (or /buyer-drops, which is guest-allowed) when isBuyerSurface.

findings.title: Search, category and PDP have no currency/locale handling (US-only checkout)
findings.problem: Currency is hardcoded 'usd' everywhere. CardField countryCode is 'US', and Google Pay allowedCountryCodes is ['US'], while sellers can configure worldwide shipping zones (shippingZones.zoneType 'rest_of_world').
findings.why_costs_money: International buyers who find brands via social can see listings but cannot complete Google Pay with a non-US address, which confuses them and loses those sales.
findings.fix: For launch, explicitly label 'Ships to US only' when the buyer locale is non-US. Later, remove the Google Pay US restriction where the seller ships internationally.

findings.title: PDP fetches seller payment status only for signed-in buyers
findings.problem: api.buyer.sellerPaymentStatus is skipped when !isSignedIn, so guests see a normal Buy now and only learn at the hosted session that 'Seller payment account is not active'.
findings.why_costs_money: Late failure after the guest has filled in contact and address means a lost buyer.
findings.fix: Expose payment readiness on the public product payload (stripeAccountStatus === 'active' boolean) and use it for all viewers.

findings.title: Cart checkout re-validates and checks every seller sequentially before opening checkout
findings.problem: startCheckout awaits validateCart, then one sellerPaymentStatus call per seller in a for-loop, then createCheckoutSession, which fetches shipping per seller, all before navigation. Checkout then validates again (buyer-checkout.tsx:404-431).
findings.why_costs_money: Multi-second spinner on the Checkout tap, and latency at the commit moment reduces conversion.
findings.fix: Run payment-status checks in Promise.all, or navigate immediately and let checkout show per-seller issues inline (it already does).

findings.title: Saved-items 'Buy now' skips seller payment / vacation checks
findings.problem: buyer-saved Buy now creates a buy-now session and pushes /buyer-checkout with no sellerPaymentStatus or vacation check (PDP does both).
findings.why_costs_money: Failures surface late inside checkout, after the buyer has committed.
findings.fix: Reuse the PDP's handleBuyNow pre-checks (or route through thread-product-detail).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Production routing sends every root-level API page (/.well-known, /l, /bio, /g, /u) to the SPA
findings.problem: The API artifact only claims the path prefix "/api" while the mobile web artifact claims "/". The API mounts /.well-known/*, /u/:username, /l/:code, /bio/:slug(/go|/shop|/p), and /g/:code at the site root (app.ts), so on brandthread.app those requests reach mobile/server/serve.js. serve.js has no handlers for them, so they get the SPA shell (or a plain 404 for non-HTML requests). Integration tests use supertest against the API app directly, so they pass while production is broken.
findings.why_costs_money: Universal links, tracked short links, link-in-bio pages, and giveaway landings all depend on these routes, and every one of them is dead in production. That removes the main ways sellers can drive outside traffic to purchases.
findings.fix: Add the root paths to the API artifact's services.paths ("/.well-known", "/l", "/bio", "/g"), or add a small proxy in serve.js that forwards those prefixes to the API origin (SHARE_PREVIEW_API_BASE) before the SPA fallback. Add a deployed smoke test that curls brandthread.app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $5k-10k/mo: deep links, short links, bio pages, and giveaways are all off-platform acquisition, roughly 10-20% of GMV-driving traffic at the $50k target

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: apple-app-site-association/assetlinks unreachable and empty: universal links never verify
findings.problem: AASA is served by the API at /.well-known, which production routing never reaches (see the routing finding). Even if it were reachable, it returns details: [] unless APPLE_TEAM_ID is set, and assetlinks returns [] unless ANDROID_SHA256_CERT_FINGERPRINTS is set. Neither variable appears in .replit or any deployment config. iOS caches the AASA at install time, so a failed fetch at launch keeps links in Safari until the app is reinstalled or updated.
findings.why_costs_money: Every shared https link (product, post, profile, store, invite, drop) opens the website instead of the app, which drops buyers into a weaker web flow. Most social shares lose the in-app purchase path.
findings.fix: Fix the routing, set APPLE_TEAM_ID and ANDROID_SHA256_CERT_FINGERPRINTS on the deployment before the App Store build, and verify with Apple's AASA validator. Also consider writing static-build/.well-known/* in build-web.js so serve.js serves it directly.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $3k-6k/mo: a large share of link-driven installs and purchases fall back to web or stall

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Signed-out visitors on shared product links are bounced to splash/sign-in
findings.problem: store/product redirects to 'product-detail', and 'product-detail' is not in GUEST_TOP_LEVEL. A signed-out visitor (anyone who just installed the app, or any web visitor) is therefore forced to /splash or /sign-in, even though buyer-product-detail and guest checkout are guest-allowed.
findings.why_costs_money: Shared and advertised product links ask cold traffic for an account before they see the product, which kills conversion.
findings.fix: After pointing the redirect at buyer-product-detail (previous finding), the guest path works. Also add 'p', 'tag', 'place' and 'invite' to GUEST_TOP_LEVEL explicitly instead of relying on effect ordering.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Included in the product-link finding; guest conversion on product links goes to about zero

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Store share links (/store/{username}) return HTTP 404 with no preview
findings.problem: share-store.tsx and launch-publish.tsx share https://brandthread.app/store/{username}. The OG preview looks up storefronts.slug = {username}, but storefront slugs are generated as store-<random hex> (store.ts:813) or set to the Clerk owner id (seller-settings-route.ts:79), so they never match. The API returns 404, and sharePreview.js then serves the page with HTTP status 404 and robots noindex.
findings.why_costs_money: A seller's main store link shows no card on iMessage, Instagram, or Facebook and is marked not-found to crawlers. Sellers' own promotion of their store gets no click-through.
findings.fix: In share-preview.ts, resolve /stores/:slug by users.username first (seller name, avatar, bio) and fall back to storefronts.slug; never 404 a valid seller username.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $1k-3k/mo: store links are the main asset sellers post on their own socials

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Signed-out profile or store landing shows no products, only Sign in / Join
findings.problem: Signed-in visitors are forwarded to /seller-profile, but signed-out visitors stay on PublicProfileLanding ("no posts, no seller commerce data") with only Sign in and Join buttons. 'seller-profile' is already a guest-allowed route, so guests could browse and buy, but they are never sent there. Store links and creator ?aff links resolve here.
findings.why_costs_money: Cold traffic from a seller's Instagram bio, store link, or Meta ad (destinationUrl is this profile URL) hits a signup wall instead of products.
findings.fix: For accountType 'seller', also replace to /seller-profile?sellerId=... when signed out. Keep the landing only for buyer profiles.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $2k-5k/mo: every store link, creator link, and paid ad lands here
