findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Buyers have no entry point to the Invite / Give $10 Get $10 screen
findings.problem: /buyer-invite is only pushed from the seller Marketing tab, from the referral_joined activity (which only fires after a successful referral), and from the invite deep link when the user is already signed in. The buyer profile, buyer settings menu (Rewards, Thread Cash wallet), thread-cash.tsx and loyalty.tsx have no Invite row. loyalty.tsx:164 describes referrals with no button.
findings.why_costs_money: The business model limits referral rewards to buyers, but buyers cannot find the program, so the main buyer acquisition loop never starts.
findings.fix: Add an 'Invite friends, get $10' row to buyer-settings-menu, the buyer profile header, the thread-cash wallet, and the post-purchase success screen, all pushing /buyer-invite.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $2k-5k/mo: the referral loop is effectively off; even a k-factor of 0.1 at the target scale matters

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: *.brandthread.app store subdomains are advertised but never wired (no DNS, TLS, or host routing)
findings.problem: Sellers are told 'Your store will be live at https://{storeUrl}.brandthread.app', and the success screen has a 'View store' button that opens that URL. Nothing in the API or serve.js reads the Host header to resolve a storefront (grep for req.hostname/headers.host finds only the Clerk proxy), and there is no wildcard DNS or TLS config. The link fails to resolve.
findings.why_costs_money: The seller's first moment after publishing is a broken link. Sellers who print or share it lose all that traffic and lose trust in what they're paying for.
findings.fix: Until wildcard hosting exists, show and share the working URL (brandthread.app/u/{username}, or the storefront path) everywhere. Later, add wildcard DNS and TLS plus host-based storefront resolution in a front proxy.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Seller trust and churn risk; every shared subdomain link loses 100% of its clicks

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Tracked short links (brandthread.app/l/CODE) are dead in production
findings.problem: Sellers create UTM short links whose URL is `${getWebOrigin()}/l/${code}` = https://brandthread.app/l/CODE. /l/* is not routed to the API in production, so the link opens the SPA shell, which renders not-found. No click is recorded and no redirect happens.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers paste these into Instagram, TikTok, and influencer posts. Every click is lost and the growth-links analytics show zero, which makes the paid Marketing tools look broken.
findings.fix: Route /l/* to the API (see the routing finding) and add a post-deploy check that /l/<known code> returns 302.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $500-2k/mo of seller-driven traffic, plus seller retention

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Link-in-bio pages (brandthread.app/bio/slug) are dead in production
findings.problem: The server-rendered bio page and its /go, /shop and /p redirects are mounted at the API root, which production routing does not reach. The seller's 'Share page' shares a URL that shows the app's not-found screen.
findings.why_costs_money: Link-in-bio is the number-one link a creator brand puts on Instagram and TikTok, and it currently sends 100% of that traffic nowhere.
findings.fix: Route /bio/* to the API, and verify that /bio/<slug> returns 200 HTML after deploy.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $1k-3k/mo: bio link is the main IG/TikTok-to-store path

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Affiliate commissions are paid from Brandthread's balance, not the seller's
findings.problem: runCreatorPayout does stripe.transfers.create({destination: creator}) from the platform balance. Nothing in lib/money (fees.ts, cartTransfers.ts, checkoutPlan.ts) reduces the seller's transfer or application fee by the commission, and no reverse transfer or account debit recovers it from the seller. Sellers can set up to 50% commission (MAX_COMMISSION_BPS 5000, default 10%). The code comments say 'the seller is never charged more than the stated percentage', but the seller is never charged at all.
findings.why_costs_money: Each affiliate order pays the creator 10-50% of the subtotal while Brandthread earns only a 5% fee. That is a net loss of 5-45% of GMV on every creator sale, and creators are a growth channel, so the loss grows with success.
findings.fix: Fund commissions from the seller: add commission to application_fee_amount at checkout (or create a reverse transfer from the seller's connected account when the commission becomes payable) before enabling AFFILIATE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: At 20% of $1M GMV via creators at 10% commission: -$10k/mo net (only off while AFFILIATE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED is unset)

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: AASA path list omits /invite/*, /community-join, /live/* and /g/*
findings.problem: DEEP_LINK_PATHS covers /u, /c, /store, /drops, /p, /tag, /place, /onboarding* and /team-invite* only. The referral link https://brandthread.app/invite/CODE, community invites (/community-join?code=), live links (/live/{id}) and giveaway links (/g/CODE) are not claimed, so iOS always opens them in Safari even after the AASA is fixed.
findings.why_costs_money: The referral invite is the main buyer-acquisition loop. When it opens in a browser, the invitee signs up on the web or drops off instead of landing in the app with the code applied.
findings.fix: Add "/invite/*", "/community-join*", "/live/*" and "/g/*" to DEEP_LINK_PATHS, and add in-app routes for /live/[id] and /g/[code].
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $1k-2k/mo: referral conversion from link tap to signed-up buyer is likely cut by 30-50% without the in-app open

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: No deferred deep linking: invite or creator code lost when the app isn't installed
findings.problem: Referral (/invite/CODE) and creator (?aff=CODE) codes are only captured when the link opens the app or the web SPA, and stored in AsyncStorage or localStorage per surface. A user who taps the link, goes to the App Store, and installs gets a fresh app with no code. Grep for branch/appsflyer/adjust/installReferrer/clipboard handoff found nothing.
findings.why_costs_money: Most invitees do not have the app yet, so most referrals and creator conversions go unattributed. Inviters and creators then stop sharing because they don't get credit.
findings.fix: Add a lightweight deferred link: the web /invite page shows an Install button that copies the code (iOS pasteboard handoff with user consent) or passes it via the Play Install Referrer, and the onboarding referral field pre-fills from it. Alternatively, adopt Branch or Expo-compatible AppsFlyer.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $1k-3k/mo: 40-60% of referral and creator installs are unattributed, which suppresses loop growth

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: No seller-to-seller referral program (subscription credit) exists
findings.file: searched: grep -riE 'seller.?referral|refer a (brand|seller)|invite a brand|brand referral' artifacts/api-server/src artifacts/mobile/app artifacts/mobile/lib returned no matches
findings.problem: Seller subscriptions are the recurring revenue line, but nothing rewards a seller for bringing another brand (for example, a free month on both subscriptions). Seller invites only exist for team members and manufacturers.
findings.why_costs_money: Seller acquisition depends entirely on paid or organic channels. Brands talk to other brands, which makes this the cheapest seller-acquisition channel.
findings.fix: Add a seller invite code applied at plan selection that grants a Stripe or RevenueCat promotional free month to both sellers after the referred seller's first paid invoice. It can reuse the referrals table with a kind column.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $1k-4k/mo of subscription MRR at the target scale, if 10-20% of new sellers come by referral

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Product share preview image is a private /objects/ path, so cards have no photo
findings.problem: Product photos uploaded in-app are stored as '/objects/<id>' with ACL visibility 'private' (products.ts:98-101). GET /public/products/:id returns images unchanged, and sharePreview.js writes images[0] straight into og:image, which gives a relative, non-public URL. Crawlers drop it, so product cards show no photo. The same raw path breaks bio-page tiles (bioPage requires https) and email product images (render.ts requires https).
findings.why_costs_money: Product links without an image get far fewer clicks on iMessage, Instagram, Pinterest, and email. Cross-ref buyer-funnel if images also fail in-app.
findings.fix: Make product images public-read (or serve them via a public /api/v1/public/media/:id route) and return absolute https URLs from public product endpoints, the bio page, and the email renderer.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $500-2k/mo: rich previews and email images drive a large share of clicks

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Sitemap lists only 6 static pages: no products, stores, or profiles
findings.problem: sitemap.xml is written at build time from PUBLIC_ROUTES (/, privacy, terms, guidelines, seller-agreement, refund-policy). The per-store product sitemap endpoint (/api/product-seo/public/:storeSlug/sitemap) exists but is never referenced from the sitemap or robots.txt.
findings.why_costs_money: Google cannot discover any product, store, or profile page, so organic search acquisition is zero.
findings.fix: Serve a dynamic /sitemap.xml (sitemap index) from serve.js or the API that lists active public products (/store/product/:id), seller profiles (/u/:username), and drops, with lastmod.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $500-2k/mo of organic traffic within 3-6 months of launch

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Store URL shows a doubled domain (store-xxxx.brandthread.app.brandthread.app)
findings.problem: getStorefront sets settings.storeUrl = `${remote.slug}.brandthread.app`, and store-publish then renders `https://${storeUrl}.brandthread.app`, which produces https://store-ab12cd34.brandthread.app.brandthread.app.
findings.why_costs_money: It looks broken to sellers at the publish moment and the link is unusable.
findings.fix: Store only the bare subdomain in settings.storeUrl (drop the suffix in storeService:418), or strip a trailing .brandthread.app before rendering.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Seller trust and activation; part of the subdomain issue

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Subdomain 'Save' only writes AsyncStorage and marks itself verified
findings.problem: handleSaveSubdomain calls updateDomain(btDomain.id, { subdomain, verificationStatus: 'verified' }), which only mutates the local storefront in AsyncStorage. The server slug never changes, and the UI shows the subdomain as verified.
findings.why_costs_money: The seller believes they own a vanity URL that resolves nowhere, and support tickets and churn follow.
findings.fix: Add PATCH /api/store/slug (unique, validated, maybe default to the username) and call it. Never set verificationStatus client-side.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Seller retention; part of the subdomain issue

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Custom domain flow says 'verified and SSL is being issued', but no SSL or routing exists
findings.problem: The server only checks a TXT record and sets verified=true. No certificate is provisioned, no host maps to the storefront, and the 'www → cname.brandthread.app' target shown in the UI has no corresponding service. The success alert promises SSL issuance.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers point their real domain at a dead target and lose their existing site traffic. That is a direct churn and refund risk for a paid-tier feature.
findings.fix: Hide custom domains behind a feature flag until a TLS-terminating proxy (for example Cloudflare for SaaS or Caddy on-demand TLS) with host-to-storefront routing exists. Change the copy to 'Verified – connection coming soon'.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Refund and churn exposure on higher tiers if marketed as a plan perk

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Giveaway share link /g/CODE is dead and its landing has no image or install path
findings.problem: Giveaways share https://brandthread.app/g/CODE, which is unreachable (routing). Even when it is reachable, the landing has no og:image or twitter:card, and its only CTA is 'brandthread://giveaway?code=', which does nothing without the app (no App Store link or web fallback). 'giveaway' is also not a guest-allowed route, so a signed-out user is sent to sign-in and loses the giveaway.
findings.why_costs_money: Giveaways exist to acquire followers and buyers virally, and this loop is broken at every step.
findings.fix: Route /g/*, add og:image (the prize or seller image), add the giveaway route to guestRoutes with sign-in gating at the Enter action, and add an App Store link (EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL) and a universal link fallback.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-1k/mo of follower and buyer acquisition per active seller cohort

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Live stream shares use custom-scheme or exp:// URLs that don't unfurl or open for non-users
findings.problem: ExpoLinking.createURL('/live', ...) and createURL('/buyer-live', ...) produce brandthread://... in store builds and exp://... in Expo Go. These are not https, have no preview, and are not tappable in many apps (WhatsApp, Instagram DMs). People without the app cannot open them.
findings.why_costs_money: Live shopping depends on real-time sharing to pull viewers in. Broken share links mean smaller live audiences and fewer live sales.
findings.fix: Share https://brandthread.app/live/{streamId} (claim it in the AASA, add app/live/[id].tsx that redirects to buyer-live, and add an OG matcher showing the host and 'LIVE now').
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $500-1.5k/mo of live GMV

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Live feed shares brandthread.app/live/{id}, but no route exists
findings.problem: There is no app/live/[id].tsx, parseShareLink has no 'live' case, and the AASA does not claim /live. In the app and on the web, the link shows +not-found.
findings.why_costs_money: Every live share from the live feed is a dead link.
findings.fix: Add app/live/[streamId].tsx that redirects to /buyer-live?streamId= (guest-allowed), plus the AASA path and an OG matcher.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Included in the live share estimate

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Creator payouts are switched off: AFFILIATE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED isn't set anywhere
findings.problem: Payouts only run when AFFILIATE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=true. It is not in .replit userenv or any docs, so creators accrue 'owed' commissions that are never paid, and the UI says 'Payouts are not switched on yet.'
findings.why_costs_money: Creators who aren't paid stop promoting, which kills the affiliate loop. Turning it on before the funding fix creates the loss described in the previous finding.
findings.fix: Fix the funding first, then set the flag and document it in docs/launch. Until then, hide creator recruitment, or label it clearly as 'commissions paid starting <date>'.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Creator loop dormant; $500-2k/mo of creator-driven GMV forgone

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Creator Connect onboarding return URL points at /api-server/..., which 404s
findings.problem: refresh_url and return_url are https://brandthread.app/api-server/seller/connect/onboard/{refresh,return}. The API is mounted only at /api and /api/v1, and serve.js explicitly 404s /api-*. Seller Connect uses /api/seller/connect/onboard (connect.ts:71). A creator who finishes Stripe onboarding lands on a JSON 404 page.
findings.why_costs_money: Creators abandon payout setup and so never get paid or keep promoting.
findings.fix: Use `${getWebOrigin()}/api/seller/connect/onboard` (same as connect.ts), or a creator-specific return route that deep-links back to /creator-program.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $200-800/mo; blocks every creator payout account

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Creator link targets /u/{brand}?aff=, so cold traffic sees a sign-up wall
findings.problem: Creator share links land on the signed-out profile landing (no products, Sign in/Join). Products aren't visible until the visitor creates an account, and there is no product-specific creator link (the shareLink only takes a brand).
findings.why_costs_money: Influencer traffic is the coldest and highest-volume traffic. A sign-up wall before any product converts poorly.
findings.fix: Send creator links to the guest-browsable seller profile or a product, and let creators generate product-level links (/store/product/{id}?aff=CODE).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-1k/mo of creator GMV

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Seller Meta CAPI events are recorded under the BUYER's id, not the seller
findings.problem: POST /meta-ads/conversion-events uses sellerId(req) = the caller's clerkUserId. The caller is the buyer (buyer-product-detail and buyer-checkout call trackAndRelayConversionEvent), so the row is stored with the buyer as sellerId and loadConnectedAccount(buyer) finds no pixel. The product's seller never receives ViewContent or Purchase events. The route also requireAuth's, so guest web visitors' events get a 401.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers running Meta ads through Brandthread get no conversion signal, Meta cannot optimize for purchases, and ROAS looks like zero. Sellers stop spending and churn from the ads feature.
findings.fix: Resolve sellerId from productId (products.ownerId) or the order. Allow unauthenticated calls with rate limiting, and include hashed em/external_id when consented.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $500-2k/mo of seller ad-driven GMV, plus retention of sellers who run ads

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Meta ads always land on the seller profile, even for product ads
findings.problem: destinationUrl = storeUrl = /u/{username} for every promoteKind, with a code comment claiming 'Brandthread has no dedicated public product page route', which is untrue (/store/product/{id} exists). No UTM parameters are appended. Ad clicks hit the signed-out profile landing with no products.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers pay Meta for clicks that land on a sign-up wall, so ROAS is near zero and sellers churn from the paid feature.
findings.fix: For promoteKind 'product', use buildProductUrl(promoteRefId) (after fixing the product route). Append utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=paid&utm_campaign=<campaign id>.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $500-2k/mo of seller ad GMV

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Email marketing: product tiles link only to the storefront and are unlinked if it's unpublished
findings.problem: Every product card's href is the store home (/api/store/site/slug), and only when the storefront is published. Otherwise the cards have no link at all. Links carry no utm_source=email or campaign id, and product images must be https (but uploads are /objects/ paths), so they render as grey boxes.
findings.why_costs_money: Email is the best repeat-purchase channel, and here it can't link to a product or be attributed.
findings.fix: Link each card to buildProductUrl(id) with utm_source=brandthread_email&utm_campaign=<campaignId>, and resolve images to public https.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $500-1.5k/mo of repeat GMV

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Web storefront URL is under /api/store/site/... and not linked from any in-app share
findings.problem: The only web page where a non-app buyer can browse a full store and check out is /api/store/site/:slug. Share Store, Launch, and the profile all share /store/{username} (an app route) instead, so web buyers never reach the working web checkout from a shared link.
findings.why_costs_money: Web visitors (Instagram in-app browser, desktop) can't buy from the link sellers share.
findings.fix: Make /store/{username} on web resolve to the published storefront (serve.js proxy, or redirect in sharePreview when a published storefront exists), and give storefronts a clean public path.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $500-2k/mo of web GMV (IG/TikTok in-app browsers ignore universal links)

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Android App Links intent filter claims the whole domain with no path filter
findings.problem: The Android intentFilter has autoVerify on host brandthread.app and www with no pathPrefix/pathPattern. Once verified, every brandthread.app URL opens the app, including /bio/*, /l/* short links, /account-deletion, /privacy and /api/store/site/* storefronts. The app has no routes for these and shows +not-found.
findings.why_costs_money: Android buyers who tap a seller's link-in-bio, short link, or web storefront get a not-found screen in the app instead of the page.
findings.fix: Replace the bare host entries with pathPrefix entries that mirror DEEP_LINK_PATHS (/u/, /c/, /store/, /drops/, /p/, /tag/, /place/, /invite/, /team-invite, /community-join, /onboarding).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-800/mo: Android share of bio, short-link, and storefront traffic dead-ends

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Seller Marketing tab promotes buyer Thread Cash referrals to sellers
findings.problem: Sellers see 'Invite and earn – Give $10, get $10 Thread Cash' and land on the buyer referral screen. The rewards code does not check account type, so sellers earn Thread Cash for invites. The owner's model says referral rewards are for buyers only.
findings.why_costs_money: Platform-funded Thread Cash goes to sellers, who can recruit their own customers through it, at $10 per invite. Meanwhile there is no seller-acquisition referral at all.
findings.fix: Replace the seller card with a seller-to-seller referral (next finding), and gate inviter rewards in applyReferralCode/qualify to buyer accounts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $200-1k/mo of unintended Thread Cash spend; cross-ref thread-cash-referrals-abuse

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Invite and community links render the generic homepage card in iMessage
findings.problem: The share-preview MATCHERS have no entry for /invite/:code, /community-join, /live/*, /g/*, or /bio/*. A referral link renders 'Brandthread | Discover what's next' instead of '<Name> invited you – get $10 to spend'.
findings.why_costs_money: A personalized, money-forward unfurl roughly doubles link click-through. The generic card wastes every invite sent.
findings.fix: Add an /invite/:code matcher that calls GET /api/v1/referrals/invite/:code (extend it to return the inviter's display name and avatar) and renders '<Name> sent you $10 on Brandthread' with a branded OG image.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-1k/mo: higher invite tap-through

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Product preview lacks og:type product, price tags, and JSON-LD Product schema
findings.problem: Every preview is og:type 'website' with no product:price:amount/currency, availability, or schema.org Product/Offer JSON-LD. Only the homepage has Organization/WebSite JSON-LD. WEB_DEPLOYMENT.md says the build generates JSON-LD, but that is only true for the static routes.
findings.why_costs_money: There are no Google Shopping free listings, Pinterest rich pins, or price-in-card on Facebook and iMessage, which are free acquisition channels for product search.
findings.fix: In the /store/product matcher, emit og:type=product, product:price:amount/currency, and a <script type=application/ld+json> Product with an Offer (price, availability, seller name, image).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-1.5k/mo of free organic shopping traffic

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: robots.txt disallows /api/, which blocks the only real web storefront from crawlers
findings.problem: The published storefront that can actually check out on web lives at /api/store/site/:slug, and short links, bio Shop buttons, and emails point there. robots.txt has 'Disallow: /api/', so Google never indexes any seller storefront.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers paying for Brandthread get no SEO for their storefront, which weakens the 'website builder' value of the subscription.
findings.fix: Serve storefronts at a public non-/api path (for example /s/:slug, proxied to the API) and allow it in robots, or add 'Allow: /api/store/site/' before the Disallow.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-1k/mo of storefront organic traffic, plus seller retention

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Published storefront page has no OG, Twitter, canonical, or JSON-LD tags
findings.problem: buildPreviewHtml only emits <title> and meta description from seo.metaTitle/metaDescription. There is no og:image, og:title, canonical, or Product/Store JSON-LD. The 'social image' the seller uploads in store-seo.tsx (socialImageUri) is never synced to the server (storeService.ts:454-460 omits it).
findings.why_costs_money: Storefront links shared on Instagram or iMessage unfurl as bare URLs, and the seller's social-image setting does nothing.
findings.fix: Sync socialImageUri in saveStorefront and add og:title/description/image/url, a twitter:card, a canonical, and Store/ItemList JSON-LD to the storefront head.

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Server landings use custom-scheme-only CTAs with no App Store fallback
findings.problem: The 'Open in Brandthread' buttons are brandthread://u/... and brandthread://giveaway..., and nothing links to the App Store or Play Store. Grep for apps.apple.com finds only landing-page.js, which is gated on EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL. There is also no apple-itunes-app Smart App Banner meta in +html.tsx or build-web.js.
findings.why_costs_money: Web visitors without the app have no path to install, so web-to-app conversion is lost.
findings.fix: Add <meta name="apple-itunes-app" content="app-id=..., app-argument=<url>"> to the SPA shell and server landings, and an App Store button using the store URL env var.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-1k/mo of web-to-app installs

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Affiliate attribution requires sign-in, so guest web checkouts never credit creators
findings.problem: The ?aff code is attached to an account only via POST /affiliate/attach (signed in). Guest checkout (web storefront, SPA guest checkout) records UTM and tracked-link attribution but never the affiliate code, so creators get no commission on guest orders.
findings.why_costs_money: Creators see clicks without commissions and stop promoting.
findings.fix: Pass the pending aff code in the guest checkout body and record an affiliate attribution keyed by checkout session or email, then commission it in the webhook the same way as signed-in orders.

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Pixel and CAPI tracking never fires on iOS/Android
findings.problem: consentGranted is only set by setMarketingPixelConsent, which _layout calls only when Platform.OS === 'web'. On native, trackAndRelayConversionEvent returns false immediately, so no CAPI relay happens for in-app purchases, which is where most GMV is. NSPrivacyTracking is false and there is no ATT prompt. That is correct for privacy, but it means no attribution path exists for native.
findings.why_costs_money: Neither Brandthread nor sellers can measure or optimize paid acquisition for the app.
findings.fix: Send server-side, non-tracking CAPI events (no IDFA, first-party only, disclosed in the privacy policy) from the order webhook for sellers with a connected pixel, keyed by productId's seller, independent of the client.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-1.5k/mo of ad efficiency

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Meta Ads integration is env-gated and needs Meta App Review (ads_management)
findings.problem: OAuth requires META_APP_ID, META_REDIRECT_URI and META_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET, none of which are in .replit. Ads management on other businesses' ad accounts requires Advanced Access through Meta App Review and Business Verification, which can take weeks.
findings.why_costs_money: If this is marketed at launch, sellers hit a non-working connect flow.
findings.fix: Start Meta Business Verification and App Review now, or hide the Meta Ads entry behind a feature flag until it is approved.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Feature unavailable at launch; seller trust risk

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Tracked-link and UTM attribution only works for web storefront guest checkout
findings.problem: recordCheckoutAttribution is only called by guest-checkout, using window.__btAttribution from the server storefront page. Short links whose destination is a product (/store/product/:id?utm..&bt_link) open the SPA or app, which never reads or forwards UTM or link codes into native or SPA checkout.
findings.why_costs_money: The growth-links revenue column reads $0 for most links, so sellers can't see which campaigns sell and churn from Marketing tools.
findings.fix: Capture utm_* and the link-code param in the SPA and app (like AffiliateRefCapture), persist for 7 days, and send them with buyer-checkout and checkout-intent so the webhook writes checkout_attributions.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Seller retention for paid tiers; indirect

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: No install or signup source attribution: users have no acquisition-source field
findings.problem: UTM parameters are recognized on the landing page (MARKETING_PARAMS) but discarded. Onboarding does not record utm, referrer, invite, or creator source on the user, and there is no SKAdNetwork, AdServices, or Play Install Referrer handling.
findings.why_costs_money: With no idea which channel produced paying sellers or repeat buyers, launch marketing spend can't be allocated toward the $50k target.
findings.fix: Persist first-touch utm, referrer, and code in storage on first open and on web, then send them with /auth/onboarding/complete into a users.acquisition jsonb column. Add Apple AdServices token capture for Search Ads.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect; misallocated acquisition spend

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Analytics has no share, invite, or referral events, and funnel events are never fired
findings.problem: ANALYTICS_EVENTS has no share, invite_sent, referral_applied, or deep_link_opened events. add_to_cart, checkout_started, follow, onboarding_completed, seller_onboarding_completed and product_published are defined but never tracked (grep for track( only finds app_opened, post_viewed, product_viewed, signup_started and signup_completed).
findings.why_costs_money: Viral coefficient and funnel conversion can't be measured, so broken loops like the ones in this file go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add share(kind, surface), invite_link_opened, referral_applied, and deep_link_opened(kind) events, and call the existing funnel events at their sites.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect; enables loop tuning

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Buyer shares (profile, post, collection) carry no referral code
findings.problem: Referral credit only flows through the dedicated /invite/CODE link. Every other share a buyer sends (posts, collections, profile QR) has no ?ref=CODE, and 'ref' is treated as an ignored marketing parameter.
findings.why_costs_money: Organic shares are far more frequent than deliberate invites. Each one is a missed referral attribution and a reason the inviter isn't rewarded.
findings.fix: Append ?ref=<inviteCode> to the build*Url helpers for signed-in buyers. Capture ref in a component like AffiliateRefCapture and pre-fill the onboarding referralCode.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $300-1k/mo of additional attributed referrals

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Contacts-based find-friends is off by default and has no 'invite non-members' path
findings.problem: The screen requires EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_SYNC_ENABLED and CONTACT_SYNC_ENABLED, both default off. Even when on, it only matches existing members to follow. There is no SMS invite with the referral link for contacts who aren't members.
findings.why_costs_money: The highest-converting invite channel (SMS to contacts) isn't used.
findings.fix: Add an 'Invite' row for unmatched contacts that opens sms: with the invite link. This is privacy-safe because it uses the device composer and nothing is uploaded.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $200-800/mo of referral volume

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Emails, bio pages, and storefronts have no 'Powered by Brandthread' seller-acquisition link
findings.problem: Only the bio page footer has 'Made with Brandthread', and it is unlinked to any signup or UTM. Marketing emails and storefront pages carry no Brandthread attribution, so seller-generated traffic never advertises Brandthread to other brands.
findings.why_costs_money: The Shopify/Linktree-style 'powered by' loop is free seller acquisition, and it is missing.
findings.fix: Add a small 'Sell with Brandthread' footer link to emails, storefronts, and the bio page, pointing to https://brandthread.app/?utm_source=powered_by&utm_medium=<surface>&ref=<sellerCode>.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $200-1k/mo of seller subscription MRR

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Product and store SEO editors save fields that no page renders
findings.problem: The product-seo route admits that no per-product page exists, so product SEO titles and handles are never rendered. The editor previews 'brandthread.app › products › handle' and the store editor previews 'brandthread.app/{storeUrl}', and neither URL exists.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers spend effort on, and are sold on, SEO that has no effect. That is a churn and trust risk for a paid feature.
findings.fix: Use the resolved product SEO in the /store/product share-preview matcher (title and description) and in the canonical, and change the preview URL to the real /store/product/{id}.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Seller retention; $200-500/mo

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Storefront slug can be the seller's Clerk user id in public URLs and emails
findings.problem: If the seller saves policies before the storefront exists, the upsert inserts slug = owner_id (user_xxx). The public storefront URL, short-link redirects, and email 'shop' links then expose /api/store/site/user_2abc....
findings.why_costs_money: It produces ugly, untrustworthy links in buyer-facing emails and ads and leaks an internal id.
findings.fix: Use the same store-<hex> generator (or the username) in the policies upsert.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: <$100/mo, trust and hygiene

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Seller-provided Meta/TikTok pixels only load on the /api/store/site storefront
findings.problem: store_pixels are injected only into the server-rendered storefront. The pages where buyers actually land from shares and ads (SPA /u/, /store/product/, the in-app PDP) never load the seller's pixel.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers' retargeting audiences and conversion tracking miss most traffic, so their ads underperform and they spend less.
findings.fix: Inject the owning seller's pixel on SPA product and profile routes (web, consent-gated), and send server CAPI on orders for sellers with pixels.

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Buyer QR code encodes the bare homepage when the user has no username, and never the invite
findings.problem: The QR falls back to 'https://brandthread.app' and never includes the buyer's invite code, so scanning in person gives no referral.
findings.why_costs_money: In-person word of mouth isn't attributed or rewarded.
findings.fix: Encode https://brandthread.app/invite/<code> (or /u/<username>?ref=<code>).

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Invite share sends the link twice on iOS and relies on server text on Android
findings.problem: The server shareText already ends with 'tap: <link>', and the client also passes url: invite.link. On iOS, Messages and WhatsApp receive both the text with the link and the url attachment, so the link appears twice or as two bubbles. The demo shareText (buyer-invite.tsx:54) has no link at all.
findings.why_costs_money: The invite message looks spammy, which lowers acceptance.
findings.fix: Pass url only on iOS with a message that omits the link, or message only (with the link) on Android, as invite-manufacturer.tsx:107 does.

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Web export is single-page: /privacy etc. are served with canonical '/' and homepage meta
findings.problem: web.output is 'single', so only index.html is exported and addCanonicalMetadata's per-route metadata never applies. Every SPA path that isn't a share-preview match (including /privacy, /terms, /invite/X, /onboarding) is served with canonical https://brandthread.app/, homepage title, robots index,follow, and Organization JSON-LD.
findings.why_costs_money: Sitemap pages are canonicalized to the homepage (duplicate content), and invite pages index as the homepage.
findings.fix: In serve.js, rewrite the canonical, og:url and title per path, or switch to output 'static' for the legal routes.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: <$200/mo SEO

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Dead brandthread.app links still in the app (/changelog, /chat, /help)
findings.problem: brandthread.app/changelog and /chat have no page (docs/review-readiness/prod-hygiene.md:102,105 flagged /chat on the Help screen as fixed, but design-canvas still opens it). /help is unverified. All of them fall to the SPA not-found screen.
findings.why_costs_money: Broken links in the app are a reviewer red flag and look unfinished to paying sellers.
findings.fix: Point Live Chat in design-canvas to the support form route, and drop or replace changelog. Add /help as a real page or point it at in-app help.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: <$100/mo; review-risk only

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: API-side /u/:username profileLanding is dead code that diverges from the SPA
findings.problem: The API renders its own signed-out /u/:username landing with a custom-scheme CTA, but in production /u/* goes to the SPA (with OG injected by serve.js). Two implementations of the same URL can drift, and this one has no og:image.
findings.why_costs_money: Maintenance confusion; if routing is changed to send root paths to the API, this would shadow the SPA profile page and its guest browsing.
findings.fix: When fixing the root routing, exclude /u/* (keep it on the SPA), or delete profileLanding.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Negligible directly; prevents a regression

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Docs claim subdomains open in a web view and product previews work; code disagrees
findings.problem: README §7 says '{store}.brandthread.app links open in-app via a web view today' (nothing serves them) and §8 says product, profile, and drop share links 'now render a real preview' (the product link target is the seller screen and the image is a private path). wellKnown.ts references docs/launch/README.md at the repo root, which doesn't exist; the doc lives at artifacts/mobile/docs/launch/README.md.
findings.why_costs_money: False 'done' status means these gaps ship at launch.
findings.fix: Correct the docs and add these items to docs/launch/dev-only-tasks.md with owners.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Invite-only mode ignores member referral codes, which stalls the referral loop if enabled
findings.problem: If inviteOnlySignup is turned on for launch, an invitee holding a friend's /invite/CODE is still asked for an admin access code ('Member referral codes never unlock access').
findings.why_costs_money: Turning on scarcity mode would block the organic referral loop exactly when it should compound.
findings.fix: Let a valid member referral code also satisfy the access gate (optionally limited to N per member).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Only matters if the flag is enabled; then it blocks all referral signups

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: Community invite links have no OG preview and no AASA path
findings.problem: https://brandthread.app/community-join?code=... opens in the browser on iOS and unfurls as the generic homepage card.
findings.why_costs_money: Community growth (brand fan groups) brings repeat buyers, and these invites convert poorly.
findings.fix: Add '/community-join*' to DEEP_LINK_PATHS and a matcher rendering the community name and cover image.

findings.area_label: Growth loops: referrals, links, web, SEO, affiliates
findings.title: brandthread-woven is a design-system artifact, not a web storefront
findings.problem: brandthread-woven is kind='design-system' with no production service. Web buying depends only on the Expo web SPA and the API-rendered /api/store/site pages, both of which have the gaps listed above.
findings.why_costs_money: There is no fallback web storefront to rely on at launch.
findings.fix: No new artifact is needed. Prioritize fixing the SPA product, profile, and store guest flows and the storefront path.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Informational

findings.title: DM voice/video calls are fully simulated in production (fake 'connected' call)
findings.problem: CallSessionContext hard-wires `createPreviewCallProvider()` for every build. The phone/video buttons in every buyer and seller DM are not gated, 'ring' for 2.2s, then 'auto-connect' with no audio, video or signaling. The fake peer even 'turns their camera off' after 4s. REVIEW_NOTES.md:36 points reviewers straight at this feature.
findings.why_costs_money: A reviewer who taps Call sees a fake connected call with no media. That is a 2.1/2.3.1 rejection for a non-functional, misleading feature, and the whole launch slips.
findings.fix: Hide both call buttons in production unless a real Agora provider is wired (`IS_PROD_NATIVE && !agoraCallProvider` → hide), and remove 'Calls' from REVIEW_NOTES.md until it works.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all revenue (rejection delays launch; each week of slip is about $12k at target)

findings.title: No native iOS build has ever been configured: `eas init` never run, no projectId
findings.problem: app.json has no `extra.eas.projectId` or `owner`, so app.config.js never sets `updates.url` (OTA is off) and `Notifications.getExpoPushTokenAsync()` is called with no projectId (lib/contextualPushPermission.ts:27). That points to no EAS iOS build ever having been produced from this repo. REVIEW_READINESS.md:68-69 confirms nothing was verified on a device.
findings.why_costs_money: With 22 days left and no beta, the first native build will surface signing, extension, pod and new-architecture failures at the last moment. Push tokens will not register either, so sellers never hear about orders.
findings.fix: This week, run `eas init`, commit the projectId, run an EAS production iOS build, and install it via internal TestFlight (internal testers skip review, so this is not a 'beta').
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all revenue

findings.title: Live Activity widget extension not declared for EAS credentials
findings.problem: The plugin adds an app-extension target `com.brandthread.mobile.UploadLiveActivity` with an App Group. app.json has no `extra.eas.build.experimental.ios.appExtensions` entry, so EAS will not create a provisioning profile for the extension and the App Group is never registered.
findings.why_costs_money: The first store build is likely to fail at code signing, and it would only surface days before submission.
findings.fix: Add the appExtensions block (targetName, bundleIdentifier, entitlements with the App Group), or drop the plugin from the 1.0 build if Live Activities are not essential.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all revenue if build fails

findings.title: 'Featured on Discover' digital promotion sold via Stripe Checkout on native iOS
findings.problem: Unlike Boost and Create-ad, the Featured slot purchase has no RevenueCat/IAP branch. It always opens Stripe Checkout in `WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync`, and it is reachable from the Boost screen.
findings.why_costs_money: Paying for in-app visibility is a digital good, so guideline 3.1.1 requires IAP and a reviewer on the seller account will reject. (Cross-ref subscription-iap.)
findings.fix: On native, hide the Featured entry, or route it through RevenueCat consumables like boost.tsx:755.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all revenue (rejection)

findings.title: Reviewer notes template admits Boost is a non-IAP digital purchase
findings.problem: The 'Review notes' block meant to be pasted into App Store Connect says Boost/ad promotion is 'currently Stripe Checkout… a digital, in-app-consumed feature… please flag if this blocks'. It conflicts with REVIEW_NOTES.md, the newer file.
findings.why_costs_money: Pasting it all but guarantees a 3.1.1 rejection, and it signals to Apple that the team knew.
findings.fix: Delete that paragraph and the TestFlight note. Keep a single source (REVIEW_NOTES.md).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all revenue (rejection)

findings.title: Legal docs still carry placeholder entity/address and IS_DRAFT=true; doc claims PASS
findings.problem: LEGAL_CONTACT.operator is '[LEGAL ENTITY NAME]' and the address is '[REGISTERED POSTAL ADDRESS]', with IS_DRAFT = true. Terms and Privacy name 'Brandthread, Inc.', but the business is Dev's LLC. The governing-law, venue and liability-cap sections are only [LAWYER REVIEW] notes, which are stripped, so the shipped Terms have an empty 'disputes and governing law' section. app-store-readiness.md row 14 claims 'PASS'.
findings.why_costs_money: Contracts that name the wrong legal entity weaken enforcement of the 5% fee, seller subscriptions and chargeback terms. They also won't match the App Store seller name or the Stripe account holder, which can trigger 5.1.1 privacy-policy and Stripe KYC questions.
findings.fix: Replace 'Brandthread, Inc.' with the LLC's legal name and address, fill in governing law and the liability cap, set IS_DRAFT=false, and get counsel sign-off before submission.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks launch (legal/merchant entity mismatch)

findings.title: OAuth-only users (Apple/Google) can only delete via emailed code that depends on Resend + Apple relay
findings.problem: Accounts without a password must enter a 6-digit code emailed through Resend. Without RESEND_API_KEY/MAIL_FROM the server returns MAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED. For 'Hide My Email' SIWA users the mail reaches them only if the sending domain is registered with Apple's Private Email Relay, and that step appears nowhere in docs (grep 'privaterelay' finds only a test).
findings.why_costs_money: A reviewer who signs up with Apple and tries to delete never gets the code, so in-app deletion appears broken. That is a 5.1.1(v) rejection.
findings.fix: Register the mail-from domain in Apple Developer → Sign in with Apple for Email Communication, and add the step to dev-only-tasks.md. Also let SIWA users re-authenticate by re-running SIWA instead of email.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks launch (rejection)

findings.title: iPad support on with untested layouts; checklist depends on TestFlight that won't happen
findings.problem: `supportsTablet: true`, and iPad allows all 4 orientations plus Split View. Every sign-off box in the iPad checklist is unchecked, and 35 files read `Dimensions.get` at module scope, so layouts go stale on rotate or resize. The checklist itself says to test 'with the TestFlight build', but there's no beta plan. Store iPad screenshots are stretched phone web renders.
findings.why_costs_money: Apple reviews on iPad. Broken iPad layouts are a common 2.1/4.0 rejection, and iPad support can't be removed after release.
findings.fix: For 1.0, set `supportsTablet: false` (the app then runs in iPhone compatibility mode on iPad and still gets reviewed there), and add proper iPad support in 1.1 after testing.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk; blocks launch

findings.title: eas.json submit config still placeholders
findings.problem: `appleId`, `ascAppId` and `appleTeamId` are all REPLACE_WITH_*, and `verify:submit-config` fails right now.
findings.why_costs_money: `eas submit` can't upload the build.
findings.fix: Fill them in once the App Store Connect record exists, and commit.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks launch until done

findings.title: Store Analytics screen always errors; seller dashboard links to it
findings.problem: `getStoreAnalytics()` unconditionally throws 'Store analytics are not available yet'. The screen shows 'Couldn't load store analytics' with a Retry button that never works. The dashboard's Traffic-sources 'See all' and source rows open it. `getMarketingAnalytics` throws the same way (analytics-marketing.tsx:112).
findings.why_costs_money: A reviewer on the demo seller account hits a permanent error screen, which counts as a 2.1 bug. Sellers also lose trust in the paid tool.
findings.fix: Point 'See all' to an existing working analytics screen, or render a real empty state. Remove the unreachable analytics-marketing/store routes.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo (seller churn and rejection risk)

findings.title: Apple Sign-In token is never revoked on account deletion
findings.problem: Grepping for appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke finds nothing. Deletion only schedules a purge 30 days out, then calls `clerkClient.users.deleteUser`. No code calls Apple's REST revoke endpoint, and whether Clerk revokes it is unverified. REVIEW_READINESS row 2 lists this as still open.
findings.why_costs_money: Apple's 5.1.1(v) guidance requires revoking SIWA tokens on deletion. Reviewers test SIWA plus deletion together, so this is a rejection risk.
findings.fix: Confirm in Clerk docs/support that deleteUser revokes Apple tokens. If it doesn't, call Apple's /auth/revoke with the stored refresh token when deletion is scheduled.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk → launch slip

findings.title: Demo reviewer accounts can't delete themselves (seeded open orders block deletion)
findings.problem: The seed gives the demo buyer a paid 'processing' order and a 'shipped' order, and the demo seller owns them. getDeletionBlockers returns `buyer_orders_awaiting_shipment` and `seller_open_orders`, so DELETE /api/auth/account returns 409 'Settle the items below'. REVIEW_NOTES still tells reviewers deletion works from Settings.
findings.why_costs_money: Apple reviewers routinely test deletion on the provided account. A blocked deletion reads as 'deletion not available', which is a 5.1.1(v) rejection.
findings.fix: Mark seeded demo orders as delivered or cancelled, or exempt review accounts from blockers. Better still, tell reviewers in notes to create a fresh account to test deletion.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk

findings.title: Moderators are never alerted to new reports; '24h' SLA promised to Apple and users
findings.problem: POST /api/reports only inserts a row. Grepping for notify/email/push/Slack finds no moderator alert. The SLA exists only as an 'overdue' count in the admin queue that someone must open. Terms and review notes promise action within 24 hours.
findings.why_costs_money: Under guideline 1.2, Apple can pull the app if objectionable content reported during review sits unactioned. Unhandled scam reports also drive chargebacks.
findings.fix: On report insert, send an email or push to every moderator (or a safety@ mailbox or Slack webhook). Add an hourly job that escalates reports older than 12h.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection/takedown risk

findings.title: Image/video moderation silently disabled unless Replit OpenAI integration env is present
findings.problem: `mediaModerationEnabled()` returns false unless AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_BASE_URL and AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_API_KEY are set. Images and video frames then get verdict 'skipped' with no alert. Review notes claim automatic screening.
findings.why_costs_money: Nudity or violence in posts, products and stories goes unfiltered on a 13+ commerce app. That is a 1.2 takedown risk.
findings.fix: Treat moderation as required in production: fail readiness when it's disabled in NODE_ENV=production, or log at error level. Set the env in production.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: takedown risk

findings.title: API server crashes at boot without Replit-specific AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_BASE_URL
findings.problem: The OpenAI client module throws at import if AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_BASE_URL or AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_API_KEY is missing, and four modules import it statically. env.ts lists the key as 'optional'. REVIEW_READINESS.md:51 says 'or OPENAI_API_KEY', which isn't enough.
findings.why_costs_money: If production is hosted anywhere but a Replit deployment with the integration, the whole API fails to start, and the reviewer sees a dead backend.
findings.fix: Make the import lazy (as mediaModeration does) or accept OPENAI_API_KEY with a default base URL, and move the vars to REQUIRED in env.ts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: blocks all revenue if hit

findings.title: User DMs to AI 'Brandthread Agent' sent to OpenAI with no explicit consent
findings.problem: Every user is auto-given an AI agent conversation by the onboarding welcome hook, and their messages and history go to OpenAI (`gpt-5.4-mini`). Grepping for consent/opt-in finds no prompt; only the privacy policy mentions 'AI providers'. The same applies to AI studio tools.
findings.why_costs_money: Guideline 5.1.2(i) (2025 update) requires clearly disclosing third-party AI sharing and getting explicit permission. Without it, expect a rejection.
findings.fix: Before the first agent message or first AI tool use, show a one-time consent sheet ('Your messages are sent to OpenAI to generate replies') and store the acceptance.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk

findings.title: Privacy labels say search history not collected; server logs every query with userId
findings.problem: `db.insert(searchLog).values({ userId: viewerId, query, normalized })` stores each signed-in search linked to the account. privacy-labels.md says search queries 'are not stored on the server', and NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeSearchHistory is missing from app.json. search_log is also never purged on deletion.
findings.why_costs_money: Inaccurate privacy labels are grounds for rejection or removal under 5.1.2 and an FTC exposure.
findings.fix: Either drop userId from search_log, or declare Search History (linked, App Functionality) in the manifest, labels and verifier, and purge it on deletion.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk

findings.title: Support URL undefined; brandthread.app/help is behind the sign-in wall
findings.problem: PUBLIC_SCREENS covers only privacy, terms, community-guidelines, seller-agreement and refund-policy. 'help' is neither public nor a guest route, so a signed-out visitor to https://brandthread.app/help is redirected to /splash or /sign-in. The in-app 'Contact' button opens that URL in the external browser, where the user isn't signed in. No Support URL is chosen in any doc.
findings.why_costs_money: App Store Connect requires a Support URL that shows contact info. A login wall there is a 1.5 rejection, and buyers with order problems can't reach support, which turns into chargebacks.
findings.fix: Add 'help' (or a static /support page with the email) to PUBLIC_SCREENS and use it as the Support URL. Point help.tsx:222 to mailto or the in-app form.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk + chargebacks

findings.title: Sentry crash reporting off by default; only crash signal with no beta
findings.problem: Sentry is a no-op unless EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN is set, and the docs call it 'optional'. Server SENTRY_DSN is also optional (env.ts:53).
findings.why_costs_money: With no TestFlight cohort, launch-day crashes in checkout or onboarding would be invisible, and every crash is a lost sale or seller.
findings.fix: Make the DSN mandatory for the production EAS env (fail the verify script if it's missing) and set alerting.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-5k/mo of undetected checkout/onboarding failures

findings.title: Agora not configured = Go Live broken, yet review notes tell reviewer to Go Live
findings.problem: AGORA_APP_ID/AGORA_APP_CERTIFICATE are 'optional' env vars, and REVIEW_NOTES directs the reviewer to 'Go live with the seller account'.
findings.why_costs_money: If they're unset in production, the advertised feature fails during review (2.1).
findings.fix: Add Agora to required production env, or remove live from the review notes and hide Go Live when it's unavailable.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk

findings.title: Clerk new-device verification may block reviewer password sign-in
findings.problem: Review notes promise the demo accounts 'need no email or SMS code'. Clerk production instances can require an email code when a password sign-in comes from a new device ('Client Trust'), and the reviewer can't read the demo mailbox. Nothing in the repo disables or verifies this.
findings.why_costs_money: If the reviewer can't sign in, the result is a 2.1 'unable to sign in' rejection.
findings.fix: In the Clerk production dashboard, disable new-device verification, or use a demo email inbox the team can monitor. Test a sign-in from a fresh device.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk

findings.title: expo-updates enabled but no update URL; OTA hotfix path for launch week absent
findings.problem: `updates.enabled` is true, but `updates.url` is only derived from the missing projectId, so the first store binary can't receive OTA fixes even after projectId is added later (the URL is baked in at build time).
findings.why_costs_money: With no beta, OTA is the only same-day fix path for a launch-week JS crash in checkout. Without it, every fix waits 1-3 days in review.
findings.fix: Run `eas init` before the first store build so the binary carries the URL, and verify with `pnpm run update:production` on the production channel.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: days of downtime on any launch bug

findings.title: Deletion screen doesn't tell subscribers to cancel App Store subscription
findings.problem: The screen never mentions subscriptions (grep 'subscription' finds no matches), even though sellers pay an auto-renewing RevenueCat/StoreKit plan. Apple keeps billing after account deletion.
findings.why_costs_money: Apple's deletion guidance asks apps with auto-renewing subscriptions to explain that billing continues and how to cancel. Deleted sellers who keep being charged file refund requests and chargebacks.
findings.fix: For sellers with an active entitlement, add a notice with a 'Manage subscription' link (`Linking.openURL('https://apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions')`).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-500/mo in refunds/complaints

findings.title: Account purge leaves community messages, live comments, Q&A, freelancer and AI data
findings.problem: purgeAccount deletes DMs, posts and comments, but never touches community_messages, live_comments, product_questions, story_question_answers, giveaway_entries, freelancers/freelancer_jobs, design_studio_*, ai_generated_media, manufacturer_messages or search_log. Uploaded media objects in storage are never removed either. The deletion screen promises that 'posts, comments and messages will be permanently deleted' (delete-account.tsx:343).
findings.why_costs_money: Promising deletion and keeping the data breaks 5.1.1(v) and GDPR/CCPA. It means regulatory exposure and a possible rejection if probed.
findings.fix: Add DELETE/anonymize statements for these tables plus an object-storage cleanup job, and add a test that lists every table with a user_id column.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: regulatory exposure; low direct $

findings.title: No moderator account provisioning step in launch docs
findings.problem: requireModerator checks users.role in the DB. No dev-only task covers promoting Dev's account to moderator/admin in production, and invite-only.md also assumes moderator access.
findings.why_costs_money: Without a moderator nobody can resolve reports, and the 1.2 obligation fails on day 1.
findings.fix: Add a step: set `users.role='admin'` for the owner account in production and confirm /admin-reports loads.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection/takedown risk

findings.title: Invite-only mode would lock reviewers out; no code in review notes
findings.problem: If Dev turns on `inviteOnlySignup`, any new account (SIWA or Google, which reviewers often create) is routed to /access-code with a waitlist. REVIEW_NOTES has no invite code.
findings.why_costs_money: A reviewer stuck at an invite wall gets a 2.1 rejection, and invite-only also caps sign-ups.
findings.fix: Keep the flag off for launch, or put a multi-use reviewer code in the notes.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk if enabled

findings.title: Stale app-store-readiness.md: Boost FAIL now partially fixed, filter 'missing', 17+ rating
findings.problem: Row 5 says there's no automated content filter, but contentModerator.ts exists. Row 10 says Boost uses Stripe, but there's now an IAP path behind a flag. Row 14 claims the legal text is placeholder-free, which is false. The metadata doc recommends '17+', a tier Apple replaced with 13+/16+/18+.
findings.why_costs_money: The team can make go/no-go decisions on wrong data.
findings.fix: Rewrite readiness as one current checklist. Answer the new age-rating questionnaire (UGC, messaging, live video and AI likely mean 16+ or 18+), and reconcile it with the 13+ in-app age gate.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: indirect

findings.title: Age rating vs in-app 13+ gate mismatch
findings.problem: The app admits 13-17 year-olds (only under-13 is blocked, and under-18 can't sell). The planned store rating is 17+/18+. If it's rated 18+, minors still use DMs, live and stranger messaging with no extra protections.
findings.why_costs_money: Apple rejects ratings that don't match content, and child-safety failures are the fastest takedown path.
findings.fix: Pick 16+ or 18+ honestly in the new questionnaire. If minors are allowed, restrict adult-to-minor DMs and default minors to private.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: takedown risk

findings.title: Thread Cash pays users for 7 minutes of app time — guideline 3.2.2(x) risk
findings.problem: A daily monetary credit for 420s of foreground time is compensation for 'using the app'. Guideline 3.2.2(x) forbids requiring users to take actions such as watching or engaging in order to receive monetary compensation. The current review notes don't explain the reward.
findings.why_costs_money: A rejection or forced removal of the buyer-retention mechanic Dev is paying for.
findings.fix: Explain in review notes that it's a loyalty credit redeemable only for physical goods, and avoid the wording 'earn by using the app'. Have a fallback (daily check-in or purchase-based credit) ready behind a flag.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection risk; retention loop at stake

findings.title: Story composer 'More tools' button just says 'coming soon'
findings.problem: The `...` button opens Alert 'Additional tools are coming soon.'
findings.why_costs_money: A placeholder in a core creation flow is a 2.1 risk.
findings.fix: Remove the button.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection-risk polish

findings.title: Seller 'Customer privacy' setting opens a 'Not available yet' page
findings.problem: The settings catalog lists 'Customer privacy' for sellers, and the screen just says 'Not available yet'. customer-events is the same.
findings.why_costs_money: Dead-end settings look unfinished to the reviewer and to sellers paying for a plan.
findings.fix: Remove the catalog row and route until the feature is built.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: rejection-risk polish

findings.title: Instagram Stories share uses bundle-style appId, not a Facebook App ID
findings.problem: `appId: 'com.brandthread.app'`. Instagram Stories sharing requires a registered Facebook App ID, and this string doesn't even match the bundle id.
findings.why_costs_money: Sharing to IG Stories, the main free acquisition loop for fashion sellers, fails silently. (Cross-ref growth-loops.)
findings.fix: Register a Meta app and use its numeric App ID.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo of lost referral traffic

findings.title: Product listings (seller UGC) not run through text/image moderation
findings.problem: Grepping for moderation imports shows posts, comments, reviews, communities, live and profiles are screened, but products.ts is not. Product titles, descriptions and photos are public UGC.
findings.why_costs_money: Prohibited or explicit listings stay up until reported, which risks 1.2 and Stripe's restricted-business rules.
findings.fix: Run screenMedia/moderateText on product create/update and hold flagged listings for review.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Stripe/App Store risk

findings.title: No startup/perf budget for 357 routes / 162k-line app with eager native routes
findings.problem: Async routes are enabled only for the web export. Native bundles all ~357 screens (design-canvas.tsx alone is 6.1k lines), plus Skia, Agora and Stripe. No measured cold-start time on a real device exists in docs, and images are never resized server-side (hardening-report.md:261-269, still open).
findings.why_costs_money: Slow cold start and heavy full-res images on mid-range iPhones hurt first-session conversion, and 2.4 watchdog kills at launch are rejections.
findings.fix: Measure cold start on an iPhone 12-class device with the first build. Add a sharp resize pipeline on upload.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo conversion

findings.title: Privacy labels doc says birthday never sent; DOB is POSTed to /api/auth/age
findings.problem: Onboarding sends dateOfBirth to the server, which reduces it to an age band and stores `users.ageBand`. The labels doc says the birthday 'is never sent to Brandthread'.
findings.why_costs_money: A small label inaccuracy and a minor review risk.
findings.fix: Correct the doc. The age band is derived data, but say it's sent and immediately discarded.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: negligible

findings.title: Taxes & duties screen shows two 'Not available yet' cards
findings.problem: Tax-inclusive pricing and DDP duties render as 'Not available yet' cards.
findings.why_costs_money: These are honest, but they look incomplete to the reviewer, and international sellers can't offer DDP.
findings.fix: Collapse them into a single info line ('Prices are tax-exclusive; international orders ship DAP').
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small

findings.title: General settings 'Change log' links to nonexistent brandthread.app/changelog
findings.problem: The row opens https://brandthread.app/changelog, which has no page and redirects to sign-in on web.
findings.why_costs_money: A broken link is a 2.1 polish issue.
findings.fix: Remove the row.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: negligible

findings.title: Server never enforces Terms acceptance before UGC
findings.problem: Terms consent is client-side only (a checkbox in onboarding). Nothing on the server (posts, comments, communities, onboarding/complete) checks `termsAcceptedAt`, so an older client or an OAuth path that skips the checkbox can post UGC without agreeing.
findings.why_costs_money: Guideline 1.2 needs EULA agreement before UGC. This is a low but real risk, and it also weakens enforcement of fees.
findings.fix: Reject POST /auth/onboarding/complete (and UGC routes) when termsVersion is null.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small

findings.title: Product Q&A, freelancer profiles/reviews are public UGC but not reportable
findings.problem: REPORT_TARGET_TYPES omits product_question, freelancer and freelancer_review, yet these are public user text.
findings.why_costs_money: A reviewer looking for a 'report' option on Q&A won't find one (1.2).
findings.fix: Add the target types and a Report action to those surfaces.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small

findings.title: Contacts permission string promises 'never uploaded or stored' but opt-in stores hashes
findings.problem: The NSContactsUsageDescription says the contact list 'is never uploaded or stored'. Hashes of contacts are uploaded to /api/social/contacts/match, and the user's own hashes are stored on opt-in.
findings.why_costs_money: Misleading purpose strings are a 5.1.1(ii) rejection risk if the feature flag is on during review.
findings.fix: Reword to 'Contacts are converted to scrambled codes on your phone; only those codes are sent to find matches and are not kept.'
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small

findings.title: Physical-goods checkout untestable by reviewer (live Stripe keys, no test path)
findings.problem: Reviewers are told test cards are rejected and that they can 'open the checkout… without paying'. Apple sometimes asks for a complete purchase flow to verify that the IAP-vs-3.1.3 split is correct.
findings.why_costs_money: A possible 2.1 'could not complete purchase' follow-up delays approval.
findings.fix: Seed a 100%-off discount code or a $0.50 product for the reviewer, and say so in the notes.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: small delay risk

findings.title: Starter sellers' Home dashboard always fails: it calls Growth-only manufacturer API
findings.problem: loadSecondaryData runs orders, inventory, quote requests, sample orders and GET /api/manufacturers/threads in one Promise.all. GET /manufacturers/threads requires requirePlan('growth'), so on Starter it returns 403 and the whole Promise.all rejects. Every Starter seller gets 'Some dashboard data couldn't load' permanently, and loses recent orders, the 'orders to ship', low stock and returns counts, and top products.
findings.why_costs_money: Starter is the entry tier most new sellers pick. The first screen they see after every open looks broken and hides orders to ship, which leads to late shipments, delivery-deadline auto-refunds and churn in the trial.
findings.fix: Use Promise.allSettled for the hub calls (or skip the manufacturer calls when plan < growth) so a 403 on one optional tile never wipes out the order and inventory tiles.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$2-5k/mo: if 30-50% of ~400 sellers are on Starter at $29 and even 15% churn in the trial over a broken home screen, plus refunds from missed shipments

findings.title: Package presets API is never mounted, so saved box sizes silently fail
findings.problem: packagePresetsRouter is imported at index.ts:153 but no router.use('/package-presets', ...) exists, so every /api/package-presets call returns 404. fulfill-order swallows the list error (.catch(() => [])) and creating a preset fails. Only the integration test mounts the router itself.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers have to type package dimensions on every label. Repeat shipping friction is a top reason small sellers leave marketplaces, and wrong typed weights cause carrier adjustments.
findings.fix: Add router.use('/package-presets', packagePresetsRouter) next to /shipping-labels (the router already applies requireAuth and teamContext itself).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1k/mo in reduced fulfillment churn and fewer mis-weighted labels

findings.title: Bulk 'Print labels' buys the cheapest label for a hard-coded 1 lb box, falling back to the buyer's address as sender
findings.problem: handlePrintLabels quotes every order at weight 1, 10x8x4 and buys the cheapest rate with no confirmation step and no total cost shown. fromAddress falls back to order.customer.shippingAddress, so a seller with no from-address buys labels that ship from the buyer to the buyer. Only the first label is shared (line 92); the others must be opened one by one.
findings.why_costs_money: Under-declared weights cause carrier adjustments billed to Brandthread's Shippo account. Wrong-origin labels are wasted spend plus a refund. Bulk shipping is the feature that keeps volume sellers, and right now it is risky.
findings.fix: Require a from-address and a chosen package preset (or each product's weight from parcel-suggestion) before buying. Show a confirm sheet with the total cost. Merge the label PDFs into one file to print.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-1.5k/mo in carrier adjustments and wasted labels at a few thousand labels/mo

findings.title: Shippo carrier adjustments are not handled, so the platform absorbs re-weigh charges
findings.problem: All labels are bought through Brandthread's single Shippo account (Replit connector 'shippo', not a seller account). The label price is taken from order funds at purchase, but there is no handling of carrier adjustments or invoices: the webhook handles tracking only and no-ops on other events. Carrier surcharges for wrong weight or size land on Brandthread.
findings.why_costs_money: Re-weigh adjustments are a well-known cost leak on platform-owned label accounts. Combined with the 1 lb default in batch fulfillment, every heavy package costs Brandthread money.
findings.fix: Ingest Shippo invoices/adjustments (or poll the transactions API) and recover the adjustment from the seller's balance through the existing recoverLabelCost path, with an in-app notice.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-1k/mo assuming 3-10% of labels get a $3-8 adjustment

findings.title: Sellers get no notification when a buyer leaves a review
findings.problem: POST /api/reviews inserts the review and returns. There is no publishNotification or email (reviews.ts never imports notifications-feed). Replies at :336 don't notify the buyer either. The notification-type list has no new_review type.
findings.why_costs_money: Bad reviews go unanswered and good ones go unshared. Fast replies to reviews protect conversion, and a 'You got a 5-star review' push is one of the strongest reasons sellers re-open the app.
findings.fix: After the insert, call publishNotification({userId: sellerId, category:'reviews', type:'review_received', targetType:'review'}). Add the matching buyer notification on seller reply.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1k/mo through better seller engagement and review-driven conversion

findings.title: Failed payouts are silent: payout.failed is not handled
findings.problem: The Stripe webhook switch handles payout.paid (payout_sent push plus email) but has no case for payout.failed or payout.canceled. A grep for payout.failed / payout_failed finds nothing.
findings.why_costs_money: A seller whose bank rejects a payout believes they were paid until they check. 'Where is my money' is the top churn and support-cost trigger in marketplaces, and it blocks the next payout.
findings.fix: Handle payout.failed: notify the seller (push and email) with failure_code, link to payout-setup, and log it on the payout row.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo in support cost and churn among affected sellers

findings.title: No new-order email to sellers; order alerts are push or in-app only
findings.problem: On a paid order, sellers get only publishNotification (in-app plus push). brandthreadEmail has buyer order confirmation, shipping, return and payout emails, but no seller 'You have a new order' email.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers with push off, a reinstalled app or a backgrounded token miss orders. Missed orders hit the delivery-deadline auto-refund (lost GMV and commission) and are the main 'this app doesn't work' churn reason.
findings.fix: Add sendSellerNewOrderEmail(order) next to sendOrderConfirmationForOrder, respecting notification prefs (new_orders), with a digest option for high-volume sellers.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2k/mo: about 1-2% of GMV auto-refunded for missed orders at ~$500k GMV is $5-10k GMV, plus commission and churn

findings.title: No weekly performance summary for sellers
findings.problem: The jobs folder has abandoned cart, trial reminder, dispute, live reminders and similar jobs, but nothing that sends sellers a weekly recap (sales, views, top product, orders to ship, payouts). A grep for weekly/digest/summary in jobs and lib turns up only payout-schedule weekly anchors.
findings.why_costs_money: A weekly 'you made $X with Brandthread' email is the cheapest way to justify a subscription and catch quiet sellers before they cancel. Without it, sellers with slow weeks just churn.
findings.fix: Add jobs/sellerWeeklySummary.ts (Monday 9am local) that reuses lib/sellerSnapshot.ts and analytics home numbers. Send through brandthreadEmail plus one push, with an extra 'zero sales: try these 3 things' version.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo: a 1-3 point cut in monthly seller churn on ~$25k subscription MRR

findings.title: No churn defenses: no cancel survey, pause plan, downgrade offer or win-back
findings.problem: 'Manage or cancel subscription' opens the Stripe portal or the App Store URL directly. There is no reason prompt, no 'downgrade to Starter instead', no 'pause for a month' (useful with vacation mode) and no win-back job. A grep for cancel survey, pause_collection or winback finds nothing; automation.tsx even advertises win-backs as 'coming'.
