findings.why_costs_money: Save flows usually keep 10-20% of would-be cancellers. With no data on why sellers leave, the product can't fix it.
findings.fix: Before opening the portal or App Store link, show a one-screen reason picker with a downgrade or pause offer, and log the reason server-side. For Stripe subscribers, offer pause_collection.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-2.5k/mo if 10-20% of ~$10k/mo of gross cancellations are saved

findings.title: More > Customers opens a dead 'Not configurable' screen; the real customer list is unreachable
findings.problem: The Operations menu item 'Customers - Browse your customer list' routes to /customer-accounts, a placeholder that says 'Not configurable from the app'. The working customers.tsx (and customer-orders) has no inbound navigation except a back-fallback.
findings.why_costs_money: A customer list (repeat buyers, top spenders) is a core reason to keep paying for a seller tool, and right now it looks missing.
findings.fix: Change the More route to '/customers'. Delete or hide customer-accounts, customer-events and customer-privacy (all 'not available' placeholders).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-500/mo in perceived value and retention

findings.title: Mobile App Builder is a fake Pro feature with a dead CTA
findings.problem: The screen promises a 'drag-and-drop' branded iOS/Android app, native checkout and one-tap App Store publishing, with a 'Pro' badge. The CTA TouchableOpacity has no onPress and there is no backend. No inbound links exist, but it is registered as a route and deep-linkable.
findings.why_costs_money: Advertising a feature that doesn't exist is an App Store 2.1/2.3 rejection risk and a false-advertising problem if it is ever surfaced as a Pro perk.
findings.fix: Delete the screen and its Stack.Screen entry (or replace it with nothing). Don't market it in plans.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks launch if a reviewer reaches it; otherwise $0

findings.title: Seller marketing emails share the auth MAIL_FROM sender, so one spammy seller can block OTP and password-reset email
findings.problem: sendRawEmail sends seller campaigns from `${fromName} <${mailFromAddress()}>`, the same address and domain as auth, OTP, password reset, order and payout emails. Complaint and bounce reputation from any seller's campaign lands on the transactional sender.
findings.why_costs_money: If the domain gets throttled or blocklisted, sign-up verification and password resets fail for every user, which hits sign-up conversion across the whole platform.
findings.fix: Send marketing from a separate subdomain (for example news.brandthread.app, MARKETING_MAIL_FROM env) on its own Resend domain or IP pool, and keep MAIL_FROM for transactional mail only.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Tail risk: a blocklist event could stall sign-ups for days (tens of % of a month's new sellers)

findings.title: Email marketing is not tier-gated, and the 1,000/day/seller cap means Starter can cost about as much as it pays
findings.problem: /marketing/email has no requirePlan. Every seller, including an unpaid 'starter' fallback, can send up to EMAIL_DAILY_SEND_CAP (default 1000) emails a day. That is about 30k a month, roughly $25-30 of Resend volume, the same as the $29 Starter price.
findings.why_costs_money: This is unbounded per-seller variable cost, and the strongest marketing upgrade lever is given away free.
findings.fix: Add per-plan monthly caps (for example Starter 500, Growth 10k, Pro 50k) in sender.ts via getVerifiedPlanAccess, and send PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED to the upsell modal.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-2k/mo between capped Resend cost and upgrade pull

findings.title: Email audience can only grow from a web-store form; there is no opt-in in app checkout or follow
findings.problem: The audience docs say recipients come only from email_subscribers and that checkout has no opt-in box. subscribeEmail is called only from the public web store form (/api/public/stores/:slug/subscribe). In-app buyers, the main channel, can never join a seller's list.
findings.why_costs_money: The email marketing feature (compose, results, settings, audience) sends to near-empty lists, so it can't drive repeat sales or justify a paid tier.
findings.fix: Add a 'Get emails from {store}' consent checkbox at checkout and on Follow that calls subscribeEmail with source 'checkout' or 'follow' (unchecked by default).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo GMV-driven commission from repeat-purchase campaigns, plus upgrade value

findings.title: Boosts are Pro-only while ad campaigns, featured slots and Meta ads are open to all
findings.problem: /boosts and boost IAP verify use requirePlan('pro'), so Starter and Growth sellers can't pay to boost. /ad-campaigns, /featured-slots and /meta-ads have no plan gate, and plans.tsx markets 'Boost and promotion management' as Pro-only. The rules are inconsistent and block one paid product.
findings.why_costs_money: Boosts are pay-per-use ad revenue. Most sellers (Starter/Growth) are the ones who most need reach and can't buy it, so a high-margin line is left unsold.
findings.fix: Let every paying tier buy boosts (remove requirePlan('pro') from /boosts). Make Pro's perk a discount or bonus reach on boosts, and line up plans.tsx copy with the server rules.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-4k/mo if 10-20% of 300 non-Pro sellers spend ~$30-60/mo on boosts

findings.title: Live selling is Pro-only ($199), so the live feed will be empty at launch
findings.problem: Starting, ending, tagging products, pinning and scheduling lives all need requirePlan('pro'). At launch few sellers will be on $199, so buyers will mostly see an empty Live surface.
findings.why_costs_money: Live shopping converts very well, but only with supply. Limiting it to the smallest tier makes the buyer-side feature look dead and loses live GMV and commission.
findings.fix: Move live hosting to Growth with a monthly minutes cap (for example 4h on Growth, unlimited on Pro), metered from live session durations, to control Agora cost.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$1-3k/mo in commission on extra live GMV, plus upgrades from Starter to Growth

findings.title: Go Live and Boost show a generic error on PLAN_REQUIRED instead of an upgrade prompt
findings.problem: When the server returns 403 PLAN_REQUIRED, seller-go-live shows Alert 'Could not start live' and boost shows Alert 'Error'. Neither uses getEntitlementRejection or PlanUpsellModal (used only in team, manufacturer, tech-pack and analytics-customers/cohorts). There is no client pre-check, so sellers fill in the whole form before hitting the wall.
findings.why_costs_money: The moment a seller wants a paid feature is the best moment to upsell, and right now it reads as a bug.
findings.fix: Check useSubscriptionPlan on entry and show a locked state, and on 403 use getEntitlementRejection to open PlanUpsellModal with requiredPlan set.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-2k/mo in upgrades at the moment of intent

findings.title: Giveaway rules template lacks the Apple disclaimer required by App Store 5.3
findings.problem: The rules template says 'not sponsored, endorsed or administered by Brandthread', but it never says Apple is not a sponsor or involved. Guideline 5.3.3 requires that for in-app sweepstakes. The seller can also edit the rules freely and remove disclaimers.
findings.why_costs_money: This is a likely rejection reason when a reviewer opens a giveaway, and the launch goes straight to the App Store with no beta.
findings.fix: Append a fixed, non-editable footer server-side ('Apple is not a sponsor of, and is not involved in, this giveaway...') to every giveaway's rules at render time.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Can block launch (rejection delays all revenue)

findings.title: Live checkout makes buyers type their full address and phone during the stream
findings.problem: Buying in a live works (createSession and verifySession with liveStreamId), but street, city, region, postal code and phone start empty and must be typed while watching. Saved buyer addresses (buyer-addresses) and saved payment methods aren't prefilled.
findings.why_costs_money: Live purchases are impulse buys, and every extra field loses buyers, which cuts the GMV that makes Pro/live worth paying for.
findings.fix: Prefill from the default saved address (api.buyer.addresses) and the user's phone, and collapse the form into 'Ship to {address} · Change'.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1.5k/mo in commission if it lifts live checkout conversion 20-40%

findings.title: The seller drops list is unreachable; sellers can create a drop but not find it again
findings.problem: The create FAB opens /seller-drop-create, but the list screen /seller-drops has no inbound link anywhere (only its _layout registration). Sellers can't get back to edit, monitor or close drops, and the drop wallet (held preorder funds) is hard to reach.
findings.why_costs_money: Drops and preorders are a strong sales mechanic. Sellers who can't manage them abandon the feature or file support tickets about held money.
findings.fix: Add 'Drops' to the Store section in More and a 'Your drops' row in the Products tab.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-1k/mo in drop GMV commission and fewer support tickets

findings.title: Most seller growth tools have no server tier gate (drops, giveaways, discounts, email, push, store domain)
findings.problem: Server gates exist only for AI design (growth), Manufacturer Hub (growth), advanced and customer analytics (pro), live hosting (pro) and boosts (pro), plus product (25) and team-seat limits. Drops and preorders, giveaways, discounts, sales, email marketing, push broadcasts, featured slots, ad campaigns, gift cards, store domain, Shopify, growth links and pixels are open to all, including unpaid 'starter'.
findings.why_costs_money: Growth's only real value is AI and the manufacturer hub. Brands that don't design with AI have no reason to move up from $29, which caps average revenue per seller.
findings.fix: Suggested tiers. Starter: storefront, 25 products, discounts, sales, 1 push/week, 500 emails. Growth: unlimited products, drops/preorders, giveaways, email 10k, push 3/week, custom domain, Shopify sync, live 4h. Pro: live unlimited, advanced analytics, team unlimited, boost discount. Enforce with requirePlan or getVerifiedPlanAccess.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$2-6k/mo if 10-15% of Starter sellers move to Growth (+$50 each)

findings.title: No packing slips or pick list in batch fulfillment; slips are one order at a time
findings.problem: Packing slips exist only inside fulfill-order, one order per PDF. fulfill-batch offers only 'Print labels' and 'Mark shipped': there are no batch slips and no combined pick list.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers with 20+ orders a day (the ones paying for Growth/Pro) need batch slips and pick lists. Without them, operations-heavy sellers go to Shopify instead.
findings.fix: Add 'Print packing slips' to fulfill-batch, reusing buildPackingSlipHtml over the selected orders in one PDF, plus a pick-list page that totals quantity per SKU.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo in retained higher-volume sellers

findings.title: Vacation mode keeps billing the full plan, which pushes sellers to cancel
findings.problem: Vacation mode correctly blocks checkout (buyer.ts:442,669, guest-checkout.ts:169, cartCheckout), but it is not tied to billing. A seller pausing for a month still pays $29-$199.
findings.why_costs_money: Seasonal and drop-based brands cancel instead of pausing, and many don't come back.
findings.fix: When vacation is turned on for 2 weeks or more, offer a low-cost 'paused' plan (or Stripe pause_collection) that keeps the store and data, and auto-resume when vacation ends.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo in sellers kept instead of cancelled

findings.title: Six analytics screens are orphaned or stubbed (sales, products, customers, marketing, production, profit)
findings.screen: analytics-sales, analytics-products, analytics-customers, analytics-marketing, analytics-production, analytics-profit
findings.problem: Of the 14 analytics-* screens, only product-stats, content, audience, goals, export, advanced and cohorts are linked from the Reports list, plus analytics-store from Home. A static search finds no inbound links to analytics-sales, analytics-products, analytics-customers, analytics-marketing, analytics-production or analytics-profit. Four of those call stubs that throw. The linked screens use real APIs; preview fixtures are only active in dev builds (lib/devPreview.ts).
findings.why_costs_money: These are maintenance and review cost with no seller value. A deep link or App Review crawl lands on 'not available yet' screens (guideline 2.1 risk).
findings.fix: Remove the four stubbed screens from _layout (keep the files if needed). Either link analytics-sales and analytics-customers from Reports (they call real endpoints) or delete them.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Indirect: reduces App Review rejection risk and dev time

findings.title: Automation screen is a 'coming soon' placeholder; restock alerts and win-backs don't exist
findings.problem: The only content is EmptyState 'Automations are coming - Soon you'll set restock alerts, win-backs and more.' There is no backend. It is registered as a route with no inbound links.
findings.why_costs_money: Restock alerts (waitlist exists server-side) and win-back emails are the automations that actually raise repeat revenue. The placeholder adds review risk without value.
findings.fix: Remove the route for launch. After launch, build 2 real automations on existing parts: abandoned cart (job exists) and win-back (email marketing sender), and make them the Growth-tier hook.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Removal: $0 and lower review risk; building automations later: ~$1k+/mo as an upgrade driver

findings.title: Custom domains can be claimed by anyone before verification (unique constraint enables squatting)
findings.problem: POST /api/store/domains inserts any domain string with no format validation, and storefront_custom_domains.domain is UNIQUE. The first seller to type 'nike.com' or a rival brand's domain blocks the real owner from ever adding it.
findings.why_costs_money: Brand-squatting disputes cost support time and hurt the brands Brandthread most wants to sign.
findings.fix: Validate the hostname format. Allow multiple unverified claims (a partial unique index only WHERE verified), and expire unverified claims after 7 days.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-300/mo in support and lost brand signups

findings.title: Email campaign content isn't moderated (push broadcasts and giveaways are)
findings.problem: Seller push broadcasts and giveaways run evaluateContent, but the email campaign create, update and send paths never call it (grep evaluateContent / moderat in email-marketing finds nothing). Phishing links and scam copy go out from Brandthread's domain.
findings.why_costs_money: This is the fastest way to get the shared sending domain flagged (see the MAIL_FROM finding) and it carries legal liability.
findings.fix: Run evaluateContent on subject, preheader and text blocks at send time and reject or hold on 'reject'. Allowlist link domains or rewrite links through a click tracker.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Tail-risk protection for deliverability; ~$0 direct

findings.title: Marketing tab leads with Klaviyo, which only reads counts and syncs nothing
findings.problem: The top stat chips show Klaviyo email and SMS subscriber counts (0 for everyone not on Klaviyo), and the main CTA is 'Connect Klaviyo'. The Klaviyo integration only checks the key and refreshes subscriber counts. It never pushes Brandthread customers, orders or events to Klaviyo. The native, working email marketing is buried further down.
findings.why_costs_money: Prime space goes to a no-op integration while the real retention tools (email campaigns, push broadcast) are hidden, so sellers don't find what they pay for.
findings.fix: Replace the chips with native numbers (email subscribers, push-reachable followers) and lead with 'Send an email' and 'Send a push'. Move Klaviyo under Integrations, or make it real by syncing profiles and orders.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo from more use of the retention tools

findings.title: Klaviyo private API keys are stored in plaintext; any team role can change them
findings.problem: klaviyo_integrations.api_key is plain text (Shopify tokens use SHOPIFY_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY and Meta uses metaCrypto). The router has requireAuth but no requireRole or requirePermission, so a 'viewer' team member can connect or delete the key.
findings.why_costs_money: A DB leak exposes sellers' whole Klaviyo customer lists, which is a breach-notification event.
findings.fix: Encrypt with the metaCrypto/shopifyCrypto pattern and add requirePermission('marketing') to the mutating routes.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Tail-risk; ~$0 direct

findings.title: Campaigns empty state says 'Create a Meta ad' but opens Brandthread's internal ad campaigns
findings.problem: The empty state reads 'Create a Meta ad to put your products in front of new buyers', but the button opens design-campaign, which creates and pays for internal /api/ad-campaigns (Stripe Checkout), not Meta. Real Meta ads live separately under Studio > Meta Ads (meta-ads-manage) and depend on META_APP_ID and Meta App Review.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers think they are buying Facebook/Instagram ads and get in-app placements, which brings refund requests and chargebacks on ad spend.
findings.fix: Change the copy to 'Promote on Brandthread' for ad-campaigns, and route 'Meta ad' wording only to meta-ads-connect.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-500/mo in avoided ad-spend refunds

findings.title: Plans page says Growth has no team, but the server grants Growth 3 seats
findings.problem: SELLER_PLANS lists 'Team operations' under Growth notIncluded and 'Team roles' as a Pro feature. PLAN_CATALOGUE gives Growth teamSeats: 3 (Pro unlimited, Starter 0).
findings.why_costs_money: Either Growth sellers who want a team upgrade to Pro for nothing (a trust issue later), or they never learn Growth already covers them. Mismatched plan pages also draw App Review and consumer-law scrutiny.
findings.fix: Pick one rule and generate plan bullets from the server's /seller/subscription/perks, including team seats and the product limit.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-600/mo in correctly sold upgrades

findings.title: Starter's 25-product cap isn't in the plan features
findings.problem: The server caps Starter at products: 25 (enforced in products.ts, product-bulk.ts and product-import.ts), but the Starter features list only says 'Storefront, products, checkout, and orders'. Only a code comment in plans.tsx mentions 25.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers hit a surprise wall mid-import, which feels like a bait-and-switch and causes churn or refunds instead of an upgrade.
findings.fix: Add 'Up to 25 products' to Starter and 'Unlimited products' to Growth/Pro, and show 'X/25 products' in the Products tab with an upgrade CTA at 20.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo in upgrades instead of churn at the cap

findings.title: Push broadcasts are not tier-differentiated (1 per 24h for everyone)
findings.problem: Push broadcasts are well built (atomic 1-per-24h limit, moderation, audience filtering, mute and quiet hours), but they are the same for all tiers, including an unpaid starter.
findings.why_costs_money: Direct push to followers is one of the strongest sales tools and isn't used as an upgrade lever, and 7 blasts a week from every seller risks buyer push fatigue and opt-outs.
findings.fix: Make it plan-based, for example Starter 1/week, Growth 3/week, Pro 1/day, using getVerifiedPlanAccess in the claim step.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-1k/mo in upgrades, and protects buyer push opt-in rates

findings.title: Live streaming has no usage cap or metering (Agora minutes cost is open-ended)
findings.problem: Host tokens last 2h and can be reminted, and viewers join without a viewer or minutes cap. There is no per-seller monthly live-minutes accounting, and cloud recording (AGORA_RECORDING_*) adds storage and processing cost.
findings.why_costs_money: Agora bills per viewer-minute. A popular Pro seller (or a runaway session) can cost more than the $199 plan.
findings.fix: Record session minutes times peak viewers, enforce per-plan monthly host minutes, auto-end sessions with no host heartbeat, and alert ops above a cost threshold.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Caps tail cost; a single 3h, 1k-viewer stream is ~$180-700 in Agora minutes

findings.title: More > Integrations skips the hub and opens Klaviyo; the Shopify connection isn't listed
findings.problem: The Integrations menu item goes straight to /integrations/klaviyo. The hub (integrations/index) is unreachable and lists only Klaviyo and Stripe, not Shopify (the real order-forwarding and import integration at integrations/shopify-fulfillment).
findings.why_costs_money: Shopify migrants are the highest-value sellers. If they can't find the Shopify connection, they don't move their catalog or fulfillment over.
findings.fix: Route More > Integrations to /integrations and add Shopify (status from api.shopify.status) to INTEGRATION_DEFS.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-800/mo in activated Shopify-migrant sellers

findings.title: Shopify integration is a one-time import with no inventory sync, so dual-channel sellers oversell
findings.problem: Shopify webhooks handle only app/uninstalled, fulfillments/create|update and orders/cancelled. There is no inventory_levels/update or products/update handling, so stock imported once drifts as soon as the seller sells on Shopify.
findings.why_costs_money: Oversells trigger sold-out auto-refunds and bad buyer experiences, and the sellers most likely to pay for Growth/Pro (already on Shopify) are hit hardest.
findings.fix: Subscribe to inventory_levels/update and products/update for linked variants and update productVariants.stock through stockReservation's change pipeline.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$300-1k/mo in avoided refunds and kept dual-channel sellers

findings.title: Home 'messages to answer' counts only manufacturer threads, not buyer DMs
findings.problem: The 'N messages to answer - Buyers and manufacturers waiting on you' tile is built from manufacturer thread unreadCount only, but taps open /seller-inbox (buyer DMs). Unanswered buyer DMs never show, and on Starter the count is broken by the same 403.
findings.why_costs_money: Buyer pre-purchase questions go unanswered, which costs conversions and makes sellers think the app doesn't drive sales.
findings.fix: Add buyer conversation unread counts (the conversations unread endpoint used by the More tab badge) to toAnswer.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$200-600/mo in commission from answered pre-sale DMs

findings.title: Orders list has no pagination, and Home reloads every order on each focus
findings.problem: GET /api/orders returns every order for the seller (multi-join, group by, no limit or cursor). The dashboard calls it on every load just to count orders and show 5 recent ones.
findings.why_costs_money: Successful sellers (thousands of orders) get slow dashboards, so the best customers have the worst experience, and DB cost grows with GMV.
findings.fix: Add cursor pagination (limit 50) plus a summary endpoint (counts by status, 5 recent) for the dashboard. Reuse lib/pagination.ts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-500/mo in DB load and top-seller retention

findings.title: Order numbers come from count(*) with no lock or unique index, so duplicates are possible
findings.problem: Both order paths compute BT-{count+1} from SELECT count(*) inside a transaction with no row lock or advisory lock, and orders.order_number has no (owner_id, order_number) unique index. Two concurrent checkouts (a drop launch, or a live) get the same order number, and purged or deleted orders make numbers repeat.
findings.why_costs_money: Duplicate 'Order #BT-00042' rows cause fulfillment mistakes (double-shipping or missed shipments) during exactly the high-volume moments sellers care about.
findings.fix: Use a per-owner counter row updated with UPDATE ... RETURNING (or pg_advisory_xact_lock(owner)) and add a unique index on (owner_id, order_number).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$100-400/mo in mis-fulfillment costs during drops/lives

findings.title: No review-request prompt after delivery, so sellers struggle to get reviews
findings.problem: On delivery the buyer gets 'Your order was delivered!' with no 'Rate your order' CTA, and no follow-up job asks for a review a few days later. A grep for review_request, 'leave a review' and 'rate your' finds nothing.
findings.why_costs_money: New brands live or die by social proof. Few reviews means lower conversion for sellers, who then see no ROI from their subscription.
findings.fix: Add a 'How was {product}?' notification and email 3 days after delivery, deep-linked to the review form (POST /api/reviews already validates delivered orders).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-1.5k/mo through higher conversion on reviewed products

findings.title: Seller verification can create unlimited paid Stripe Identity sessions
findings.problem: POST /seller/verification/start has no attempt limit, cooldown, seller-role or plan check. After a /cancel or an expired session it creates a fresh document-plus-selfie VerificationSession every time. Any signed-in user, including buyers, can call it.
findings.why_costs_money: Stripe Identity charges per verification (about $1.50+ with selfie). A loop or abuse script burns money, and the verified badge is a natural paid-tier perk that is given away.
findings.fix: Limit to 3 sessions per user per 30 days, require a seller account, and consider making the 'Verified' badge Growth+ (with Starter verification only for payouts risk).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Caps abuse; ~$50-300/mo normal, unbounded under abuse

findings.title: Shippo depends on a Replit connector with no env check or health signal
findings.problem: Label buying uses @replit/connectors-sdk proxy('shippo'). Nothing in env.ts or startup checks that the connector is linked, and only SHIPPO_WEBHOOK_SECRET is listed. Off Replit, or if the connector is unlinked, every rates and label call fails at runtime with 'Shipping provider request failed'.
findings.why_costs_money: If labels fail on launch day, every seller has to ship manually, and fulfillment is the first thing sellers judge.
findings.fix: Add a startup or health check that calls a cheap Shippo endpoint (GET /carrier_accounts) and reports it in /healthz and the seller launch checklist.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Protects launch-day fulfillment; outage cost is ~1-2 days of seller trust

findings.title: Featured slots can only be found from inside the Pro-only Boost screen
findings.problem: Featured Discover slots (paid, scarce, admin-approved) can be bought on every tier server-side, but the only entry point is a button in boost.tsx, whose data calls are Pro-gated. Non-Pro sellers effectively never find this paid product.
findings.why_costs_money: Featured placement is a high-margin, fixed-price inventory sale that goes unsold.
findings.fix: Add 'Get featured on Discover' to the Marketing tab and More > Growth for all paying tiers.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$500-2k/mo if a few slots/week sell at $50-200

findings.title: Buyer loyalty points run alongside Thread Cash: a second, overlapping reward cost
findings.problem: A separate loyalty system (1 pt per $1, 500 per referral, 100 at signup, 100 pts = $1 off via loyaltyToken at checkout) is live and linked from buyer settings, on top of Thread Cash credits. The business model names only Thread Cash.
findings.why_costs_money: Two reward currencies mean double subsidy exposure and an unclear question of who funds the $1-off (Brandthread or the seller's price). Cross-ref thread-cash-referrals-abuse.
findings.fix: Turn off loyalty earn and redeem for launch (hide the Rewards menu row) and keep Thread Cash as the single reward currency.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~1% of GMV in unplanned discounts (~$500-5k/mo) if loyalty redemptions are platform-funded

findings.title: Product bundles are overbuilt and dead: never shown to buyers or priced at checkout
findings.problem: Sellers can create and edit bundles with a bundlePriceCents, but /api/bundles/public is never called by the buyer app, and checkout and cart code never reads bundles (grep for bundle in lib/money, buyer.ts and cart-db finds nothing). The list screen has no inbound link, and the half-done audit logged 404s for /product-bundles.
findings.why_costs_money: This is a maintenance surface that could mislead sellers into thinking a bundle discount is live.
findings.fix: Remove the bundles screens from navigation for launch. Later, implement buyer display plus checkout pricing, or fold bundles into discount codes ('buy X+Y get $Z off').
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $0 direct; lowers dev cost and confusion

findings.title: Email open and click tracking is silently off unless RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set (not in env checks)
findings.problem: Delivered, opened and clicked stats need RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET. It isn't in OPTIONAL_VARS, so a missing value never even logs a startup warning, and campaign results show no engagement.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers who see no opens or clicks decide email doesn't work and stop using it (or blame the product).
findings.fix: Add RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET and EMAIL_TOKEN_SECRET to OPTIONAL_VARS, and add both to docs/launch env lists.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: <$200/mo; perceived value of the email tool

findings.title: finance.tsx and shipping-label are duplicates or orphans next to the payouts and fulfill-order flows
findings.problem: finance.tsx (376 lines, role-locked balance view) has no inbound navigation. More > Money links /payouts. shipping-label.tsx is now only a redirect to fulfill-order with no inbound links. Both stay registered as routes.
findings.why_costs_money: Duplicate money screens risk showing numbers that disagree, which is a support and trust cost.
findings.fix: Delete finance.tsx (keep payouts and statements) and drop the shipping-label route once no deep links depend on it.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: $0 direct; less maintenance

findings.title: More tab shows 'FREE' plan badge although there is no free plan
findings.problem: planLabel falls back to 'FREE' whenever plan isn't pro or growth, including Starter ($29) and while loading. A paying Starter seller sees 'FREE' next to Subscription.
findings.why_costs_money: Paying sellers think they are on a free plan (support tickets, 'why was I charged' disputes), and unpaid sellers think free is a real tier.
findings.fix: Map starter to 'STARTER', show nothing while loading, and show 'NO PLAN' with a CTA when status is none.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: ~$50-200/mo in avoided billing disputes

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Freelancer can self-complete a job and get paid instantly: no hirer approval
findings.problem: PATCH /freelancer-jobs/:id/complete is freelancer-only. It moves in_progress to completed and immediately transfers freelancerPayoutCents. The hirer cannot approve, request revisions or dispute. The UI promises 'Payment is held by Brandthread and released when the job is done.'
findings.why_costs_money: A bad-faith freelancer can accept, start and complete within minutes and withdraw. The hirer then charges back against the platform's own charge (separate charges and transfers), and Brandthread loses the full price plus the dispute fee.
findings.fix: Add a 'delivered' state. Complete from the hirer, or auto-release N days after delivery with no dispute. Only then create the transfer. Add a hirer 'open dispute' action that freezes the release.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Fraud exposure equal to 100% of freelancer GMV per bad actor. One $5k job lost is the take on $100k of jobs.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Admin revenue excludes subscriptions/IAP MRR, sample/bulk fees, freelancer fees, AI credits
findings.problem: /admin/revenue sums only orders.platformFeeCents and boost budgets. The UI says 'Subscription revenue is billed and reported in Stripe', but iOS/Android subscriptions are in RevenueCat, not Stripe. sampleOrders.platformFeeCents, freelancerJobs.platformFeeCents, AI-credit packs, gift cards and featured slots are missing.
findings.why_costs_money: The owner can't see progress toward $50k/mo or which lines work. Subscription MRR, the main revenue line, is invisible in the admin.
findings.fix: Add GET /admin/mrr (Stripe subscriptions plus native entitlements from RevenueCat webhook rows: active, trialing, converted, churned, MRR by tier) and add B2B and freelancer fee lines to /admin/revenue.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Required to manage toward $50k/mo. Can't measure trial-to-paid or MRR.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No Thread Cash budget/liability dashboard or kill switch in admin
findings.problem: The admin nav has Overview, Users, Orders, Revenue, AI spend, Moderation, Promotions, Featured, Announcements, Invites and Audit. Nothing shows Thread Cash issued, outstanding liability, redeemed or expired, or daily-reward spend, and there is no admin control to pause rewards (no admin route under thread-cash).
findings.why_costs_money: Thread Cash is a direct cash cost. An abuse ring or a viral spike can burn thousands per day unnoticed, with no way to stop it short of a deploy.
findings.fix: Add GET /admin/thread-cash (issued, redeemed, outstanding, top earners, per-day) and a feature-flag-backed pause switch for daily rewards and checkout credit (feature-flags.ts exists).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Caps uncontrolled cost. A runaway abuse day at $1-2k is plausible without it.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: PostHog analytics exists but is OFF: no key configured anywhere
findings.problem: Both clients no-op without EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY / POSTHOG_API_KEY. Neither is set in .replit userenv or eas.json build env.
findings.why_costs_money: Launch day would have no funnel data (signup, onboarding, trial, purchase), so there is no way to see where the $50k target is leaking.
findings.fix: Create a PostHog project and set EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY in the EAS production profile and web deployment, and POSTHOG_API_KEY on the API, before Oct 31.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Blocks measuring revenue. Required to optimise any funnel.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Analytics event catalogue has no subscription, trial, paywall or seller-activation events
findings.problem: The allow-list covers app_opened, signup, onboarding, product_viewed, add_to_cart, checkout_started, social events, seller_onboarding_completed and product_published. There is no paywall_viewed, plan_selected, trial_started, trial_converted, subscription_cancelled, payout_setup_completed, store_published, first_sale, thread_cash_earned/redeemed, referral_sent/redeemed or sample_order_paid. The server only emits purchase_completed.
findings.why_costs_money: Trial-to-paid, the core seller-revenue metric, and the Thread Cash ROI can't be measured, so prices and the trial can't be tuned.
findings.fix: Add these events. Emit the subscription ones server-side from the Stripe and RevenueCat webhooks (authoritative, survives app deletion) via captureServerEvent, keyed by Clerk id.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Trial-to-paid visibility. A 5-point conversion lift on 500 trials is about 25 sellers, roughly $750 MRR.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Autoscale deployment plus 25 in-process setInterval jobs: duplicate money jobs or none at idle
findings.problem: deploymentTarget = 'autoscale'. Every instance starts all jobs (money sweep, affiliate payouts, Thread Cash expiry, trial reminders, abandoned cart, email campaigns) with no leader lock and no BullMQ (Phase 4 not implemented). Autoscale also scales idle instances down, so timers don't run with no traffic. SCALE_PLAN §8: 'Do not raise Autoscale max instances above 1'.
findings.why_costs_money: Two instances can mean duplicate trial-reminder or abandoned-cart emails and double payout attempts (idempotency keys mitigate some). Zero instances means missed trial reminders, so involuntary trial loss, and late payouts.
findings.fix: Pin max instances to 1 for launch, or move jobs to a Replit Reserved VM or scheduled deployment. Add a Postgres advisory-lock leader election (pg_try_advisory_lock) around each job run as a cheap, additive guard.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Protects trial conversion emails and payout correctness. A missed trial reminder costs MRR.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Brandthread pays Stripe processing on sample/bulk cards, eating ~60% of the 5% take
findings.problem: Retail destination charges add a processing estimate to application_fee_amount (destinationApplicationFeeCents), but sample/bulk Checkout passes only platformFeeCents. Stripe's 2.9%+30c (plus 1.5% on international cards) is charged to the platform. money-flow.md:386 admits this is 'paid by Brandthread and not tracked in the ledger'.
findings.why_costs_money: On a $10,000 bulk card Brandthread keeps $500 and pays about $290 to $440 in Stripe fees. Net take falls to roughly 1-2% of B2B GMV, and the ledger overstates profit.
findings.fix: Use destinationApplicationFeeCents({merchandiseCents: priceCents, preTaxTotalCents: priceCents}) for sample orders (persist processingFeeEstimateCents), or add a seller-side 'card processing' line. Additive change to the order-card insert.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: About $2.9k/mo recovered per $100k of B2B card GMV.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Bulk orders paid from drop wallet: transfer sends 100% to manufacturer, zero B2B take
findings.problem: pay-from-wallet calls stripe.transfers.create with amount: order.priceCents even though the row carries platformFeeCents. The ledger posts the full amount to manufacturer_paid. The doc marks this an 'Owner decision', still open.
findings.why_costs_money: Bulk production is the largest B2B ticket ($5k-$50k). Funding it from preorder money (the path the drop flow pushes) skips the manufacturer-side 5% that the card path collects. Two payment routes for the same order earn different amounts.
findings.fix: Decide the policy. If the fee should apply, transfer priceCents - platformFeeCents and post the fee to a platform_revenue ledger leg in recordBulkPaidFromHeld. Show the net on the manufacturer's order card.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: 5% of wallet-funded bulk GMV. $60k/mo of bulk via wallets is about $3k/mo.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Bulk order cards up to $500k are card-only; no ACH/wire, so big orders leave the platform
findings.problem: Checkout uses payment_method_types: ['card'] for every sample/bulk card, and validateCardInput allows cards up to US$500,000. No us_bank_account (ACH) and no bank-transfer option.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers will not pay a 3% card fee on a $20k production run. They will ask the factory for wire details, and the deal (and the 5%) leaves. Brandthread also pays the card fee itself (see above).
findings.fix: Add 'us_bank_account' (ACH Direct Debit, 0.8% capped at $5) and customer_balance bank transfers to the Checkout session for bulk cards above a threshold (e.g. $1,000). Keep card for samples.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Keeps large bulk tickets on platform. Each retained $20k order is $1k gross. Likely $2k-$5k/mo at target scale.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: B2B fee charged to manufacturer while portal advertises 'Free for manufacturers'
findings.problem: Signup copy says 'Free for manufacturers' and 'List your factory — free', but every paid card has 5% deducted from the manufacturer's payout. The only disclosure is 'Brandthread's platform fee ... deducted before payout' in the send-card dialog, with no rate shown.
findings.why_costs_money: A surprise deduction pushes factories to ask sellers to pay them directly, and is a consumer-protection and chargeback risk. Every off-platform order is a 100% loss of the take.
findings.fix: State '5% platform fee on paid orders, no listing fee' on the landing, join and send-card screens. Show 'You receive $X' in the send-card dialog. Record acceptance of manufacturer terms at registration (recordLegalAcceptance).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Protects the whole B2B take. Trust and disintermediation risk on all B2B GMV.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No manufacturer terms/agreement accepted at signup (fee, non-circumvention)
findings.problem: POST /manufacturers/register inserts the manufacturer as active with no legal acceptance record. The portal onboarding has no terms checkbox. lib/legalAcceptance.ts exists but is not used for manufacturers.
findings.why_costs_money: Without a signed fee and non-circumvention clause, Brandthread has no recourse when factories take introduced sellers off-platform, and no contractual basis for the 5% deduction.
findings.fix: Add a manufacturer agreement version, require acceptance in onboarding, and call recordLegalAcceptance in register and register-via-invite. Include a 12-month non-circumvention clause for sellers introduced through the directory.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Contract basis for all B2B revenue.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Manufacturer website shown publicly and to sellers: easy route around the take
findings.problem: publicManufacturerFields, /partners/:id and seller-hub /manufacturers all return manufacturers.website. Factory sites list email, WhatsApp and WeChat.
findings.why_costs_money: A seller can find a factory on Brandthread and contact it directly before any paid card, so the platform does the discovery work and earns nothing.
findings.fix: Hide website from the directory and partner payloads until the seller has paid at least one order card with that manufacturer (or move it behind the Growth plan). Show a 'Verified on Brandthread' badge in its place.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Disintermediation on directory-originated deals. Plausibly 20-40% of B2B GMV at risk.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Manufacturer chat has no contact-info or off-platform-payment filter
findings.problem: Seller-to-manufacturer and manufacturer-to-seller messages are stored with no moderateMessage call (only routes/conversations.ts imports it). Even the existing off-platform payment regex covers only Zelle/CashApp/Venmo phrasing. Emails, phone numbers, WeChat/WhatsApp IDs, PayPal and wire/IBAN pass through.
findings.why_costs_money: B2B is where off-platform payment is most tempting (large tickets, card fees). One 'send me your email, I'll invoice you' message moves the whole relationship off-platform.
findings.fix: Run a contact/payment-steering detector on manufacturer messages (email, phone, IBAN/SWIFT, WeChat/WhatsApp, PayPal/Wise). Soft-mask before the first paid order and show both sides an 'Orders paid outside Brandthread aren't protected' notice.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Protects B2B take. Each leaked repeat-customer relationship loses all future orders.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Freelancer-job and sample-order chargebacks never claw back the payout
findings.problem: charge.dispute.* for manufacturer cards only records a payment_reversed event and sets the order to payment_review. No transfers.createReversal, and no debit from the manufacturer. Freelancer job charges are not matched by lib/disputes/store (orders table only), so they are ignored.
findings.why_costs_money: On destination and platform charges, Stripe debits Brandthread's balance for the dispute plus a $15 fee while the manufacturer or freelancer keeps the money. Every lost B2B chargeback is a direct loss.
findings.fix: For lost disputes, call stripe.transfers.createReversal on the order's transfer (or debit the connected account) and post a ledger leg. Add freelancer-job lookup to the dispute handler. Surface it in the admin disputes list.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Each B2B chargeback costs price plus $15. A few per month at $1k-$10k each is $2k-$10k/mo of exposure.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No refund/cancel path for paid sample or bulk orders
findings.problem: Cancel only handles unpaid cards. Once a sample or bulk card is paid there is no API to refund (full or partial) or reverse the transfer, and admin refunds are read-only.
findings.why_costs_money: When a factory misses a deadline or ships defects, the seller's only recourse is a chargeback, which Brandthread eats (see dispute finding). Sellers learn not to pay through the platform.
findings.fix: Add POST /sample-orders/:id/refund (manufacturer-initiated or admin) using refunds.create with reverse_transfer: true and refund_application_fee as a policy flag, plus a 'Brandthread Production Protection' promise in the UI.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Turns chargebacks into controlled refunds, saving $15 per dispute plus the full amount, and builds trust that keeps B2B GMV on-platform.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Quote acceptance doesn't create a payable order card: deals re-keyed in chat
findings.problem: Manufacturers quote quotedPriceCents on a quote request and the seller can accept. Nothing turns an accepted quote into a sampleOrders card. Someone must re-price it manually in a thread, so the agreed price and the payment are disconnected.
findings.why_costs_money: Every extra manual step between 'yes' and 'pay' is a point where the parties exchange details and pay off-platform.
findings.fix: When a seller accepts a quote, auto-create a pending_payment sampleOrders card (via the same insert as manufacturer-flow order-cards) in the linked thread with a one-tap 'Pay securely' CTA.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Raises quote-to-paid conversion. Each extra 10% conversion on $100k/mo of quotes is about $500/mo of take.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: RFQs and quote requests send no notification or email to manufacturers
findings.problem: POST /seller-hub/rfqs and /quote-requests insert rows but call neither publishNotification nor any email. The only manufacturer email that exists is the signup email. Manufacturers work in the web portal with no push token, so publishNotification (in-app plus push only) doesn't reach them either.
findings.why_costs_money: Factories don't see requests, so sellers get no quotes and conclude the directory is dead. No quotes means no order cards and no take, and the Growth plan that gates the hub looks worthless (churn).
findings.fix: Add transactional emails to manufacturers (contactEmail) for new quote request/RFQ, new message, and order paid, with a digest throttle. Add a web-push or email fallback in publishNotification for users with no device.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Underpins all B2B GMV and Growth-plan retention. Likely the biggest B2B conversion lever.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Seller-hub lists private (invite-only) manufacturers to every user, including their website
findings.problem: GET /seller-hub/manufacturers filters only status='active', so manufacturers created through a seller's private invite (isPublicDirectory: false) are listed to all users with their website. The onboarding screen promises 'Your invite is private: only the seller who invited you will see your profile.' RFQ targeting (seller-hub.ts:317) also accepts them.
findings.why_costs_money: Competitors can poach a seller's private factory. That breaks a stated privacy promise and discourages sellers from bringing their own supplier onto the platform, which is the cheapest B2B GMV to acquire.
findings.fix: Add eq(manufacturers.isPublicDirectory, true) OR an existing relationship with the caller to both the list and the RFQ targeting query.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Protects invite-sourced B2B GMV and trust. Also a privacy-claim risk.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Manufacturer self-signup goes live instantly: no vetting before taking card payments
findings.problem: POST /manufacturers/register inserts isPublicDirectory: true, status: 'active' ('no manual approval step'). After Stripe Express onboarding the account can price cards and take seller payments immediately.
findings.why_costs_money: Fake 'factories' can collect sample payments and disappear. On destination charges the dispute lands on Brandthread (see dispute finding), and fake listings make the real directory look untrustworthy.
findings.fix: Keep signup instant but hide new manufacturers from the public directory until an admin approves (status 'pending_review'), or cap the first N card payments and use a delayed payout schedule for new accounts (Stripe payout delay settings).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Fraud prevention. One fake factory running 20 x $200 samples is a $4k loss plus fees.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Manufacturer directory is real DB data but empty at launch (demo fixtures web-preview only)
findings.problem: The directory reads live manufacturers rows. The PREVIEW_MANUFACTURERS fixture only appears with isPreviewDemoMode() (dev-web preview). No seed or migration inserts manufacturers, so production launches with zero factories unless they are recruited by hand.
findings.why_costs_money: The Growth plan's headline 'find manufacturers' feature shows an empty hub to paying sellers on day one, causing refund requests and churn, and there is no B2B GMV until supply exists.
findings.fix: Recruit and onboard 30-50 real factories through the portal before Oct 31. Add an empty-state CTA ('Invite your factory') that routes to invite-manufacturer, so sellers bring their own supply.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: The Growth tier's value depends on it. The churn risk is the Growth MRR.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Landing page has no pricing: 'Start selling' with no plan prices or trial terms
findings.problem: The Sell section only says 'Selling plans and premium seller tools are available as subscriptions.' It shows no tier names, prices, 5-day trial or 5% commission, and there is no /pricing route (build-web.js PUBLIC_ROUTES has none).
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers comparing Shopify, Depop or Big Cartel bounce when pricing is hidden, which hurts web conversion where Brandthread keeps 100% of subscription revenue.
findings.fix: Once prices are set, add a /pricing section and page generated from the same plan catalogue (planCatalogue.ts / sellerPlansDisplay.ts), with trial terms and the 5% fee, and add it to PUBLIC_ROUTES and the sitemap.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Web seller conversion. +10 web sellers/mo at $30 avoids $45-$90/mo of Apple cut and adds MRR.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No web-only price advantage or 'subscribe on web' steering for sellers
findings.problem: The web plans page shows plan.priceLabel, the same list price as in-app. Nothing on the landing page or in the app's web flow positions web as the place to subscribe, and there is no web-exclusive offer such as an annual plan or a longer trial.
findings.why_costs_money: Every seller who subscribes through iOS IAP costs 15-30%. Under the US external-link entitlement and 3.1.3(b) multiplatform, web subscriptions are allowed and keep 100%.
findings.fix: Offer a web-only annual plan or discount, add a 'Subscribe on the web' link in the US iOS build (with the subscription-iap agent's entitlement work), and A/B the landing CTA.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Shifting 50% of subscription MRR to web at $30k MRR saves about $2.25k-$4.5k/mo of Apple fees.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Admin refunds and disputes are read-only: no refund, evidence or payout-hold action
findings.problem: GET /admin/refunds and /admin/disputes only list rows. docs/admin-dashboard.md says 'nothing moves money: refunds and disputes are read-only views'. Ops must use the Stripe dashboard, which bypasses the ledger handlers for some flows.
findings.why_costs_money: Slow dispute response loses chargebacks (each costs the amount plus $15). Dashboard refunds can desync seller payouts and Thread Cash, and support time per case is high.
findings.fix: Add audited admin actions: POST /admin/orders/:id/refund (calling lib/money/refunds), dispute evidence submit (reusing lib/disputes/upload), and seller payout hold/release via Stripe payout schedule.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Disputes won and ops hours. At 0.5% dispute rate on $1M GMV, winning 30% more saves about $1.5k/mo.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Admin 'platform fees' is gross: ignores Stripe fees Brandthread pays and Thread Cash subsidy
findings.problem: Revenue = sum(platformFeeCents) - refunded fees. It does not subtract Thread Cash spent (orders.threadCashAppliedCents is shown only on order detail), daily Thread Cash rewards, Stripe dispute fees, or Stripe fees absorbed on B2B and freelancer charges.
findings.why_costs_money: Thread Cash is paid from Brandthread's pocket. Showing gross fees can hide a negative contribution margin until the bank balance shows it.
findings.fix: Add a 'net take' card: fees - Thread Cash redeemed - rewards issued (from the threadCash ledger) - absorbed Stripe fees - dispute fees, using the money ledger accounts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Prevents unseen margin loss. Thread Cash could be 20-50% of fees.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No fraud/risk review queue in admin, though order risk scores are computed
findings.problem: Radar outcomes and riskLevel/riskScore are stored on orders and shown to sellers (orders.ts), but /admin/orders has no risk filter and no review queue. There is no admin view of elevated-risk sellers, new-seller payout velocity, or Thread Cash farming.
findings.why_costs_money: Fraudulent sellers or buyers are only found after chargebacks, and Brandthread is liable on negative balances of Express accounts.
findings.fix: Add ?risk=elevated|highest to /admin/orders and a 'Risk' page listing high-risk orders, new sellers with fast GMV, and Thread Cash anomalies, with a suspend/hold action.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Fraud loss prevention. Likely $1k-$5k/mo at scale.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No seller payout review/hold tooling: payouts flow automatically to new accounts
findings.problem: Admin can suspend a user but cannot view or hold a connected account's payouts or set a delayed payout schedule for new or high-risk sellers. Express accounts' negative balances are the platform's liability.
findings.why_costs_money: A seller who ships nothing and gets paid out before chargebacks leaves Brandthread holding the loss.
findings.fix: Add admin endpoints to set stripe.accounts.update(payout_schedule.delay_days / manual) for a seller and manufacturer, and show pending/available balance on the admin user page.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Limits seller-fraud losses.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: WebSocket live/community rooms are in-process Maps: break with more than 1 instance
findings.problem: Live and community chat state lives in process memory. With autoscale above 1 instance, viewers on different instances don't see each other's messages, tips or live-commerce events.
findings.why_costs_money: Live shopping (tips, live-commerce checkout) silently degrades under the very traffic spikes that generate revenue.
findings.fix: Keep 1 instance for launch, or implement the Redis pub/sub adapter (REDIS_URL plumbing exists in lib/redis.ts).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Live-commerce GMV during peaks.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Video bytes still stream through Express from object storage (no CDN/Mux)
findings.problem: GET /api/posts/media/* pipes file.createReadStream through the API. The CDN (CDN_BASE_URL) is optional and unset by default. Mux/R2 Phase 5 is not implemented (no MUX_/VIDEO_PROVIDER references).
findings.why_costs_money: Feed video egress plus API CPU is the main cost line (SCALE_PLAN estimates video dominates the bill), and saturated API cores slow checkout for everyone.
findings.fix: Before launch, set CDN_BASE_URL (Cloudflare in front of GCS) so media bypasses Express. Plan Mux or R2 when the video bill passes about $5k/mo.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Infra cost at 10k DAU: about $1.5k/mo saved with CDN versus proxying, and protects checkout latency.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: DB pool, statement timeout and pooler unset by default; rate limiter writes DB on every request
findings.problem: DB_POOL_MAX, DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS and DATABASE_READ_URL are opt-in. The rate limiter stores counters in Postgres unless REDIS_URL is set, and fails closed (503) when the DB is slow, so a DB slowdown becomes a full outage including checkout.
findings.why_costs_money: A launch-day spike can take checkout and subscription purchase down. Every minute of outage at $50k/mo is about $1.2 of GMV take, and it costs App Store rating damage.
findings.fix: For launch set DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS=15000, DB_POOL_MAX sized to the plan, a pooled (Neon -pooler) DATABASE_URL, and REDIS_URL (Upstash fixed plan) so rate limits leave Postgres.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Outage avoidance during launch spike.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Single Replit deployment hosts API, web app and portal: one failure domain for all revenue
findings.problem: API, Expo web (brandthread.app), manufacturer portal and app-tour are path-routed services in one Replit deployment. A bad deploy or platform incident takes buyer checkout, web subscriptions, B2B payments and webhooks down together. There is no documented uptime monitor (SCALE_PLAN Phase 8 lists Better Stack as todo).
findings.why_costs_money: Stripe webhooks retry, but RevenueCat, Shippo and Clerk events and live checkouts during an outage are lost revenue, and no one is paged.
findings.fix: Before launch, add an uptime monitor on /api/healthz/ready and /status with phone alerts, and a rollback runbook. Longer term, split the API from static web as in SCALE_PLAN §7.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Outage detection. Each hour down at $50k/mo is about $70 of take plus trust.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Freelancer escrow charge on platform: Brandthread pays processing out of its 5%
findings.problem: The hirer pays the price to the platform account and the freelancer gets price - 5%. Stripe 2.9%+30c (plus FX and cross-border transfer fees for non-US freelancers) is borne by Brandthread.
findings.why_costs_money: The net take on freelancer GMV is about 2%. Small jobs ($20-$50) can be loss-making after the 30c fixed fee, and cross-border fees can make them negative.
findings.fix: Add a hirer-side service fee (e.g. 3% plus $0.50, like Fiverr) shown in the hire sheet, or pass processing to the freelancer side like retail. Set a minimum job price that covers fees.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: About 3% of freelancer GMV. $20k/mo of jobs is about $600/mo.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Unvalidated client successUrl/cancelUrl on freelancer Checkout
findings.problem: POST /freelancer-jobs passes any string successUrl/cancelUrl from the request body straight into the Stripe Checkout session.
findings.why_costs_money: Brandthread-branded Checkout can redirect to an attacker domain after payment, so it can be used for phishing or fake 'payment failed, pay again here' pages. That means fraud losses and support cost.
findings.fix: Allow-list the app scheme and the brandthread.app/API origins (lib/webOrigin.ts or brandthreadCallbackUrls.ts) before accepting a custom URL.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Fraud/support prevention. Small direct $.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Seller-hub RFQ/quote and sample-order routes bypass the Growth plan paywall
findings.problem: /manufacturers seller routes use requireGrowthSeller, and the mobile hub upsells Growth (manufacturer-hub.tsx:177). /seller-hub (RFQs, quote requests, manufacturer list) and /sample-orders are mounted with only teamContext, so any signed-in account, including a free buyer, can RFQ up to 10 factories.
findings.why_costs_money: The paywall that is meant to sell Growth subscriptions is bypassable by any client, and factories get spammed by non-paying accounts.
findings.fix: Decide intentionally. Either gate /seller-hub/rfqs and /quote-requests with requirePlan('growth') (keeping /sample-orders payment open so paid GMV is never blocked), or move manufacturer sourcing to the free tier and gate only advanced features.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Growth-plan conversion integrity. Depends on unset tier prices.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: 'Verified' manufacturer badge can never be granted: no endpoint sets verifiedAt
findings.problem: The directory sorts by verifiedAt and offers a 'verified' filter, but no route writes manufacturers.verifiedAt (grep finds only reads). Admin /users/:id/verify verifies users, not manufacturers.
findings.why_costs_money: Sellers deciding where to spend $10k+ need trust signals. Without verification the directory can't compete with Alibaba Trade Assurance/Faire, and a paid 'Verified' listing tier for factories isn't possible.
findings.fix: Add POST /admin/manufacturers/:id/verify (audited) plus an admin page. Consider a paid manufacturer verification or featured-placement fee as a second B2B revenue line.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Enables trust for B2B conversion. A paid verification of e.g. $99 for 50 factories is about $5k one-time.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Public manufacturer applications go to 'pending' with no review queue anywhere
findings.problem: POST /manufacturers/public/apply creates status 'pending', isPublicDirectory: false, and says it awaits 'an authenticated review/claim flow'. No admin route lists or approves pending manufacturers, and nothing emails the applicant.
findings.why_costs_money: Inbound factory supply leads silently die, and the directory stays thin at launch.
findings.fix: Add GET /admin/manufacturers?status=pending plus approve/reject (audited), email the applicant a claim link, or remove the public apply form in favour of the portal's self-signup.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Supply-side growth for B2B.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Freelancers go live instantly with portfolio links and no review
findings.problem: POST /freelancers/apply upserts isActive: true immediately. Public profiles expose portfolioUrls (up to 4 arbitrary links) and userId (so the hirer can open a normal DM).
findings.why_costs_money: Portfolio sites carry contact details, so jobs get negotiated and paid off-platform. Fake freelancers, combined with self-complete payouts, are a fraud vector.
findings.fix: Hold new freelancers out of search until they are Connect-verified (stripeAccountId active) and admin-approved. Strip contact details from bios and portfolio pages via the same detector proposed for manufacturer chat.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Protects freelancer take and fraud exposure.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Separate-charges escrow for freelancers makes Brandthread merchant of record
findings.problem: Freelancer funds are charged on the platform account, so Brandthread is the merchant of record for the service: its statement descriptor, dispute liability, refund obligation and possible sales-tax/1099-K reporting duties.
findings.why_costs_money: Brandthread takes on liability for chargebacks and possibly tax on 100% of the gross while keeping 5%. Funds held over 90 days can run into Stripe's separate-charges limits.
findings.fix: Confirm with counsel and Stripe: use on_behalf_of to make the freelancer the settlement merchant, or keep escrow but add auto-release under 90 days and a hirer fee to fund the risk.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Liability equal to freelancer GMV. Dispute costs as above.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No platform take on RFQ/quote volume or manufacturer subscriptions (untapped B2B revenue)
findings.problem: Manufacturers pay nothing to list, receive unlimited RFQs and get directory placement free. Revenue comes only from the 5% on paid cards.
findings.why_costs_money: Factories are the side with B2B purchasing budgets. Alibaba/Faire-style supplier memberships, featured placement and lead fees are standard revenue lines that don't add to seller friction.
findings.fix: After launch, add a 'Manufacturer Pro' web subscription (Stripe on web, no Apple cut since the portal is web-only): featured directory placement, verified badge, RFQ priority. featured-slots plumbing can be reused.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: 50 factories x $49/mo is about $2.5k MRR, outside Apple entirely.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Manufacturer portal is web-only: good for a no-Apple-cut B2B revenue line, but not discoverable
findings.problem: Manufacturers work at brandthread.app/manufacturers/. The main landing page never mentions manufacturers or links to the portal, and the portal's landing isn't in the main sitemap.
findings.why_costs_money: Supply-side acquisition depends on manual outreach. Factories searching for 'streetwear brands looking for manufacturers' can't find it.
findings.fix: Add a 'Manufacturers' link and section to landing-page.js, add /manufacturers/ to robots/sitemap, and use the portal landing as SEO content for the factory side.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: B2B supply growth.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Web seller signup + Stripe subscription checkout exists: verify trial-with-card on web
findings.problem: On web, plans.tsx uses POST /subscription/checkout (Stripe) and polls for the webhook. Landing 'Start selling' writes onboarding_pending_flow=seller and routes to /onboarding. Seller web signup through paid subscription is wired. Cross-reference the subscription-iap area for trial and card details.
findings.why_costs_money: This is the cheapest seller-revenue path (no Apple fee). Any break in it directly costs MRR.
findings.fix: Add an end-to-end web funnel test (landing, onboarding, plans, Stripe Checkout, webhook, active) and PostHog events for each step (see analytics findings).
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Protects web MRR.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No admin view for manufacturers, B2B orders, or freelancer jobs
findings.problem: /admin/orders queries only the retail orders table. sample_orders (payment_review after reversals), freelancer_jobs (stuck in_progress, paid but never completed), and manufacturer accounts have no admin listing or action.
findings.why_costs_money: Money stuck in B2B and freelancer escrow and reversed manufacturer payments go unnoticed. Disputes and refund requests on these flows have no owner.
findings.fix: Add /admin/production-orders and /admin/freelancer-jobs lists with status filters, plus actions (refund, cancel, force-release) reusing existing route logic.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Ops for B2B GMV. Prevents escrow sitting unhandled.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Several catalogued funnel events are never fired
findings.problem: grep shows track()/trackAfter() call sites for app_opened, signup_*, product_viewed, add_to_cart, post_viewed, checkout_started, message_sent, video_watched, follow, live_joined, product_published and onboarding. seller_onboarding_completed has no call site outside events.ts.
findings.why_costs_money: The seller-activation funnel (signup, store, first product, first sale) has a hole at the most important step.
findings.fix: Fire seller_onboarding_completed on seller onboarding completion (api.ts:1167 path, conditioned on account type), plus store_published from the store-publish screen.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Funnel completeness.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: GMV not measurable in PostHog: purchase_completed sends only an amount bucket
findings.problem: purchase_completed carries amount_bucket, not a value, so revenue, LTV and cohort GMV can't be summed in analytics. Admin revenue is the only GMV source and has no cohort or acquisition dimension.
findings.why_costs_money: Paid acquisition and referral ROI can't be computed, so money gets spent blind on growth.
findings.fix: Add an integer revenue_cents property (not PII) to purchase_completed and the new subscription events, or build cohort GMV views in admin from orders joined to users.createdAt.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Enables ROI on growth spend.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: No install/acquisition attribution for Brandthread's own marketing
findings.problem: Landing pages accept utm_* params but nothing persists them to the signup. UTM handling exists only for sellers' own growth links. There is no MMP/SKAdNetwork attribution (no AppsFlyer, Adjust or Branch).
findings.why_costs_money: Launch ads, influencer and creator spend can't be tied to seller or buyer signups or revenue.
findings.fix: Persist first-touch utm/referrer on web (cookie into onboarding into users.acquisitionSource) and send it as a PostHog person property. For iOS, use App Store campaign links (pt/ct) at minimum.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Paid-acquisition efficiency.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Search is the slowest path: ~24 req/s ceiling after Phase 2 fixes
findings.problem: The load test shows /public/search tops out around 24 req/s at p95 29 s on a 4-core box, bounded by Postgres CPU. The result cache (Phase 3) only works with REDIS_URL.
findings.why_costs_money: Search is the buyer's path to purchase. Slow search means lost purchases, and it spikes DB cost for every other route.
findings.fix: Enable REDIS_URL so the responseCache middleware caches search, and consider Typesense/Meilisearch post-launch.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Buyer conversion on discovery.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Object storage has no lifecycle/cost guard for large uploads (45MB JSON bodies, 80MB clips, in-request ffmpeg)
findings.problem: express.json accepts 45MB bodies globally, video clips up to 80MB are buffered in API memory, and compose-video runs ffmpeg inside the request. Only design-studio and story cleanup jobs prune storage.
findings.why_costs_money: Memory spikes crash instances, so autoscale adds more of them and cost rises. Unpruned media grows the storage bill linearly.
findings.fix: Lower the global JSON limit (keep 45MB only on the specific photo routes), move uploads to signed direct-to-GCS URLs, and add GCS lifecycle rules for orphaned uploads and abandoned drafts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Storage and compute cost control.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Sample & bulk card orders DO take 5% via destination charge (wired, not stubbed)
findings.problem: Seller pays sample/bulk order cards through Stripe Checkout with application_fee_amount = platformFeeCents (5%) and transfer_data to the manufacturer's Connect account. This works end to end, but it is the only B2B take that exists, and the fee comes out of the manufacturer's side.
findings.why_costs_money: Confirms B2B production GMV is already monetised at 5%, so every fix below that moves more production spend onto cards adds revenue directly.
findings.fix: Keep this. Track sampleOrders.platformFeeCents as its own revenue line (see admin findings) and pick one pricing owner for the B2B take before launch.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Baseline: about $0.05 gross per $1 of B2B GMV. $100k/mo of production GMV is about $5k/mo gross.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Legacy /me/payment stores bank/PayPal/Wise details that never pay out
findings.problem: GET/POST /manufacturers/me/payment still accepts method, bankName, paypalEmail and wiseEmail and stores last4 in manufacturer_payments. Nothing reads it for payouts (all payouts go through Stripe Connect), and it reports isSetup: true.
findings.why_costs_money: A manufacturer or client that hits this endpoint believes payouts are configured. Card payment then fails with MANUFACTURER_PAYOUTS_INCOMPLETE and the order stalls. It also suggests PayPal/Wise is an accepted channel.
findings.fix: Mark the endpoint deprecated: return isSetup from Connect readiness, and have POST return 410 pointing to /manufacturers/connect/onboard. Additive: add a deprecation flag rather than deleting.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small, avoids stalled orders and confusion.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Wallet/bulk transfers and cross-border manufacturer payouts are USD-only, and Brandthread absorbs FX/cross-border fees
findings.problem: Manufacturers abroad use 'recipient' Connect accounts. Transfers are in USD and Stripe charges cross-border payout fees (about 0.25-1%) plus FX on the platform side. None of this is modelled in the fee.
findings.why_costs_money: International factories are most of the supply. Unmodelled fees cut the already-thin net B2B take, and some countries are unsupported, which pushes those factories to wire.
findings.fix: Model cross-border transfer fees in the B2B fee (pass through or price in). Publish a supported-country list in the portal, and for unsupported countries consider Stripe Global Payouts.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: About 0.5-1% of international B2B GMV.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: brandthread.app is the full Expo web app plus a static marketing landing: buyers CAN buy on web
findings.problem: serve.js serves the exported Expo web app at brandthread.app, plus landing.html for signed-out '/' and '/welcome'. Web checkout uses Stripe Elements (StripePayment.web.tsx), and guest checkout exists. brandthread-woven is only a design-system gallery and app-tour is a slide deck; neither is the storefront.
findings.why_costs_money: Web purchase and web seller subscription avoid Apple's 15-30% cut. The plumbing exists, so the gap is distribution (SEO, pricing page, acquisition), not capability.
findings.fix: Treat web as the primary seller-acquisition funnel: drive paid and organic traffic to brandthread.app/welcome and onward to /onboarding and the Stripe subscription checkout.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Informational. Each web-signup seller avoids 15-30% of the subscription to Apple.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: API-domain /u/:username landing only has a brandthread:// deep link (dead on desktop)
findings.problem: The server-rendered profile page's only CTA is href='brandthread://u/...'. On desktop, or on mobile without the app, it does nothing. There is no web profile/store link, App Store badge or 'Shop on web' button.
findings.why_costs_money: Shared profile links that resolve to the API host lose the visitor, both buyers and potential sellers.
findings.fix: Add 'View on web' (https://brandthread.app/u/...) and App Store/Play links. Prefer redirecting the API /u/ route to brandthread.app/u/.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Small traffic leak.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: App tour slide deck is deployed publicly at /app-tour/
findings.problem: app-tour has a production static build served at /app-tour/ on the same deployment. It is an internal walkthrough of onboarding screens, not a marketing page.
findings.why_costs_money: It exposes unreleased flows and duplicates the landing page with off-brand content, and it costs build time on every deploy.
findings.fix: Remove the production section, or put it behind auth/noindex. Add Disallow: /app-tour/ to robots.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Negligible $. Hygiene.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Admin console lives inside the manufacturer portal bundle; admins are set only by SQL
findings.problem: Ops tooling ships in the manufacturer-facing app at /manufacturers/admin. Admin role grant is DB-only. There are no granular roles (support vs finance), so every support agent who needs refunds would need full admin.
findings.why_costs_money: Hiring support staff means giving them full suspend and featured powers, or doing everything yourself, which does not scale past launch volume.
findings.fix: Add a 'support' role with read plus refund-only permissions, and consider a separate admin build/route so manufacturers never download admin code.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Ops scalability.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Mobile admin screens are limited to invites, promotions and reports
findings.problem: On-the-go ops cover invite codes, boost approvals and the report queue only. Nothing for revenue, disputes due soon, or Thread Cash spikes.
findings.why_costs_money: The founder runs launch from a phone. Disputes with evidence deadlines can be missed.
findings.fix: Add a push alert to admins for disputes needing response (disputeEvidenceReminder job exists for sellers; mirror it for admins) and a minimal admin revenue/MRR card.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Avoids missed dispute deadlines.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Web analytics fires only after cookie-banner consent, so most web funnel data will be missing
findings.problem: On web, consent is true only after the visitor grants the Analytics cookie category. Native is always on. Web (the no-Apple-fee funnel) will be under-measured.
findings.why_costs_money: The most profitable funnel (web seller subscribe) has the least data.
findings.fix: Use cookieless/anonymous server-side counting for funnel steps (subscription checkout started/completed from the API) so web conversion is visible without cookies.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Measurement quality.

findings.area_label: Web, manufacturer portal, admin, analytics & infra
findings.title: Clerk and AI bills scale per user with no billing alerts documented as done
findings.problem: SCALE_PLAN estimates Clerk at about $0.02/MAU above the free tier and says to 'set billing alerts before launch campaigns'. Nothing in docs/launch confirms alerts are set for Clerk, OpenAI, Stripe or GCS.
findings.why_costs_money: A viral buyer spike (buyers pay nothing) raises Clerk and infra cost with no revenue. 100k MAU is about $2k/mo of Clerk alone.
findings.fix: Set vendor billing alerts and a monthly budget per vendor, and add them to docs/launch/dev-only-tasks.md.
findings.dollar_impact_estimate: Cost visibility. Up to about $2k/mo at 100k MAU.
